heading: DATUM (family hub): notes for Claude
text: DATUM (family hub): notes for Claude. Read MEMORY.md first. It is the family memory: decisions for every app, the apps list, the site, and a log of every session. At the end of every session that changes anything, update MEMORY.md (session log, decisions, next steps). What this repo is: - The family "brain": FAMILY.md (the design guide, source of truth for every app), MEMORY.md, apps.json, brand/. - Stats history in stats/history.json: one entry per day of every app's public numbers, written by stats/snapshot.mjs from .github/workflows/stats.yml (daily); for growth charts later. - Status reports in status/ (one dated file per review: each app's progress, gaps and priorities). Read the latest before planning work for any app; write a new dated file at the next review. - The brain: brain/graph.json, generated by node brain/brain.mjs from FAMILY, MEMORY, apps.json and each app's MEMORY/CHANGELOG/site.json (schema in brain/BRAIN.md). Regenerate and commit it at the end of every session. - The website in site/ (Astro, static, GitHub Pages at one landing page (index.astro), one page per app (pages/apps/[id].astro) and the interactive network (network.astro + src/scripts/network.ts), deployed by .github/workflows/pages.yml. Pages › Source must be GitHub Actions.

heading: DATUM (family hub): notes for Claude
text: DATUM (family hub): notes for Claude. - The site's look: simple, professional and technical, for engineers and scientists, never "artistic". Paper-and-ink grid (framed column, numbered section bars), IBM Plex Sans and Mono, plus Instrument Serif italic only for the changing blue words ("Tools to *plan projects.*", "for every *project.*"; class .it); no giant words, no floating decorations, FAMILY §3 accents. Glass section bars (sticky, blurred), an index by the ruler with a scroll marker, words coming into focus and cards rising on scroll (CSS scroll timelines). The hero is two panels: "Datum" and "Tools to " with the lead and two buttons on the left; on the right one tile per app (Hero.astro; two columns up to four apps, three columns for five or six, a 3×3 bench for seven or eight with the Datum mark in the centre cell and "More to come" filling the last place, a 4×3 bench for nine or ten with the Datum mark across the two middle cells of the centre row), each an animated vector drawing of what the app does (AppGlyph.astro: Gantt, curve fit, property chart, control loop, calc sheet with a PASS check, meshed bracket with its stress contour, pipe run with an expansion loop and its deflected shape, mini P&ID with a control loop and "0 errors", isometric pipe route from a vessel to a pump

heading: DATUM (family hub): notes for Claude
text: DATUM (family hub): notes for Claude. - Datum Home in home/ (Tauri 2 + SolidJS, like the apps): the desktop app that installs, updates, opens and removes the Datum apps. Rules in crates/core (unit-tested, no I/O); registry, processes and installers in src-tauri/src/sys.rs. It reads home.json (written by the site build) and each app's GitHub releases; checks only when opened; installs only verified installers (SHA256SUMS.txt) from the app's own releases; never touches the user's files. Released from this repo with tags home-vX.Y.Z (.github/workflows/home-release.yml); checked by home-ci.yml. The site offers both Datum Home and each app on its own. - The app repos (Edgar-Mendonca/Datum-Plan, Datum-Plot, Datum-Atlas, Datum-Sim, Datum-Calc, Datum-Mesh, Datum-Pipe, Datum-Schema, Datum-Layout) are read-only from here. Changes to an app happen in that app's own chat; give the user text to paste there. - Public text never names or compares with commercial products, and never says an app copies or replaces one (FAMILY §13).

text: DATUM (family hub): notes for Claude. with a valve and "0 clashes"), around the amber datum square. A new app needs its drawing in AppGlyph and its phrases in Hero. The italic phrase changes by itself every few seconds and its app's tile lights up; hover or focus holds a tile, and the cycle resumes when the pointer leaves. Tiles open the app's page. heading: DATUM (family hub): notes for Claude
text: DATUM (family hub): notes for Claude. - The landing page stays one page: the hero, 01 the apps (the Datum Home band, then compact cards with a status badge: Stable/Beta/Alpha from apps.json status or the version), 02 the method, 03 the newest release of each app, 04 In use (family totals from GitHub: installer downloads, releases, stars, issues closed; a releases-per-day chart by app, per week once the history passes eight weeks; downloads by app; shown only when GitHub answered). App cards and app pages carry a small stats line (stars, forks, downloads, releases). Modest figures in the grid style, never giant counters. Never say how many apps there are. Each app also has its own page (/apps/ ): hero with the app's drawing and download, 01 Overview (about + three steps), What it does (highlights), Screens (up to four), Roadmap, Releases (last five, expandable), Get it, previous/next app. Family memory and decisions live in the repo and the network, not as pages. On app pages the italic .it takes the app's accent. - Never fail the build because of one app: show "Coming soon" instead. Checks before pushing: - cd site && npm ci && npm run build (works without a token).

heading: The Datum family: one design and one way of working
text: The Datum family: one design and one way of working. The Datum apps are free, open-source desktop tools for engineers, scientists, researchers and analysts: small, fast Windows apps that do serious technical work. Datum Plan (project scheduling) is the first, Datum Plot (data analysis and graphs) the second, Datum Atlas (materials selection and property charts) the third, and Datum Sim (system simulation and control design) the fourth. Every app looks, feels and ships the same way; only the accent colour and the logo glyph change. This file is the single source for that. It lives in the DATUM repo (Edgar-Mendonca/Datum); each app keeps a short docs/FAMILY.md that links here. Datum Plan's code is the reference implementation: copy from it rather than reinventing anything. Section numbers are stable, so "FAMILY §3" means the same thing everywhere.

heading: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 2. Stack (the same in every app)
text: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 2. Stack (the same in every app). - Several documents at once (from Datum Plan 0.5.5, placed in 0.5.14): one tab per open document between the ribbon and the work area, shown even for one document, with ＋ to open another (a dot for unsaved changes, Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+W, Save All on close, recovery for each). Links between documents keep the other file and the last known values, and change only when the user updates them. A linked item is always marked where people look (beside its ID and on its chart), in one colour for "waits for another document" and another for "another document waits for it". Several documents of one job form a project: the master keeps the ordered, nested list of its parts, their tabs sit together in one colour (the master marked), and the master can show its parts read-only (each opens in its own tab to change). File › Close and Close All always exist beside New and Open. Printing: Save as PDF writes the file directly (no browser header or footer), the header and footer are pictures (any number per side, each sized, on every page), a title and tick boxes, the legend lists only what the pages show. Dashboards lead with the main chart across the page and show a card only when the data has it (the user can choose);

heading: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 2. Stack (the same in every app)
text: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 2. Stack (the same in every app). - Rust + Tauri 2 desktop shell (src-tauri), Windows first (NSIS per-user installer, WebView2). - Engine in a pure-Rust crate (crates/core): all calculation lives there, with unit tests. The window only shows what the engine computes. - UI: SolidJS + Vite + strict TypeScript in ui/src/*.tsx, built to ui/dist (embedded at compile time). State in ui/src/store.ts. Plain CSS with tokens (no CSS framework). - Charts: Chart.js in the family chart style (see §7). An app may add its own SVG plot engine for publication graphs, but must keep this look. - Spreadsheet formulas: the GridCraft crates (pinned git dependency, attribution in NOTICE) where the app needs them. - Sheets inside an app (from Datum Plan 0.5.0) behave like a spreadsheet through GridCraft (references by clicking, suggestions, fill and paste that move references, insert and delete rows) and read the app's data by name: GridCraft tables and workbook names, not copied values. Countries show as flags from bundled SVGs (flag-icons, MIT), never emoji. Dashboards of the user's own (from Datum Plan 0.5.3) are tiles on a 12-column grid whose figures are formulas over the same names.

heading: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 2. Stack (the same in every app)
text: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 2. Stack (the same in every app). a file named inside someone else's document is never fetched from a network server it names. Charts can go to Datum Plot as a one-way copy (a Datum Plot button on each chart writes a .dplot and opens it; nothing comes back). Every app has a guided tutorial example (Help › Tutorial): one document that uses every view, with a note on each view stored in the document, and nothing the user did not choose is printed, never the program name. Class names in an app are prefixed by their part, so two parts never share one. - No Python inside the apps (size and second runtime). The one exception is Datum Plot, which bundles its own Python (numpy, SciPy, matplotlib) for statistics and graphs; the decision is recorded in Plot's docs/MEMORY.md. - Small, compact code that matches the surrounding style.

heading: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 4. Type
text: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 4. Type. - IBM Plex Sans for text, IBM Plex Mono for uppercase spaced labels, tabs, buttons, numbers and IDs (@fontsource, Latin subsets only, about 200 kB). - Group captions, card headings and buttons: Plex Mono, 9.5–11 px, letter-spacing: .1em, uppercase. - Body 12–13 px; page titles 23 px, 600–700 weight. - Tables and grids: 12–13 px; numbers right-aligned.

heading: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 5. Logo and branding
text: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 5. Logo and branding. - Tile: 256×256 viewBox, a rounded square (x=8 y=8 w=240 h=240 rx=56), a white→accent-tint diagonal gradient, and a 4 px border in a light accent tint. - Glyph: drawn in the accent with 11 px strokes, round caps. It may use one light tint fill (the --sky colour). It always has one amber #F2B233 diamond (the family mark). - Files: ui/public/logo.svg (in the app) and docs/brand/datum- -icon.svg (README). Windows icons are generated from it (npx tauri icon). Copies of every icon, and the family mark, are in this repo's brand/. - The family mark ("Continuum", designed by the user): two concentric D's drawn as one continuous line, with the amber #F2B233 datum square where the line starts. Navy #0C1A2B (or light #E6EDF5) ink only, never an app colour, so it stays right however many apps the family has. Files, construction and rules: brand/BRAND.md (datum-logo.svg, datum-mark.svg, datum-icon.svg and light versions). - Name: "Datum " in Plex Sans 600. Tagline in the README. - README: the logo, the name, a one-line tagline, shields.io badges (release, CI, downloads, license MIT, platform Windows 10/11, Rust, Tauri 2, SolidJS), then for-the-badge buttons (Download for Windows · What's new · Memory & roadmap), then a screenshot.

heading: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 6. Window layout
text: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 6. Window layout. - Title bar: quick access (save, undo, redo, print), document name, "Tell me what you want to do" (Ctrl+K), a Theme button (Auto/Light/Dark). - Ribbon: a FILE button in the accent, then tabs. Groups have a mono uppercase caption. Big buttons have an icon above the label; split buttons have the command on top and the menu on the bottom ▾. Contextual tabs carry a small label above them. The ribbon never scrolls sideways: it tightens, then folds groups from the right (icons only). - Left sidebar: icon + mono label per view, with Setup first. Groups are separated by rules. - File page (backstage): a sidebar in the accent colour (Home, New, Open, Import, Save, Save As, Export, Print; Options and Updates at the bottom). - Home: template tiles, recent files, a Roadmap tile, and the updates card. The card has Check again with a spinner and the time it checked, and the GitHub, Releases and Report an Issue buttons. - Status bar: Ready, key facts, view switches, zoom. - Options page: sections (General, Start-up and saving, New , Printing and branding, Updates). Each option has a name plus a one-line hint on the left and the control on the right. - Help tab: - Getting Started: written for people coming from other tools, in plain words;

heading: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 6. Window layout
text: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 6. Window layout. - Glossary: plain-language terms, searchable; - Shortcuts, Tell Me, What Is This Tool?; - the GitHub links. - ? help beside the tools: a small ? beside each ribbon group, page, panel and main dialog opens a card (what it is for, how to use it) from one HELP table in ui/src/help.tsx.

heading: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 7. Components
text: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 7. Components. - Controls: square corners, 1 px lines, no heavy shadows. Buttons are Plex Mono uppercase (.btn, .btn.pri filled accent, .btn.sm). - Menus: icons in the tick column, keyboard hints on the right, submenus to any depth, close on an outside click. - Dialogs: a title bar with ×; OK/Cancel at the bottom right; Enter = OK, Esc = Cancel. - Grids (spreadsheet-like): - one scroller with a sticky header and frozen key columns; - range selection (drag, Shift, Ctrl, whole rows and columns, Ctrl+A); - Sum/Average/Count in the formula bar; - TSV clipboard that pastes into any spreadsheet; - a fill handle with series (Ctrl copies); - Paste Special (Ctrl+Alt+V); - Font/Alignment formatting (Ctrl+B/I/U); - a date picker on date cells. Reuse Plan's selection.ts, cells.ts and fmt.ts. - Toasts: bottom left; green for success. - Empty states: say what the view is for and offer the first action.

heading: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 7. Components › Icons
text: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 7. Components › Icons. 24×24 viewBox, in one SVG sprite in ui/index.html ( ). - Line style: stroke="currentColor", stroke-width 1.6–1.8, round caps and joins. - At most one light accent fill (#9CC2F7 in Plan; use the app's --sky). - Red #C0392B only for delete or critical; green #2E9D57 for done or ok; amber for highlight. - One icon per meaning (no duplicates).

heading: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 7. Components › Charts (the family chart style)
text: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 7. Components › Charts (the family chart style). - white plot area, thin axes, no heavy gridlines; - Okabe-Ito colour-blind-safe series colours (#0072B2 #E69F00 #009E73 #D55E00 #CC79A7 #56B4E9 #F0E442 #000000); - a crosshair tooltip; - a PNG button on every chart; charts printable; - horizontal bar charts name every bar (autoSkip: false); - a whose options load later marks the chosen instead of setting value on the select (found in Datum Plan 0.4.1); - hand-drawn SVG charts over plain numbers use SolidJS , not ( reuses nodes by value, so equal values keep stale positions; found in Datum Plan 0.4.0).

heading: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 8. Printing
text: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 8. Printing. - File › Print (Ctrl+P) shows settings on the left and a live page preview on the right, for every view. - The settings: paper, orientation, scaling or fit-to-pages, margins, page ranges, header and footer (left/centre/right) with codes and logos, legend, and view options. - Pages are drawn as SVG at real size and printed with the WebView dialog ("Save as PDF"). - Report-type pages print as flowing documents with the header and footer on every page and page numbers. - Reuse Plan's print.tsx (Frame, Slot, codes).

heading: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 9. Updates and releases
text: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 9. Updates and releases. - Updater: src-tauri/src/update.rs. - Set REPO to the app's repo. It checks GitHub releases at start, and beta versions when turned on. - It downloads the installer, checks SHA256SUMS and installs. - The CHANGELOG section becomes the in-app "What's new". - Versions: small numbered releases (0.1.0, 0.1.1, …), always three numbers (the updater compares three), consecutive with no jumped numbers. - Release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml, windows-latest): - builds the UI and the app and creates the tag; - publishes Datum -x.y.z-setup.exe + SHA256SUMS.txt. - Run it with workflow_dispatch when tag pushes are blocked. - CI (ci.yml, ubuntu): clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, npm run check:ui, the Playwright UI tests. - Options and recovery files in the app's data folder (com.edgarmendonca.datum ). - Datum Home (home/ in DATUM) installs and updates every app from one window. It relies on this release shape: a per-user NSIS installer named Datum -x.y.z-setup.exe that accepts /S, a SHA256SUMS.txt beside it, the Windows display name equal to the app's name in apps.json ("Datum Plan") and the publisher "Datum" (bundle.publisher in tauri.conf.json; apps released before 2026-10-29 used "Edgar Mendonca", which Datum Home still accepts). A release without SHA256SUMS.txt is never installed by Datum Home.

heading: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 10. Docs in every repo
text: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 10. Docs in every repo. - CLAUDE.md: read MEMORY first; update it at the end of every session; the user's preferences; the checks; the release steps. - docs/MEMORY.md: product table, architecture (files), decisions (version ; decision ; why), roadmap (✅ 🔜 ⬜), session log, known limits, and the "How we work" workflow. - CHANGELOG.md: ## x.y.z — date, a one-line summary, then bold sections in plain language for users. The site shows the last five sections. - docs/site.json: the app's public summary, read by the family site at build time and by File › Roadmap in the app: when is one of Next, Soon, Later, Goal. Screenshots are 1440×900 PNGs in docs/images/; the app's page on the site shows the first four. about and steps (three steps: how the app is used) fill the Overview of the app's page (/apps/ ); until an app sets them, the hub's apps.json supplies them. - The brain: DATUM's brain/graph.json is generated from these files (node brain/brain.mjs); keep the MEMORY tables (Files, Decisions, Roadmap, Session log, How we work) in the same shape so it can read them. - docs/PLAN-x.y.md: feedback → diagnosis → proposal → size → questions, written before any big release. - NOTICE for third-party code and fonts; MIT license.

heading: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 10. Docs in every repo
text: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 10. Docs in every repo. - The guide (from Datum Plan 0.4.4): docs/guide/ .md (English, and other languages users need; Datum Plan has Simplified Chinese) with screenshots in docs/guide/img/ (numbered orange markers, made by a script from the real window), built to PDF by scripts/guide.cjs (cover, contents, figures, page numbers; Noto Sans SC for Chinese), attached to every release as Datum -Guide- .pdf and listed in SHA256SUMS.txt. In the app, Help › Guide and a File-page tile download the version's guide, verify it against the checksums, save it in Downloads and open it; nothing is bundled in the installer. Translations keep the English UI names in bold with the meaning in brackets.

heading: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 11. How we work (from Datum Plan)
text: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 11. How we work (from Datum Plan). 1. The user reviews a release and sends screenshots. 2. Reproduce first. 3. Big asks get a plan file and questions; build after the answers. 4. Engine first (with a test), then the UI. 5. Check every change in the real app (Xvfb screenshots). 6. Add a UI test for every bug. 7. Run all checks: clippy -D warnings, cargo test (with the hardening tests below), the UI type-check and UI tests, cargo deny check. 8. Release. 9. Report in plain language: what changed, what was checked, what is not done. Hardening standard (every app, from Datum Plan 0.3.11). Each app's engine has a hardening test module that proves: - a failed edit leaves the document exactly as it was; - random documents (a small built-in generator, no extra crate) never panic and keep their invariants; - damaged files for every reader (cut short, garbled bytes, loops) never panic: they open or give a clear error; - a speed gate on a large document (a looser limit in debug builds).

heading: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 11. How we work (from Datum Plan)
text: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 11. How we work (from Datum Plan). - trust in the results (from Datum Plan 0.3.12): hand-worked cases for each core rule, with the expected values worked out before running (cases.rs); parity files that carry their own results, checked value by value (tests/parity, where real exports from other tools can be dropped in); random-input checks of the rules themselves (for Plan: every link holds, no task starts later than its links need, row order does not matter), and random sequences of edits. - hostile values (from Datum Plan 0.4.2): a battery that runs every engine function the window or a script can reach (exercise) on documents with deliberately impossible values (huge or negative spans, zero-length units, year 1 and year 9999, non-finite numbers, IDs at their maximum) and on extreme edits. Loading clamps such values (normalize), and date and time arithmetic saturates at a horizon instead of unwrapping past the end of the date range. Safety rules for every app's shell (from Datum Plan 0.4.2): - release builds panic = "unwind"; edits, opening, importing and long analyses run inside a guard() that turns a panic into an error message, and a panic hook appends to crash.log in the app data folder;

heading: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 11. How we work (from Datum Plan)
text: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 11. How we work (from Datum Plan). - every save (documents, autosave, recovery, settings, exports) is atomic: write a temporary file next to the target, sync_all, then rename; every file read has a size limit; - the updater installs nothing without SHA256SUMS.txt, matches the installer's line exactly, accepts only *-setup.exe names of safe characters, downloads into a new private folder and caps the size; - the window's CSP: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none', images 'self' data: blob: (blob: is needed to resize pictures in the window); only Tauri's core permissions; - links open only to the app's own GitHub pages (an exact prefix plus plain URL characters); - CSV exports prefix ' to text starting with =, +, - or @ (unless a plain number); - CI also runs npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high. Plus: deny.toml + cargo deny check (advisories, licences, sources) and license = "MIT" in every crate; CI runs cargo test on Windows and macOS as well as Linux; the shell's state lock recovers from a poisoned mutex; SECURITY.md and CONTRIBUTING.md in the repo. rustfmt is not enforced (the code keeps its compact hand style).

heading: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 12. Starting a new Datum app (checklist)
text: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 12. Starting a new Datum app (checklist). 1. Create the repo Edgar-Mendonca/Datum- (MIT). 2. Copy the skeleton from Datum Plan: - the workspace Cargo.toml, crates/core (empty engine), src-tauri (main, update.rs, tauri.conf); - ui/ (index.html with the icon sprite, styles.css, store.ts, ui.tsx, help.tsx, ribbon/backstage/options/print/roadmap patterns); - package.json, .github/workflows, tests_ui/run.cjs, CLAUDE.md, NOTICE, LICENSE. 3. Rename: product name, identifier, file extension, REPO in update.rs, installer name in release.yml. 4. Apply the accent set from §3 and draw the logo per §5; copy the icon into DATUM brand/. 5. Write docs/MEMORY.md and docs/PLAN-0.1.md (brainstorm and questions) before building features. 6. Release 0.1.0 (shell, updater, Home, one working view) so the updater works from day one. 7. Add the hardening standard (§11): the hardening tests, deny.toml, the Windows/macOS CI jobs, SECURITY.md and CONTRIBUTING.md. 8. Publish docs/site.json (§10) and add one line to DATUM's apps.json; the site picks the app up on its next build.

heading: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 13. Principles and public words
text: The Datum family: one design and one way of working › 13. Principles and public words. Datum: free, open-source desktop tools for engineers, scientists, researchers and analysts. Small, fast apps that do serious technical work, written from scratch in Rust, with one look and one way of working. No accounts, no subscriptions, no telemetry: your files stay on your computer. - Small and fast. Quick to install; opens in a moment; smooth with large files. - Private. Files stay on the user's computer. The only network call is the update check. - Built for real technical work. Each app has its own engine in a pure Rust crate, with tests. - One design. The same window, ribbon, help, printing and updater in every app (§5–9). - Small releases. One release is one small numbered version, shown in the in-app updater. - Written down. Docs and memory are kept in every repo (§10). - Free forever. MIT licence. Rules for all public text (README, site, release notes, CHANGELOG): - Describe what each app does and who it helps. Never name or compare with commercial products, and never say an app copies, clones or replaces one. Every Datum app has its own engine and its own design. (The family site leaves out any CHANGELOG or site.json line that names one, and lists it in the build log.)

heading: Datum: family memory › 5. Session log › 2026-10-29: Session 19 (brainstorm: the brain, AI and shared code)
text: Datum: family memory › 5. Session log › 2026-10-29: Session 19 (brainstorm: the brain, AI and shared code). - User: is the network a neural network that can be "trained" as Datum's brain, and could an AI assistant use it? Answer: brain/graph.json is a knowledge graph (facts and links, rebuilt hourly, exact, explainable), not a neural network; training our own model would be costly, imprecise and stale. The right pattern is retrieval: the graph and docs hold the facts, an existing language model reads and answers with citations. Ideas (not started): an "ask the brain" tool for the app chats; offline help search shared by the apps; later an opt-in assistant (local model or the user's own key), citing sources and never producing engineering numbers itself (results only from the tested engines). Privacy promise (no telemetry) rules out a default cloud assistant. - User: is code and icon reuse real? Answer: decisions come from the hub, code is copied from the reference apps (not rewritten), the graph is the map. Proposed a shared kit (crates + UI package + one icon library in the hub); the user declined for now: separate apps are safer (decision above).

heading: The apps › Why Datum
text: The apps › Why Datum. - Small and fast. Quick to install, opens in a moment, smooth with large files. - Private. Your files stay on your computer. The only network call is the update check. - Built for real technical work. Each app has its own tested engine: scheduling, statistics, materials selection, system simulation, calculation, finite elements, pipe stress, P&IDs, 3D layout. - One design. The same window, ribbon, help, printing and updater in every app. Learn one, know them all. - Free forever. MIT licence, built in the open.

heading: The apps › Principles
text: The apps › Principles. - Engine first. All calculation lives in a pure Rust crate (crates/core) with unit tests; the window only shows what the engine computes. - One window style. A Tauri 2 shell with a SolidJS window, IBM Plex type and one set of colour tokens; only the accent and the logo glyph change. - Small releases. One release is one small numbered version (0.1.0, 0.1.1, …), shown in the in-app updater with its notes. - Written down. Every repo keeps CLAUDE.md, docs/MEMORY.md (decisions, roadmap, session log) and a plain-language CHANGELOG.md.

heading: The apps › How the family is built
text: The apps › How the family is built. - FAMILY.md: the shared design guide (stack, colour, type, logo, window, components, printing, releases, docs, workflow). - MEMORY.md: the family memory: decisions that apply to every app, the apps list, the session log. - apps.json: the registry the website builds from. Adding an app is one line. - brand/: the Datum logo ("Continuum") and its guide BRAND.md, and every app icon. - briefs/: the briefs new apps start from: Datum Sim (released), Datum Calc and Datum Mesh (released), Datum Pipe (released), Datum Schema (released), Datum Layout (released). - status/: dated status reports: where each app stands, what it lacks, and the priorities. - stats/: a daily snapshot of every app's public numbers (stars, forks, downloads, releases), kept for growth charts. - brain/: the Datum brain: graph.json, one graph of every app, design rule, technology, source file, decision, release, plan and session, generated from the repositories (BRAIN.md). Read it before starting anything new. - home/: Datum Home, the desktop app that installs and updates the others (Tauri, a tested Rust core, a SolidJS window); released from this repository with tags home-vX.Y.Z. - site/: the website (Astro): the landing page, one page per app (/apps/ ) and the interactive Datum network. It reads each app's docs/site.json, CHANGELOG.md, latest release and the brain when it builds, every hour and on every push.

heading: The Datum brain

heading: Datum family status: 2026-11-01 › Context
text: Datum family status: 2026-11-01 › Context. - Eight apps built in under two weeks (Plan started 2026-10-24; Schema 2026-10-29), working day and night. - Real users: Datum Plan, Plot and Calc are in use by people outside the project. heading: Changelog › 0.7.1 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.7.1 — 2026-11-07. Hardening: very large plans, measured at 100,000 tasks. - Undo stays within memory on very large plans. Each undo step keeps a copy of the plan (about 33 MB at 100,000 tasks). Small plans still keep 200 steps; very large plans keep fewer (20 at 50,000 tasks, 10 at 100,000), so undo holds about 330 MB at most instead of several gigabytes. - Less work per edit: the plan sent to the window after each edit no longer copies all its tasks to JSON first only to drop them (a tenth of a second per edit at 100,000 tasks), and the task rows sent to the grid are about a quarter smaller (no false flags, dates rounded to under a second). - Smoother Gantt scrolling: the row of each task is worked out once per change of the rows, not on every scroll frame. - Measured (in the repository: npm run bench and npm run perf:ui): at 100,000 tasks the engine schedules in about 0.12 s, an edit takes about 0.2 s, saving 0.1 s and opening 0.4 s; the window paints the first rows in under 0.1 s and scrolls at full frame rate.

heading: Changelog › 0.7.0 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.7.0 — 2026-11-07. The portfolio and a shared resource pool. - Portfolio (sidebar) now has three tabs, with totals for the whole workspace at the top: plans and tasks, plans finishing after their baseline, late tasks, average complete, and (for plans that use the modules) contract dates late or at risk and orders late for their plans. - Plans: every plan of the workspace folder, grouped by subfolder (EPS), with its finish against the baseline and, where a plan uses them, its contract, document and procurement figures. Plans open in a tab show their unsaved changes. - Timeline: every plan as one bar from start to finish with its progress and baseline finish, red when it finishes after the baseline, and today's line. - Resource Pool: every resource's work across all the plans (matched by name) against its capacity, as a heat strip by week or month, over-allocated resources first. Click a resource for its hours by plan against the capacity line.

heading: Changelog › 0.7.0 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.7.0 — 2026-11-07. - The pool plan: choose a plan of the workspace whose resources are the pool. Its units, availability and calendars set the capacity, and Take resources from the pool gives the plan in the tab the pool's rates, units, availability and calendars for resources with the same names (…and add the others brings the rest of the pool too). Without a pool plan, a resource's capacity is the most any plan gives it.

heading: Changelog › 0.6.2 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.6.2 — 2026-11-07. The Procurement Register: a module for sub-orders from enquiry to delivery. - Project › Modules › Procurement Register adds it to a plan (sidebar › Procurement). - Orders: item number, order or equipment, sub-vendor, country of origin, PO number and value, long-lead flag, remarks. - Five milestones, planned against actual: RFQ issued, PO placed, manufacturing start, inspection release (IRN) and delivered. Planned dates can be typed, or come from the task for the order's manufacture and delivery (its start and finish), with the inspection release a set number of days before delivery. - The vendor's promised delivery against the date the plan needs the item (the start of the task that needs it, or a date typed). The float shows red when the order is late for the plan and amber under the days set in Settings. - Status, next milestone and days late for every order; Done on marks the next milestone in the register itself, and the manufacturing % is typed in the row. - Weighted progress: milestone weights from a preset (balanced, more credit at the order, more credit at delivery) or your own; manufacturing counted pro rata to its %; orders weighed by PO value, equally or by a typed weight. Weekly and monthly S-curves, and orders by sub-vendor and country.

heading: Changelog › 0.6.2 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.6.2 — 2026-11-07. - Expediting log: dated notes per order. - Linking to the Document Register is your choice (Settings): linked, each order lists the vendor documents it waits for, shows how many are accepted and is flagged when its drawings hold up manufacturing; unlinked, orders stand on their own. - Import a procurement status register from Excel or CSV (the heading row and the planned and actual columns are found by themselves; check and change any of them). Export to Excel writes the register and the expediting log. - On a master, a table adds up the registers of its open subplans; Apply Setup to Subplans › Modules gives the subplans the register's settings.

heading: Changelog › 0.6.1 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.6.1 — 2026-11-07. The Document Register: a module for vendor documents and their review cycle. - Project › Modules › Document Register adds the register to a plan (sidebar › Documents). - Documents: number, title, vendor, package, discipline, type, class (1, 2 or 3), key document, MRB, VDB, IOM, PIM, native, engineering and QA review, weight, counted in progress, recurring, the task that needs it, remarks. - Planned dates from the P date (purchase order or kick-off; the plan's start when empty): the first issue at P + n weeks or days (or on its own date), then the client's review and our turnaround in working days. - Calendars: the client's review and our turnaround each count on the plan's calendar or a calendar of their own, for a client's working week or an engineering office in another country. New calendar… creates one from the plan's calendar and opens its working time. - The cycle: classes 1 and 2 go first issue → approval issue → construction issue → final issue; class 3 goes construction issue → final issue. The issue purposes (ICR, IFA, IFC1, IFC2 by default), the return codes (which accept, which ask again) and the progress weights of the six steps per class are all settings.

heading: Changelog › 0.6.1 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.6.1 — 2026-11-07. - Transmittal log: one row per submission with revision, purpose, transmittal, date sent, review due date, return transmittal, date returned, code and comments reference. + Sub logs a document's next submission: next revision, the purpose its cycle needs. - Worked out for every document: submissions and resubmission cycles, latest revision and purpose, review due, status (Not submitted, Not submitted – overdue, Under review, Review overdue, Resubmit, Accepted – next issue, Final issued), first-issue delay, days the client kept it past the review period, earned and planned progress, the forecast of every step, and whether it is late for the task that needs it. - Progress: weighted planned and actual S-curves by week (ending on the plan's week-end day) or by month, first issues per period, and progress by vendor, discipline, type and class. Recurring submissions are never counted. - Import a document register or a transmittal log from Excel or CSV: choose the sheet, the heading row (found by itself) and what each column holds (guessed from the headings). Running it again updates documents with the same number. Export to Excel writes the register and the transmittal log. - On a master, a table adds up the registers of its open subplans. Apply Setup to Subplans › Modules gives the subplans the register's settings and the calendars they count on.

heading: Changelog › 0.6.0 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.6.0 — 2026-11-07. Modules: registers a plan takes on only when it needs them. The first is Contract Dates & Payments. - Project › Modules ticks the modules a plan uses. A plan without modules looks and saves exactly as before. Switching one off hides it and asks whether to keep its data (kept by default) or delete it. - Contract Dates & Payments (sidebar › Contract, or Project › Contract): - Contract dates, each met by a task: the task's forecast (or actual) finish against the contract date, days late or early, the baseline, and a status (On track, At risk, Late, Met, Met late). "At risk" is less float than the days set at the top (14 by default). - Trend: the forecast at every period close, so a slipping date shows as a rising line. - Delay damages: a % of the value (the unit's price, or the contract value) per week or part week late, after grace days, up to a cap. The page adds up the damages at today's forecast and their cap. - Payment milestones: a share of the contract value or an amount, due some days after a task finishes, with invoiced and paid dates. A chart shows planned, forecast and received cash.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.29 — 2026-11-05
text: Changelog › 0.5.29 — 2026-11-05. Bigger, clearer text on printed Gantt charts. - Print › Page Setup › Text (Gantt, Tracking Gantt, Timeline): the text size in points on paper, and the size it really prints at. - Fit to pages wide keeps the text size: long task names wrap onto up to three lines and the chart can narrow to a quarter of the page before the page is shrunk. When it still has to shrink, Print says so and what to change. - Columns as wide as their text (on by default), so the table takes only the room it needs and the chart gets the rest. Turn it off to print columns as wide as on screen. - Rows grow with their text; the timescale, milestone dates and resource labels on the bars grow with it. - Sizes by row type: top summaries, other summaries, tasks and milestones, each in points (empty = the text size). - Rows you choose: select rows in the task sheet, then give them a size in Print › Text. Clear chosen sizes takes them back. Rows formatted with Home › Font keep their size relative to the text size.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.28 — 2026-11-05
text: Changelog › 0.5.28 — 2026-11-05. A master's setup goes to its subplans in one step. - Project › Apply Setup to Subplans (also on the master's tab menu and in Subplans): tick what to give and the subplans to give it to, then Apply. The parts are project details (client, manager, company, location, logo), logos and pictures, the print header, footer and page setup, calendars and working time, currency, reporting periods, and activity codes and custom fields. - Each subplan keeps its own name, code and description, its print title and subtitle, and its own logos; the master's pictures are added beside them once, and the header points at the subplan's copy. - The subplans change in their open tabs: save them to keep it, or undo it in any one of them. A note offers Open All when some subplans are closed. The ticked parts are remembered.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.27 — 2026-11-05
text: Changelog › 0.5.27 — 2026-11-05. The last open items closed, and Ctrl+K back to Tell Me everywhere. - Ctrl+K opens Tell Me in Sheets too. Add a link with Insert › Link… or right-click › Link…. - Rules follow their cells: validation limits, list sources and conditional formats that point at cells move with inserted, deleted and shifted cells and renamed sheets, and show #REF! when their cells go. Conditional formats can compare with a cell (=$E$1). - Validation by a custom formula (=AND(A2>0,A2<=B2)), checked for each cell, with Stop or Warn and Circle Invalid Data. - Names for one sheet: a defined name's scope is the plan or a single sheet. Sheet names go to and from Excel workbooks as local names, and move with their sheet to another plan. - Defined names in task-sheet formula columns: =[Cost]*(1+VAT), lookups into named sheet ranges and the plan's own figures, worked out per task. - Elapsed lags on links to other plans (FS +7ed) in the Link to Plan dialog, scheduled in calendar time. Links to other plans now show their lags as the task sheet does (FS+5d, +4h).

heading: Changelog › 0.5.26 — 2026-11-05
text: Changelog › 0.5.26 — 2026-11-05. Sheets move between plans, a clearer project tab group, and the open items from 0.5.25 closed. - Move a sheet to another plan: right-click a sheet tab › Move to Plan, or Move or Copy… › To plan. The sheet goes, with its pictures and frozen panes, to another open plan, for example from the master to one of its subplans. Its formulas on plan data then read that plan. The message counts formulas that read other sheets of the first plan. - Project tabs: a project's open plans sit in one framed group with the project's name. The master comes first with a Master badge, and its subplans follow with Sub badges. - Alt+Enter for several lines in a cell. - Links: web and e-mail addresses and =HYPERLINK() show as links. Ctrl+click opens them after showing the full address. Link… (Ctrl+K in a sheet) adds or edits one. - Defined names with a Name Manager: use them in any sheet formula and in dashboard tiles. - Data Validation: whole numbers, decimals, dates, times and text length within limits. Each rule has an input message and a stop or warn error, and Circle Invalid Data marks cells that break their rules. - Inserting or deleting cells, and Remove Duplicates, now also move conditional formatting, filters and validation.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.26 — 2026-11-05
text: Changelog › 0.5.26 — 2026-11-05. - All of these go into an exported workbook and come back from one. - Elapsed lags such as 4FS+7ed: calendar time, weekends included, as for curing. They go to and from Project XML. - Usage hours split at the status date: a started task's work done sits between its actual start and the status date, and the remaining work runs from there to the finish. This applies in Task and Resource Usage, the resource graph, period hours and the cost curve.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.25 — 2026-11-05
text: Changelog › 0.5.25 — 2026-11-05. Sheets that work like a full spreadsheet, a simpler ribbon, and a night of bug fixing across the app (more than 70 fixes, each with a test). - Home also has the everyday task commands (New Task, Indent, Outdent, Information, Link, Unlink, Scroll to Task); they are on Schedule too. From Sheets, a task command opens the Gantt. - Sheet Tools is always on the ribbon, with one tab, Format: cells, data, views, page setup and printing. From another view it opens Sheets; Gantt Chart Tools › Format opens the Gantt. - A full right-click menu on cells, row numbers and column letters: Cut, Copy, Paste, Paste Special, Insert… and Delete… (shift cells or whole rows and columns), Clear, Sort, Filter, Notes, Format Cells…, number format, borders, merge, wrap, rows and columns, freeze panes, AutoSum, functions, plan data and drop-down lists. - Format Cells… (Ctrl+1): number, alignment, font, border and fill. - Notes on cells (Shift+F2): a red corner; they show when you point at the cell. - Filter (Ctrl+Shift+L): values, conditions, top N, above or below average; sort from the heading. - Drop-down lists in cells, from typed values or from cells. - Remove Duplicates, Find All, Find and Replace on every sheet, Go To (F5) and a Name Box you can type in.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.25 — 2026-11-05
text: Changelog › 0.5.25 — 2026-11-05. - Keys: Ctrl+; today, Ctrl+Shift+; the time, Ctrl+Space and Shift+Space, Ctrl++ and Ctrl+-. - Notes, filters and drop-down lists go into an exported workbook and come back from one. - Fixed, in the sheets' calculations (14): - plan dates in sheets no longer carry a hidden time of day, so COUNTIFS on Tasks[Finish], ProjectFinish lookups and date differences give the right answers; - dates typed as 05/01/2026 follow the plan's day order, also inside formulas; two-digit years work; - a date plus days shows as a date, and a date minus a date shows as days; - amounts typed with €, £ or the plan's currency are numbers; - money rounds halves up; - very deeply nested formulas show #VALUE! instead of closing the app; - Save as Excel keeps the same results and formats when the workbook is recalculated; - imported formulas follow renamed tabs; - the fill handle keeps thousands separators and continues day and month names. - Fixed, in dashboards and reports (18): - the S-curve's actual line runs to the status date, and planned and actual are measured on the same day, so a plan on time no longer shows behind; - long plans' S-curves reach 100 %, and phase curves run forward;

heading: Changelog › 0.5.25 — 2026-11-05
text: Changelog › 0.5.25 — 2026-11-05. - earned schedule after completion, plans of milestones only, and plans with no status date give the right figures; - dashboard tiles: large ranges stop at the data, rings show errors and text, pies refuse negative values, tiles on a deleted sheet say so, and dashboards with more than 200 formulas fill completely; - the Report Builder prints the report and period on screen, without blank pages; - the status marker on cost and earned value charts sits in the right period. - Fixed, in the task sheet, Gantt and file exchange (19): - Move Up/Down of a block, remaining and actual durations longer than planned, Fill Down copies instead of counting; - progress and scheduling-mode buttons work when a summary is selected; Insert Summary Task and Paste undo in one step; - percent lags in the task details; Calendar and Team Planner show collapsed tasks; renaming a calendar keeps people on it; - typing a start or finish on a task under way sets its actual dates; a finish typed on a milestone keeps it a milestone; daily recurring tasks skip non-working days; - XER: elapsed durations, row order, task calendars and % complete; Project XML: elapsed lags; CSV/Excel import: progress set after the links.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.24 — 2026-11-04
text: Changelog › 0.5.24 — 2026-11-04. A cleaner ribbon, zoom for sheets, and fixes to Page Breaks view. - Home tab: the first tab now holds what the task sheet and the Sheets share: Clipboard, Font, Alignment and Editing (Find, Fill, Clear, Sort). Each tool acts on what is in view, so nothing is repeated. - Building the schedule (Insert, Links, Outline, Properties, Tasks, Paths) is on the Schedule tab. - Sheet Tools › Cells keeps only what a sheet has: Lines, Number, Look, Rows & Columns, Insert and Formulas. - Sheets opens on Home. - Zoom for sheets: from 10 % to 400 %. Use the status bar slider and its − and +, View › Zoom, or Ctrl with the mouse wheel. Click the percentage to go back to 100 %. Page Layout view follows the zoom. - in Page Breaks view, dragging a dashed (automatic) page break onto the print area's edge, or past it, now joins the two pages into one by lowering the sheet's scale. Before, nothing happened; - a picture placed in its cell no longer shows a dotted blue outline; the outline shows only while the picture is selected.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.23 — 2026-11-04
text: Changelog › 0.5.23 — 2026-11-04. Set the printed pages of a sheet by hand, in Page Breaks view. - Page Breaks view: - the print area has a solid blue edge, and everything outside it is grey; - drag the edge to change the print area; - drag a page break to move it; dashed lines are automatic breaks, solid lines are breaks you set; - drag a break out of the print area to remove it; - a page made bigger than the paper lowers the sheet's scale so it fits; - right-click a cell for Insert Page Break, Remove Page Break, Reset All Page Breaks, Set Print Area and Reset Print Area. - Column page breaks: Insert Page Break starts a new page above the cell's row and left of its column. Page › Breaks also has a new page at only the row or only the column. Column breaks go into an exported workbook and come back from one. - a new picture on a sheet sits inside its cell instead of over the cell's borders; - title rows above the print area now print at the top of every page; - merges, pictures or formatting far from the cells no longer stretch the print over thousands of empty rows or columns;

heading: Changelog › 0.5.22 — 2026-11-03
text: Changelog › 0.5.22 — 2026-11-03. The open Sheets items closed, and a hardening pass. - Conditional formatting by date: Highlight Cells › A Date Occurring…: before today (overdue), today, yesterday, tomorrow, last or next 7 days, last, this or next week or month, after today. It goes into exported workbooks as a date rule. - Hide and unhide rows and columns: right-click, or Rows & Columns › Size. - A double line marks where something is hidden. - Arrow keys step over hidden rows and columns. - Hidden rows and columns don't print, and stay hidden in Excel, both ways. - Fixed, from a hardening pass over Sheets and Excel (28 new tests): - Bringing in a workbook: - a workbook with cells far apart (A1 and the last cell) could stop the app; it is now refused with a message; - text starting with "=" or that looks like a number, date or percentage stays text; - formulas from .ods files work; - pictures saved by spreadsheet programs come in at their real size. - Sheet names and Save as Excel: - Save as Excel no longer fails on sheet names that are too long, end in an apostrophe, or are called Tasks or DatumPlan; - names are fitted for the workbook, and formulas that point to them follow;

heading: Changelog › 0.5.22 — 2026-11-03
text: Changelog › 0.5.22 — 2026-11-03. - copies of long sheet names stay within 31 characters. - Conditional formatting: - a rule left without a value, or Top/Bottom with 0 or a huge count, no longer breaks the workbook; - text rules with quotes are written correctly; - data bars over very large ranges no longer stop the Sheets view, and now print. - Inserting or deleting rows moves the print area, title rows and pictures as well. - Fill: filling dates follows the plan's date format (day first or month first) and keeps the cells' look. - Ctrl+D on one row copies the row above; - Cut and Paste moves merged cells; - Replace treats $ in the new text literally. - A round trip keeps the plan's own page setup for sheets that have none of their own.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.21 — 2026-11-03
text: Changelog › 0.5.21 — 2026-11-03. Conditional formatting, Find and Replace, and more Sheets fixes. - Conditional formatting on sheets: Cells › Look › Conditional. - Highlight Cells: greater than, less than, between, equal to, text that contains, blanks, duplicates. - Top and Bottom: top 10, bottom 10, above or below average. - Data Bars and Colour Scales. - New Rule… and Manage Rules…: edit, reorder and delete rules; the first matching rule gives a cell its look. - Rules print, go into exported workbooks as real conditional formats, and come back when the workbook is brought in again. - Find and Replace: [[Ctrl+F]] and [[Ctrl+H]], or Data › Find: match case, match the whole cell, Replace All. - Fill handle: fills up and to the left as well as down and right; series run backwards. - Copy and paste: a copied range takes its merged cells along. - Format Painter: also brings the number format. - Fixed: Sort compared every number as equal; it now sorts by the numbers themselves. - The guide covers conditional formatting and Find, in English and Chinese.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.20 — 2026-11-03
text: Changelog › 0.5.20 — 2026-11-03. Sheets and Excel, both ways. - Bring an Excel workbook into Sheets: Sheet Tools › Cells › Excel Workbook… opens .xlsx, .xlsm, .xls, .xlsb and .ods files. Every sheet becomes a tab with: - values, formulas and number formats; - fonts, fills, borders and alignment; - merged cells, column widths and row heights; - frozen panes, tab colour, page setup and pictures. One Undo takes the whole import back. - Save the sheets as an Excel workbook to share: Sheet Tools › Page › Save as Excel. The workbook carries: - real numbers and dates, formulas with their results, and number formats; - styles, merged cells, sizes, pictures, frozen panes, tab colours and page setup. Formulas that read the plan keep working, from the plan's data on hidden sheets. - Excel export, improved (also File › Export › Excel workbook): - number formats (currency, dates, percentages, Text) are kept; - typed dates are real dates; - formulas carry their last results, so the values show at once; - frozen panes, tab colours and hidden tabs are kept. - Country flags survive a round trip: Excel shows the country's name, and a hidden sheet lets Datum Plan bring the flags back. - The ribbon shows Gantt Chart Tools first, then Sheet Tools (Cells, Page).

heading: Changelog › 0.5.20 — 2026-11-03
text: Changelog › 0.5.20 — 2026-11-03. - Backspace on a cell clears it and starts typing there; - a leading + or − before a cell or function starts a formula; - Increase and Decrease Decimal work on Currency. - The guide describes sheets and Excel workbooks, in English and Chinese.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.19 — 2026-11-03
text: Changelog › 0.5.19 — 2026-11-03. Sheets that format, print and behave like a spreadsheet. - Sheet Tools has two tabs, Cells and Page, laid out our own way. - Cells is grouped as Clipboard, Font, Align, Lines, Number, Look, Rows & Columns, Insert and Data. - Look has a full cell style gallery: good, bad and neutral, data and checks, titles and headings, accents at 20, 40, 60 % and full, and number styles. - Page: each sheet prints its own way. - Paper: size, orientation and margins. - What Prints: a print area, title rows on every page, and page breaks. - Fit: to so many pages wide and tall, or a scale. - On the Paper: Header & footer on or off (the cells only, without the plan's logos and title), gridlines, row and column labels, and centre on page. - The same choices are at the top of File › Print. The plan's own page setup is unchanged. They also go into an exported .xlsx workbook. - Three ways to look at a sheet: Normal; Page Layout, the pages exactly as they will print; and Page Breaks, each printed page outlined over the cells with its number. Switch from Sheet Tools › Page or the buttons by the sheet tabs.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.19 — 2026-11-03
text: Changelog › 0.5.19 — 2026-11-03. - Place in cell: a picture on a sheet fits inside its cell, or merged cells, and follows the cell's size. A small button by the selected picture switches it on and off. - Fixed in Sheets, from a full review: - Paste: it now brings formats and number formats and is one undo step. Cut clears the source only when you paste, and one cell pasted on a larger selection fills it. - Fill and sort: filling keeps styles and number formats. Sort moves formulas with their rows and keeps formats, with empty cells last. - dates follow the plan's date format (05/01/2026 is 5 January when the plan writes the day first); - the fill handle continues dates; - a formula on a date shows a date; - the Text format keeps what was typed (001). - Merged cells: deleting the first row of a merge shrinks it instead of removing it, and Enter and Tab step past a merge. - Layout changes: a width, height, merge or page change no longer undoes an edit made a moment before. - Frozen panes: the cell editor and merged titles show in frozen rows; pictures no longer cover the column letters; the cursor stays in view under frozen panes; renaming a sheet keeps its frozen panes.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.19 — 2026-11-03
text: Changelog › 0.5.19 — 2026-11-03. - Sheet size: the sheet goes on past row 200 and column Z. - Rows and text: rows grow to fit a bigger font or wrapped text, and long text runs on over empty cells. - printed sheets show country flags; - cells that only have borders or fills print too; - a sheet prints without row numbers and column letters unless you ask. - Sum in the status bar counts numbers only. - Sheet names are checked for characters a workbook cannot use. - New keys: - [[Ctrl+Arrow]] to the edge of the data; - [[Ctrl+Home]], [[Home]], [[End]] and [[Ctrl+End]]; - [[Page Up]] and [[Page Down]]; - [[Ctrl+Enter]] puts what you typed in every selected cell; - [[Ctrl+D]] on one cell copies the cell above. - The guide describes Sheet Tools › Cells and Page, in English and Chinese.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.18 — 2026-11-03
text: Changelog › 0.5.18 — 2026-11-03. Sheets: clearer tools, a proper colour chooser, and plan data in one click. - Dropdown arrows are part of their button, as in a spreadsheet. Before, they were drawn like pane dividers: a grey bar with a resize cursor. - Pictures in the menus: every border choice shows the lines it draws, line styles show their line, and the merge choices have their own icons. - Colour palette: font colour, fill, border line colour and tab colour open a palette under the button, with: - theme colours with lighter and darker shades; - standard colours; - your recent colours; - More Colors…, a small Colors window with a colour field, a hue bar and hex and RGB boxes. The system colour box that opened at the top of the screen is gone. - Merged cells keep the sheet's white background (they turned grey). - From the plan, on the Sheets toolbar: one click puts a live block at the selected cell. - Project facts: start, finish, status date, baseline finish, % complete, planned %, SPI, CPI and the task counts. - Milestones, Critical, Late, Next 4 weeks, In progress and Resources: live lists. - Task value…: one value of one task, such as its finish or % complete. - The guide describes them, in English and Chinese.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.17 — 2026-11-03
text: Changelog › 0.5.17 — 2026-11-03. Sheets with the tools of a spreadsheet. - Sheet Tools › Home: a ribbon tab that opens by itself in Sheets and goes back to Task when you leave. - Clipboard: Paste (and Paste Special), Cut, Copy and Format Painter. - Font: font, size up to 48, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, colours. - Alignment: top, middle and bottom; left, centre and right; indent; Wrap Text; Merge & Center, Merge Across, Merge Cells and Unmerge. - Borders: bottom, top, left, right, all, outside, thick outside, top and bottom, double and thick lines, no border, with a line colour and style. - Number: formats, currency, percent, comma style and decimals. - Cell styles: Good, Bad, Neutral, Calculation, Check Cell, Input, Output, Note, Title, Headings, Total and Accent. - Cells: insert and delete rows, columns and sheets; row height, column width and AutoFit. - Insert: Picture (a logo from the plan's pictures at a cell), Function, Plan Data and Freeze Panes. - Editing: AutoSum, Fill, Clear, and Sort A to Z or Z to A. - Row heights: drag the line under a row number, or use Format › Row Height. - Sheet tabs work like a spreadsheet's: - double-click to rename in place; - right-click for Insert, Delete, Rename, Move or Copy, Tab Color, Hide and Unhide;

heading: Changelog › 0.5.17 — 2026-11-03
text: Changelog › 0.5.17 — 2026-11-03. - drag a tab to move it. - No more browser boxes: renaming, deleting and naming things (sheets, dashboards, reports, calendars, codes, pictures) now use Datum Plan's own dialogs. - Merged cells, borders, wrapped text, row heights and tab colours are saved in the plan, print as shown, and go into exported .xlsx workbooks. - Selected cells keep their fill colour under a light tint, so formatting stays visible while you work. - Security: the spreadsheet reader used for imports is updated; a malformed .xls or .xlsb file could crash the app. - The guide describes Sheet Tools, in English and Chinese.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.16 — 2026-11-02
text: Changelog › 0.5.16 — 2026-11-02. Logos and pictures in the plan, a fix for Save as PDF, and a full hardening pass. - Pictures and logos are saved in the plan. Project › Pictures (or the Logos step of Project Setup) keeps the logos of the client, your company, the main contractor, consultants, vendors and sub-vendors, and any other picture, inside the .dplan file. - Print header: + Logo ▾ puts any of them on the left, in the centre or on the right. - Dashboards: a new Picture tile. - Sheets: Picture ▾ places one at a cell; drag to move, drag the corner to resize, Delete to remove. It prints with the sheet and goes into an exported .xlsx workbook. - Fixed: Save as PDF could give a blank first page (header and footer only) on prints of two or more pages shrunk to fit the paper. Each printed page is now kept whole, and printing waits for fonts and pictures. - Printing, also fixed: - a long table in a report no longer leaves page 1 nearly empty; - charts in printed reports (Progress, Dashboard, S-Curves) are drawn; - printed reports are on white paper, and side-by-side tables fit the page;

heading: Changelog › 0.5.16 — 2026-11-02
text: Changelog › 0.5.16 — 2026-11-02. - "Legend on the last page only" never pushes the footer off the page, and on portrait paper the legend's text stays in its box; - the Reports view prints the open report, and the look-ahead prints the weeks you chose. - Fixed in the window: Escape closes a dialog after a click on its title; the tutorial notes no longer cover a dialog's buttons. - Fixed in the engine (each with a test): - XER export keeps finish milestones on their day and keeps deadlines; - XML and XER export of a master plan keep the dates held by other plans; - odd numbers in resource rates and limits can no longer make a file that will not open; - two-digit years ("5 Nov 26") read as 2026, and dates stay between 1800 and 2600; - recurring tasks and dates at the end of the calendar stay in order; - numbers are saved exactly; - milestones constrained to their own day no longer show −1 day float; - Mark on Track marks unstarted work; Actual Duration can be typed; % Complete above 100 is refused; - remaining duration on elapsed-day tasks gives the right %, and split pieces are drawn in order; - Activity ID numbering never overflows;

heading: Changelog › 0.5.16 — 2026-11-02
text: Changelog › 0.5.16 — 2026-11-02. - sheet formulas accept the task sheet's column names (Tasks[Task Name], Tasks[Total Slack]). - Faster on big plans: Update Project, Mark on Track, filling % Complete down, levelling and XER, XML, PMXML and MPX exchange. - Public text: the changelog, docs and code comments describe Datum Plan's own design and name no other products. Product and file-format names are trademarks of their owners and are used only to describe file compatibility. - The guide has a new section, "Pictures and logos", in English and Chinese.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.15 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.15 — 2026-11-01. Sharper charts, and any chart in Datum Plot. - Charts look sharper on screen and in print. They are drawn at twice the screen's resolution, and at three times when printing or saving a PDF, so lines and text stay crisp. - Easier to read: - each line ends with its latest value (for example 27.6 % actual against 100 % planned); - the status line names its date; - the bottom axis has a baseline, and the gridlines are lighter. - Datum Plot button on every chart: it opens a copy of the chart's values in Datum Plot, to style the graph for a report or a paper. - Charts over time keep their dates; other charts become a grouped table drawn as bars. - The copy is saved in Documents › Datum Plan › To Datum Plot. - It is a one-way copy: what you change in Datum Plot never changes the plan. - If Datum Plot is not installed, the message says where the file is. - The guide explains the chart buttons, in English and Chinese.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.14 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.14 — 2026-11-01. Plan tabs where you work. - The plan tabs moved below the ribbon, just above the timeline and the plan, so they sit with the plans they switch between. - A tab even for a single plan. ＋ beside it opens another plan in a new tab: Blank plan starts one at once, ready to schedule and link to the other tabs; templates, saved plans, the examples and the tutorial are there too. - Fixed: the ribbon's group names (View, Clipboard, Font…) were cut off on some screens; the ribbon now grows to fit them. - The guide describes the tabs' new place, in English and Chinese.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.13 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.13 — 2026-11-01. A guided tutorial, and the last open items from the full check. - The tutorial (Help › Tutorial, or the tile on the Home page): a small office fit-out, five weeks into the work, that uses every part of Datum Plan. A note at the bottom right of each view says how it was filled in and what to try; Next and Back go through the views in the sidebar. × hides the notes and Help › Tutorial Notes shows them again. The plan uses: - links with lags, a constraint, a deadline, elapsed days, an inactive task and a recurring meeting; - activity codes, your own columns with formulas, and conditional formatting; - people, a material and a cost, resource calendars with leave, and a six-day week for one task; - a baseline, five closed weeks of progress, and a rule of credit with quantities; - risks with duration ranges, a constraint log and the week's notes; - a sheet that reads the plan, a dashboard of your own, a saved report and a saved filter. - Fixed: a cost or material amount above 1,000 was cut to 1,000 when a plan was opened (a 1,500 fee became 1,000). - File exchange: - PMXML keeps links to and from summaries, and percent lags.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.13 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.13 — 2026-11-01. - MPX writes link lags, and names each assignment's resource by ID and unique ID. - MPX writes units as 1 = 100 % and the rates in their right fields. - XER keeps physical % complete both ways. - Very large .xls and .ods sheets are refused with a message instead of exhausting memory. - Resource custom fields with a classic formula (IIf, [Field]) now work out their value for each resource. - In a formula column, Tasks[Cost] and Resources[...] read the whole column. - Dates in text show in the plan's date format. - Max() and Min() with nothing in them show an error. - Sheets and dashboards: - Dashboard tiles follow a sheet that is renamed, or whose rows or columns are inserted or deleted. - An insert that would push cells off the sheet is refused. - Scheduling: a task shared by people on different calendars counts finish-to-finish links and finish constraints back on the right calendar. - Schedule risk: the hit rate of a risk counts only the runs kept. - The guide explains the tutorial, in English and Chinese.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.12 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.5.12 — 2026-10-31. A dashboard that leads with the S-curve, and a full check of every engine: formulas, scheduling, links between plans, progress, file exchange and security. - The project dashboard: the S-curve across the whole page, then the other charts side by side, filling each row with no empty space. A card shows only when the plan has data for it (no costs: no cost cards; no resources: no manpower). Cards ▾ lets you choose the cards yourself; a card you turn on without data stays blank, also in print. The choice is saved with the plan. - A field that reads itself, or two fields that read each other, shows an error instead of closing the app. - Fields that read other fields are worked out once, not again and again: a chain of 16 fields over 200 rows went from over a minute to a fraction of a second. - Very long or deeply nested formulas are refused instead of crashing. - "" (empty text) works in formulas, as in IIf([Text1] = "", …). - Classic formula functions give the standard results: - DateDiff in weeks and hours, and the quarter ("q") interval; - Sgn(0) is 0, and Round uses banker's rounding; - Mod and \ round their operands first; - InStr counts characters, with a start position;

heading: Changelog › 0.5.12 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.5.12 — 2026-10-31. - numbers in text keep their digits. - A finish field rolled up to a summary shows the right day. - A formula column that reads a classic-formula field gets the current value. - Sheets show numbers, not dates, for columns G to K of sheets other than Plan. - A phase with a finished task no longer shows zero float and turns critical. - Links to other plans use the lag calendar you chose (Schedule Options). - Remaining work after a split counts only the pauses still ahead. - A started task waits for its unfinished predecessor in another plan (retained logic), as it does for one in the same plan. - With several people on a task, it starts when the first of them can. - Links to dates before 1970 work. - Speed: scheduling, the network diagram and the checks take linear time (10,000 tasks: a tenth of a second instead of one second, and 20,000 in under 0.2 s). Levelling puts 120 one-day tasks for one person on 120 days in a quarter of a second; before, it gave up after 5 s with the person still over-allocated. - Update Links: - It names the links it cannot follow (a deleted task, a file not found) instead of saying all is up to date.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.12 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.5.12 — 2026-10-31. - It tells apart plans of the same name in different folders. - Progress and reports: - Baseline work is kept when the baseline is set, so work variance shows. - The planned S-curve reaches 100 % when the baseline ends after the current plan. - Without a status date, earned value, the cost curve and planned % are measured on the same day as the progress shown beside them. - A summary's % complete is rounded like the project's (67 %, not 66 %). - Schedule risk counts risks on milestones and on phases. - File exchange: - XER keeps links to and from summaries, percent lags, resource rates and cost resources, and reads calendar hours in either order. - Project XML keeps fixed costs, elapsed durations and physical % complete. - A damaged XER calendar no longer stops the import. - Security and safety: - A plan from someone else can no longer make Windows connect to a network server it names (subplans and links are looked for on your own server or next to the plan). - A tiny crafted .xlsx file or a deeply nested XML file can no longer crash the app on import. - Report names are escaped in Save as HTML, and updates are downloaded only from this app's own releases.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.11 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.5.11 — 2026-10-31. Pictures and a full legend in print, subplans that print as you see them, and a checked engine. - Pictures in the header, as many as you like: on the left, in the centre and on the right, side by side, on every page. Each picture has its own size; ← and → move it along the row or to the next place; × takes it out. The header grows to fit them. - Fixed: a picture in the centre covered the title and subtitle. They now sit under the centre pictures. Title size sets how large the title prints. - A complete legend. It lists only what the pages show (task, critical task, progress, milestone, critical milestone, summary, subplan, baseline, deadline, link, status date) beside the project's name, start, finish and status date. Print bars show the baseline and the deadline, as on screen. - Fixed: expanded subplans printed collapsed. The Subplans choice now sits under What to print; "As shown on screen" prints the subplans you expanded with their tasks. - Engine fixes from a full check of formulas, links and progress: - DateDiff and DateAdd count months and years by the calendar: 30 Nov to 1 Dec is one month, and adding a month keeps the time.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.11 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.5.11 — 2026-10-31. - A finish date from a formula shows its own day, not the day before. - A plan of milestones only reports its % complete. - The cost curve's earned line adds up to the earned value, and follows physical % complete when the task uses it. - Earned schedule counts working time within a day. - A level-of-effort task ends the working day before its successor starts. - A start-to-start link from a summary follows the summary's start. - Actual dates on a day off stand as recorded. - A link to another plan on a summary holds back every task under it. - A row that mirrors a task in another plan (start-to-start and finish-to-finish to the same task) takes its length. - Update Links settles long hand-back chains between plans. - The guide explains the header pictures, the legend and printing subplans, in English and Chinese.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.10 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.5.10 — 2026-10-31. Printing you can rely on, with a simple header and footer. - Save as PDF writes exactly the pages in the preview to a file you name, at the paper size and orientation you chose, with nothing added by Windows: no date, window title, web address or page count. Print… opens the print window for a printer. - Fixed: blank or split pages and the browser's own header and footer. The print window read the page setup after the app had already removed it, so a landscape page came out on portrait sheets, split in two (half blank), with the browser's date, title and address. The page setup now stays in place until the print window has finished. - Fixed: the print settings panel was squashed into one line with a sideways scroll bar (Header, View and every other tab). A style name of the plan tabs clashed with the panel's.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.10 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.5.10 — 2026-10-31. - Header & footer, simply: up to three pictures at the top (left, centre, right; your company logo or any picture) with one height for all, a title (the plan's name unless you type another) and a subtitle, and at the bottom only what you tick: printed date (and time), page number, status date, company name, revision and your own text. Nothing else is printed. Advanced keeps the code boxes for exact control; plans that used their own header or footer keep it. - Master plans print their subplans as on screen (purple rows, their tasks in grey), or one row each, with all their tasks, or not at all (View › Subplans). - Page Setup tabs fit on one line; margins read Top, Right, Bottom, Left. - The guide explains Save as PDF and the header and footer, in English and Chinese.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.9 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.5.9 — 2026-10-31. The whole project in the master's Gantt. - The combined view. Under the master's own tasks, each subplan has a row (◇) with its duration, dates and the columns shown, in the order and hierarchy of Subplans, and a purple bar on the Gantt. Subplans are read from their files, open or not. - Expand a subplan (▷) to see its tasks in the master, greyed and read-only. - Double-click a subplan's task (or right-click › Go to this task in its plan) to open the subplan's tab with that task selected, and change it there. - Format › Show/Hide › Subplans turns the combined view on and off. - The guide explains the combined view, in English and Chinese.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.8 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.5.8 — 2026-10-31. A project made of plans: a master plan and its subplans, kept together. - The master keeps the project's list of subplans, in order, with a hierarchy: a subplan can sit under another (two engineering plans under Engineering). Dates still come from the links between the plans; the list arranges them. - Project › Subplans: each subplan with its dates, % complete, number of tasks and whether it is open; ↑ ↓ to reorder, Indent and Outdent for the hierarchy, Show or Open, and × to take a plan out of the project (its file is kept). - New Subplan… makes a plan of the project: a name and its place, saved next to the master with the same calendars and currency, and opened in its tab. Add Existing… takes a saved plan into the project. The master is saved straight away when it had no other changes, so the list is not lost. - The project's tabs sit together, in one colour: ◆ marks the master and › its subplans, in the master's order; other plans keep plain tabs. A subplan open without its master shows Open master beside the tabs.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.8 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.5.8 — 2026-10-31. - Opening a master offers to open its subplans. A tab's right-click menu has Open All Subplans, New Subplan… and Close Project (the master and its open subplans, asking to save changes first). - The linked-plans example is now one project: the main schedule is the master of engineering, procurement and construction. - The browser's own right-click menu (Back, Reload…) no longer appears in the window, outside text fields. - The guide explains projects, the master and subplans, in English and Chinese.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.7 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.5.7 — 2026-10-31. Clearer links between plans, and fixes. - Go to the linked task. Click the ⇠ or ⇢ mark by a task's ID (or right-click › Linked Tasks…): the menu lists the tasks it is linked to, and Go to shows the other plan's tab with that task selected, opening the plan from its file when it is not open. - See when a link needs updating. When the other plan has moved, the mark turns amber (⇠!), the label on the Gantt says so, and the plan's tab shows ⟳ with how many tasks wait for new dates. Update Links is on the mark's menu and the tab's right-click menu. - File › Close and Close All, and Close / Close All Plans on a tab's right-click menu.
