New and Open add a tab and leave the others open; now they are easy to close. - Link to a plan that is not open: Browse… in Link to Plan picks a saved plan file. - Fixed: saving one plan deleted the recovery copies of the other open plans with unsaved changes. Each unsaved plan now keeps its copy until it is saved or closed. - Fixed: Escape did not close menus. - The guide explains Go to, the update warnings and closing plans, in English and Chinese.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.6 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.5.6 — 2026-10-31. See at a glance what is linked to what between plans. - Marks by the ID: ⇠ (purple) on a task that waits for a task in another plan (click it to see or change the link), ⇢ (green) on a task that a task in another open plan waits for. Point at a mark to read the tasks. - On the Gantt: what a task waits for is written before its bar in purple, with a dashed arrow into it ("Construction › A1130 Mechanical completion ⇢ ◆"); which other plan waits for it is written after the bar in green ("→ Construction › A1010 Site mobilisation"). - Linked Plans now shows both directions: what this plan waits for, and which tasks of this plan other open plans wait for, with Show plan to open that tab. - The External Predecessors column reads like the Gantt: "Engineering › A1180 Final documentation issued (FS)". - The linked-plans example shows the External Predecessors column beside Finish, and every plan's calendar closes for Christmas and New Year. - The guide explains how to see what is linked, in English and Chinese.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.5 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.5.5 — 2026-10-31. Several plans at once, in tabs, with links between them: a main schedule and its subplans, each in its own file, moving together. - Plan tabs. Every plan you open or create gets a tab above the ribbon; a dot marks unsaved changes, × closes it (asking to save first), ＋ makes a new plan, opens one or opens the example. Ctrl+Tab goes to the next tab, Ctrl+W closes one. Opening a plan that is already open shows its tab. When you close the window, every plan with unsaved changes is listed and can be saved at once, and recovery covers every open plan. - Links between plans. Select a task and choose Project › Link to Plan (or right-click › Link to Plan…): pick another open plan, find its task, and set the type (FS, SS, FF, SF) and lag. The task waits for it like for a normal link. The External Predecessors column shows the links.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.5 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.5.5 — 2026-10-31. - Linked Plans (Project tab) lists every link of the plan with the date it last knew and the date now, and marks the ones that have Moved. Update All Open Plans brings the new dates into every open plan, in the right order, until nothing moves; Update This Plan does one. Plans that are not open are read from their files, and links still find each other when the folder is moved. A loop between plans is refused with a message. - A detailed example: File › Linked plans (example). A compressor station in four plans saved to a folder you choose and opened in tabs: a main schedule with its milestones, engineering, procurement (with long-lead equipment and costs) and construction, joined by thirteen links. Engineering and construction use resource calendars (a lead engineer's leave, a six-day site week with a holiday break). Change the manufacture time in procurement and update the links to see the main schedule move. - The guide has a new chapter on tabs and links between plans, in English and Chinese.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.4 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.5.4 — 2026-10-31. Resource calendars that drive task dates: each person's own working week and leave decide when their work gets done. - Working Time for each person. Resources › Info… › Working Time: the person's base calendar (the project calendar, or another such as a six-day site week) and their leave or exceptions: annual leave, training, a holiday at home, or mornings or afternoons only. - Turn it on in Project › Schedule Options › Resource calendars. Each assignment then runs on the person's own calendar, and a task finishes when the last person on it finishes. A task with its own calendar works only when both the task and the person work. It is off until you switch it on, so existing plans keep their dates. - Ignore Resource Calendar (a task field, in the details and as a column) keeps a task on its own calendar whoever works on it: a cure time, a delivery. - Workload, the Resource Graph and levelling count each person's own available hours, so leave shows as less capacity. - Exchange files keep it: Project XML writes and reads a calendar per person with their leave (and Ignore Resource Calendar); XER writes resource calendars and resource-dependent activities, and reads them back. - The guide has a new section on resource calendars, in English and Chinese.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.3 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.5.3 — 2026-10-30. Your own dashboards: build the board your client or manager wants, inside the plan, always up to date. - Several dashboards per plan, as tabs on the Dashboard page next to the built-in Project dashboard. + New dashboard makes a blank one or starts from a template: Client dashboard, Weekly progress or Vendors and countries. Rename, duplicate or delete them from Dashboard ▾. - Tiles you lay out yourself. Edit layout, then + Add tile; drag tiles to reorder them, and set each one's width (a quarter to full width) and height (one to four rows). - Number: any formula, as in Sheets (=SPI, =ProjectFinish, =COUNTIF(Tasks[Late],TRUE), =Vendors!B4), with a format, a second line and an optional rule that turns it green or red. - Progress ring: a percentage as a ring. - Chart: one of the plan's charts (S-curve, progress per period, progress by phase, cost and earned value, manpower), or a chart of a sheet range or formula: columns, stacked columns, bars, line, area, doughnut or pie. - Table: a plan list (milestones, late or critical tasks, starting next period, completed this period), or a sheet range or formula; a column of countries shows their flags. - Countries: flags with how many resources or vendors come from each country. - Text: a heading or a note.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.3 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.5.3 — 2026-10-30. - Dashboards are saved with the plan, follow every change and print with Print / PDF. - A new name for formulas: PlannedPercent, where the baseline says the plan should be at the status date (0–100). - The guide has a new section on dashboards, in English and Chinese.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.2 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.5.2 — 2026-10-30. Better-looking charts that are never cut off. - A new look for every chart (Dashboard, S-Curves, Manpower, Schedule Risk, reports, Report Builder): smooth lines with a soft fill under the actual progress, rounded bars, light horizontal gridlines instead of heavy black axes, round legend markers, a dark rounded tooltip and a status-date label, in a clearer set of colours. - No more cropped charts. Charts follow their box when the window, the sidebar or the panes change size, and they are laid out again for printing, so a printed or PDF dashboard shows every chart whole (two per row). - Charts in the same row are the same height, with no empty band under the shorter one. - A chart with nothing to show says so ("No costs in this plan yet", "No hours assigned yet") instead of drawing empty axes. - Manpower's forecast joins its weeks with straight lines (a smooth curve suggested values between the weeks). - The guide's pictures show the new charts.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.1 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.5.1 — 2026-10-30. - Scrolling the schedule no longer sticks. The task sheet and the Gantt chart scroll together; each one used to echo the other's position back a moment late, so smooth scrolling fought itself and seemed to get stuck (worst near the end of the plan). Now a pane that was moved by the other does not echo it back. - Tell Me (Ctrl+K) no longer hides the window. The search box now opens over the plan with the window dimmed behind it, instead of a blank page.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.0 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.5.0 — 2026-10-30. Sheets that work like a spreadsheet and read the plan live: your own reports and vendor lists inside the plan file, with nothing copied by hand. - Click cells into a formula. Type =, then click a cell or drag over several to add them (A1, A1:A5), or click another sheet's tab; each reference gets a coloured box. F4 cycles the $ anchors, and Enter closes any bracket left open. - Suggestions as you type: all 490 functions, the plan's names and table columns, with Tab to insert. Inside a function, a hint shows its arguments with the current one underlined. - Σ AutoSum (Alt+=; also Average, Count, Max, Min) and fx Insert Function, which finds a function by name or by what it does. - Fill and paste carry formulas: the fill handle, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+R and copy and paste move references (=A1*2 becomes =A2*2); Cut moves cells. - Insert and delete rows and columns (right-click, the toolbar, Ctrl+Shift++ and Ctrl+−); formulas on every sheet follow, and references to deleted cells show #REF!. Renaming a sheet updates the formulas that name it.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.0 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.5.0 — 2026-10-30. - Number formats: spreadsheet format codes (#,##0.00, 0.0%, dd-mmm-yy, custom codes), more or fewer decimals, currency and the plan's date format. Results of TODAY, DATE or a lookup of plan dates show as dates by themselves, and plan percentages get a % sign. - Results that spill into several cells (FILTER, SORT, UNIQUE, SEQUENCE…) are shown. Column widths can be dragged or fitted with a double-click. Pointing at an error explains it. - Fixed: typing quickly into a cell no longer loses the second key. The plan, live, by name - Tasks[column] has one row per task (Name, Start, Finish, % Complete, baseline dates and cost, float, Critical, Late, Milestone, Resources, earned value, custom fields…); Resources[column] has Name, Group, Country, Rate, Work, Cost…. - Names for the plan's numbers: ProjectFinish, BaselineFinish, FinishVariance, PercentComplete, SPI, CPI, TotalCost, TasksLate, CriticalCount and more. - Plan Data… puts a live list at the selected cell: milestones, critical, late, unfinished or in-progress tasks, or those starting in the next four weeks, with the columns, order and number of rows you choose. One formula fills the rows and follows the plan. - Older formulas such as =SUM(Plan!M2:M200) keep working. Excel export adds the Tasks and Resources tables and the names, so the workbook works in other spreadsheet programs too.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.0 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.5.0 — 2026-10-30. - A Country with flag number format shows a country's flag and name: type a code (DE, cn) or a name (Germany, UK). - Resources have a Country (person, crew or vendor), shown with its flag in the Resource Sheet and readable as Resources[Country]. - Help › Guide works on computers without a Downloads folder set up (it saves in the home folder's Downloads, Documents or the temporary folder instead). - The guide's chapter on Sheets is rewritten with two new pictures, in English and Chinese.

heading: Changelog › 0.4.4 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.4.4 — 2026-10-29. The Datum Plan Guide: a step-by-step guide with pictures, in English and Simplified Chinese. - Help › Guide (and a Guide tile on the File page, with a PDF icon) offers the guide in English or 中文. One click downloads it from GitHub, checks it against the release's checksums, saves it in your Downloads folder and opens it. The app itself stays small. - About 30 pages with numbered screenshots: installing and updating, the window, building a plan (tasks, durations, links, constraints, calendars), people, man-hours and costs, baseline and progress, reports and printing, risk, the look-ahead and manpower, sheets and formulas, files, the command line, a glossary of planning terms and the keyboard shortcuts. - The Chinese guide keeps the English names of buttons and menus (the app is in English) with their Chinese meaning beside them, and has an English–Chinese glossary. - The first time Datum Plan starts, a short hint points to the guide. Tell Me (Ctrl+K) finds it too.

heading: Changelog › 0.4.3 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.4.3 — 2026-10-29. - Windows now lists the publisher as Datum. - An update keeps a custom install folder chosen at the first install (the installer used to remember it under the old publisher name).

heading: Changelog › 0.4.2 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.4.2 — 2026-10-29. Stronger and safer, with a command line for scripts and AI assistants, and every report view printable. Robustness and security - An internal error no longer closes the app. The action that failed is stopped with a message, the plan stays as it was, and the details go to crash.log in the app's data folder (nothing is sent anywhere). - Saving can no longer corrupt a plan. Plans, autosave copies, exports and settings are written to a temporary file first and then replace the old file in one step, so a crash or a full disk never leaves a half-written file. - Damaged or hand-made plan files can no longer crash or freeze the app. Values far out of range (a duration of a million years, huge lags or delays, a zero-length working day, impossible numbers) are clamped when the plan opens, and the calendar arithmetic has a safe horizon (years 1800 to 2600). Files over 300 MB are refused. - Long plans stay quick. Working time over long spans is counted a week at a time, and daily S-curves of plans longer than ten years use weeks.

heading: Changelog › 0.4.2 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.4.2 — 2026-10-29. - Updates are stricter. An update installs only if the release has a checksum file and the download matches it exactly; it downloads into its own new folder, with a size limit, and only installer files with the expected name are accepted. - CSV exports cannot run formulas when opened in a spreadsheet: text starting with =, +, - or @ gets a leading apostrophe. Calendar (.ics) exports escape line breaks fully. - A tighter security policy for the window (no frames, objects, form posts or remote scripts), and links open only to this project's pages. - New checks on every change: every engine function run on deliberately hostile plans and edits, hostile spreadsheet formulas, a security audit of the window's libraries (npm audit) next to the existing licence and advisory check. Command line and AI assistants - datum-cli (on the Releases page): show a plan's facts or its schedule (also as CSV), change it with named operations, export it to any format, run the schedule risk analysis or the look-ahead, and start plans from templates. - Named operations: every change to a plan is one of the operations the window sends; datum-cli ops lists them with an example each.

heading: Changelog › 0.4.2 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.4.2 — 2026-10-29. - datum-cli mcp: a Model Context Protocol server, so an AI assistant can open or start a plan, read the schedule, change it with the same operations, run the risk analysis and save it. A failed change leaves the plan as it was; nothing is saved unless asked. - Costs are exact to the cent: each task's cost and actual cost are kept in whole cents, so totals are the exact sum of what you see. Typed fixed costs are kept to the cent. Print and polish - Schedule Risk, Look-ahead and Manpower print as themselves. Before, printing one of them printed the Dashboard. On paper, Schedule Risk's charts take the full width. - The last Schedule Risk run is kept with the plan, so it is still there after reopening (with the date it was run). - Photos in progress reports could not be added: the window's security policy blocked the picture while it was being resized. They work again. - An empty plan's work showed as "-0 hrs".

heading: Changelog › 0.4.1 — 2026-10-28
text: Changelog › 0.4.1 — 2026-10-28. Progress history: the actual S-curve follows what really happened at each period close, and new tools for the weeks ahead. Progress over time - Actual S-curves follow the stored periods. Each time you close a period (or store a snapshot), the progress of every task is kept. The actual line now runs through those points instead of a straight line from the start to today, and so do the progress report and the dashboard. - Earned schedule on the S-Curves page and the Dashboard: when the plan expected the progress made so far, SPI(t) (schedule performance in time, which stays meaningful near the end of a project), and the finish date at the current pace. - Manpower (Progress › Manpower, or the sidebar): people per week or month for all trades or one trade (a resource's Group), planned against the work done so far and the forecast for the rest. - Rules of Credit (Progress › Rules of Credit): split a kind of work into weighted steps (for example cable: pulled 60 %, terminated 30 %, tested 10 %). There are built-in rules for concrete, steel, piping, cable, equipment, documents and software, and you can make your own. Applying a rule gives the selected tasks those steps; ticking them off sets the task's physical % complete.

heading: Changelog › 0.4.1 — 2026-10-28
text: Changelog › 0.4.1 — 2026-10-28. - Installed quantities: new task columns Quantity, Installed Quantity and Quantity Unit. Installed ÷ planned quantity becomes the task's physical % complete. - Physical % complete now counts in the S-curves for every task that uses it, not only when progress is weighted by physical. Look-ahead (Progress › Look-ahead, or the sidebar) - The unfinished work in the next 2, 3, 4 or 6 weeks from the status date, with a bar for each task and whether it is ready to start. - A constraint log: what each task needs before it can start (material, drawings, permits, access, people, equipment), who owns it, the need-by date and whether it is cleared. A task is ready when all its constraints are cleared; overdue ones are flagged. - Drop-down lists whose choices load a moment later (the Resource Graph's person or trade, the progress report's period, the constraint log's task) now show the right choice.

heading: Changelog › 0.4.0 — 2026-10-28
text: Changelog › 0.4.0 — 2026-10-28. Risk and resources: see how likely your finish date is, see the workload of each trade, preview levelling, and get a report on every import. Schedule Risk (Report › Schedule Risk, or the sidebar) - Runs the plan 500 to 5,000 times. In each run every unfinished task takes a duration between its optimistic and pessimistic duration (most often the planned one), and each open risk in the register happens with its probability. - Shows the chance of finishing by the planned date, the P50, P80 and P90 finish dates, the cost at P50 and P80, a chart of finish dates with the cumulative curve, how often each task was critical, and which tasks drive the finish. - New task columns Optimistic Duration and Pessimistic Duration. Tasks without them use a default range (−10 % to +25 %, which you can change). - The Risk Register has a new Delay (days) column: working days a risk adds to its linked tasks when it happens (an opportunity takes them off). Probabilities 1–5 count as 10 %, 30 %, 50 %, 70 % and 90 %. - The same plan and settings always give the same answer, so you can compare before and after a change.

heading: Changelog › 0.4.0 — 2026-10-28
text: Changelog › 0.4.0 — 2026-10-28. - Resource Graph › Trades adds up everyone in the same Group (their trade or role) against the trade's capacity. People shows the load as people instead of hours. - Level All and Level Selection first show a preview: which tasks move, the new finish date, and how many overallocated days remain. Nothing changes until you click Level. - Opening an XML or XER file ends with a short report: anything Datum Plan changed or left out (links to tasks that are not in the file, secondary constraints, elapsed lags), and whether every task gets the same start and finish as in the file, with the first differences listed. - XER files keep their activity types: level of effort, WBS summary, resource dependent and milestones. - Resource Graph bars and labels stay in place when you switch between people, trades and periods. - A horizontal bar chart now names every bar.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.12 — 2026-10-28
text: Changelog › 0.3.12 — 2026-10-28. Trust in the dates: the scheduling engine is now checked against worked examples, plan files that carry their own dates, and thousands of random plans. The checks found two scheduling mistakes, now fixed. - As Late As Possible tasks with successors now move only as far as their free float allows, so they never delay the tasks that follow them. Before, they used all their total float and could push past a successor's link. - Float before work already under way is right again. A task's late dates were measured against the whole duration of a successor that had already started, rather than its remaining work, so with retained logic the predecessor could show negative float it did not have. - Finished tasks no longer limit the float of the tasks before them, and with progress override neither does work already under way. Under the hood - 47 hand-worked scheduling cases (over 90 task dates checked to the minute): every link type with leads and lags in days, hours and percent, every constraint, deadlines, holidays, part days, task calendars, elapsed durations, splits, summaries, progress with retained logic and override, scheduling from the finish, levelling, critical tasks and man-hours.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.12 — 2026-10-28
text: Changelog › 0.3.12 — 2026-10-28. - Plan files that carry their own dates (Project XML and XER, in crates/core/tests/parity) are opened, rescheduled and compared task by task. Exports from other scheduling tools can be dropped into the same folder. - Random-plan checks now include constraints, calendars, splits and elapsed tasks: every link must hold, no task may start later than its links need, and the dates must not depend on the row order. Random sequences of edits must never break a plan, and damaged CSV and Excel files must never crash the app.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.11 — 2026-10-27
text: Changelog › 0.3.11 — 2026-10-27. Sturdier: new automatic checks found and fixed two ways a damaged file could stop the app, and two small bugs are gone. - Dashboard: without a status date, actual progress is measured at today or at the latest progress you recorded, whichever is later, so a plan updated ahead of time no longer shows 0 %. The Dashboard says which date it used. - Date picker: it closes as soon as you pick a date. - Opening a damaged XER file no longer stops the app: a WBS that loops back on itself, or a cut-off calendar, is read as far as it makes sense. - If anything inside the app ever fails, the rest of the app keeps working (before, one failure could lock every later command). Under the hood - New automatic checks on every change: a failed edit must leave the plan exactly as it was; 1,000 random plans must schedule without errors and with sensible dates; thousands of damaged XML, XER and plan files must never crash the app; 2,000 tasks must reschedule quickly (about 3 ms in the app). - Checks on Windows and macOS as well as Linux, and a licence and security check of every library the app uses. - SECURITY.md and CONTRIBUTING.md.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.10 — 2026-10-25
text: Changelog › 0.3.10 — 2026-10-25. - Roadmap on the File page (a Home tile and a sidebar item): everything Datum Plan will do next and when, with links to suggest a feature or report an issue. - Print: "Fit timescale to 1 page wide" no longer adds a nearly empty second page when the table is wide (e.g. with the Man-hours and Cost columns). - Network Diagram: the cross on completed tasks is lighter, so the text stays readable. - The Roadmap list is kept in docs/site.json, which the Datum family website will read too.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.9 — 2026-10-25
text: Changelog › 0.3.9 — 2026-10-25. A small "?" beside the tools: click it to see what the tool is for and how to use it. Help beside every tool - Every ribbon group has a small ? next to its name. A click opens a short card: what the tool does, how to use it, and a tip where one helps. - The views (Network Diagram, Check Schedule, Risk Register, resources, Portfolio, Update Progress, reports), the details pane, Project Setup and the main dialogs (Task Information, Change Working Time, Schedule Options, Set Baseline, Formula Column, Reporting Periods, Columns, Bar Styles, Conditional Formatting) have one too. - Help › What Is This Tool? lists every card, so you can read about a tool before you look for it. - Dialogs with only a Close button (such as these help cards) now close with Escape or Enter straight away.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.8 — 2026-10-24
text: Changelog › 0.3.8 — 2026-10-24. - Printed Gantt charts now show the links between tasks (Finish-to-Start and the other types), as on screen. Critical links are drawn in red. - Date picker: every date can now be picked from a calendar. - In the task sheet, the selected date cell (Start, Finish, Deadline, Constraint Date, baseline dates…) shows a calendar button. - In the details pane, every date field has one. - Typing a date still works. A real Tracking Gantt, templates with a team and man-hours, a whiteboard-style Network Diagram, one grid engine and a consistent icon set. Tracking Gantt (now different from the Gantt chart) - Grey bars show the baseline under each task. Coloured bars show the current dates, solid where the work is done and light where it remains. Each bar shows its % complete. - Opens with the Tracking table: actual start, actual finish, % complete, physical %, actual and remaining duration, actual cost and work. Going back to the Gantt chart brings the Entry table back. - A banner explains what you see. When there is no baseline yet, it says so and offers Set Baseline. Templates with people, man-hours and costs - Every template has its team, on 8-hour days on the Standard calendar, with groups, hourly rates and available units: project managers, engineers, crews, technicians…

heading: Changelog › 0.3.8 — 2026-10-24
text: Changelog › 0.3.8 — 2026-10-24. - Tasks are assigned to people (e.g. "Design Engineer[200%]"), so man-hours, costs, resource usage, the histogram and overallocation work from the first click. - Purchases and contracts have fixed costs. - New Man-hours (Work) and Cost columns in the task sheet. - A dotted whiteboard canvas on screen; printing stays on white paper. - Cards: white with a coloured edge (red for critical, blue otherwise) and a soft shadow. Milestones are amber hexagons; summaries are slanted boxes. - Summary tasks: show the phases as boxes over their first task. - By WBS: each top-level phase in its own band, with its name. One grid engine for the task sheet and Sheets - Both views now share one engine for selection, keyboard, clipboard, fill and formatting. - Sheets gains several ranges with Ctrl+click, whole columns from the column letters, whole rows from the row numbers, Shift to extend, and Sum, Average and Count in the formula bar. - Clear, number formats and text formatting act on every selected range. - Redrawn in one line style: the progress, scroll, track, baseline, split, manual, auto, inactive and style icons, and a new Custom Fields icon. Every view prints properly, a complete Network Diagram, a zoom box on the timeline, and the finishing touches from your 0.3.5 review. Task tab, fonts and formatting

heading: Changelog › 0.3.8 — 2026-10-24
text: Changelog › 0.3.8 — 2026-10-24. - Font list (Aptos, Calibri, Arial, Segoe UI, Tahoma, Verdana, Times New Roman, Cambria, Georgia, Garamond, Consolas, IBM Plex Sans), each shown in its own font. Used in the sheet, Sheets tabs and printouts. - Fill colour has a proper paint-bucket icon. - The Task tab now also holds the everyday commands: % complete, Mark on Track, Link, Unlink, Indent, Outdent, Find, Scroll to Task, Fill Down. - Paste is a split button: Paste, Paste Special… (Ctrl+Alt+V), Paste Values, Paste Formatting, Transpose. Fill and paste (task sheet and Sheets) - The fill handle continues series: - numbers 1, 2, 3 (or any step); - "Phase 1" → "Phase 2"; - dates continue their step. - Hold Ctrl to copy instead. Durations, links and resources are copied. - Paste Special: all, values only or formats only, and transpose. - Sheets tabs: a fill handle (down or right), Ctrl+D, Ctrl+R and Freeze Panes. Timeline zoom box - The timeline shows the part of the plan in view as a box: drag it to scroll, drag its edges to zoom, double-click for the whole project. It follows the Gantt chart. The status date is marked. - Box styles with a legend: - critical (red), not critical (blue); - milestone (hexagon), summary (dashed); - completed (crossed), in progress (slashed), late (amber corner).

heading: Changelog › 0.3.8 — 2026-10-24
text: Changelog › 0.3.8 — 2026-10-24. - Compact, Standard and Detailed boxes. Detailed adds total float, % complete and resources. - Driving links in bold. Link labels for SS, FF, SF and lags, with a tooltip on every link. - Zoom, Fit, 100%, Ctrl+wheel, drag to pan, and a mini-map for large networks. - Highlight path: select a task to light up its whole chain of predecessors and successors. Printing for every view (File › Print) - Network Diagram: across pages, with its legend. It stays readable and continues on more pages. - Calendar: a month per page with task bars. - Resource Sheet, Task Usage, Resource Usage, Team Planner and Sheets tabs: as tables, split down and across with the first column repeated. Sheets print with their cell formatting. - Dashboard, Progress, S-curves, Report Builder, reports and other pages: as shown, with your header and footer on every page and page numbers. - All views use the same paper, margins, scaling, headers, footers and logos. Excel export keeps formatting - Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, font, size, colours, fill and alignment are kept for tasks and sheet cells, along with sheet column widths. Help and links - File › Home: "Check again" shows a spinner, then the time it checked. GitHub, Releases and Report an Issue buttons open the project's pages.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.8 — 2026-10-24
text: Changelog › 0.3.8 — 2026-10-24. - Help tab: Getting Started (for people coming from other scheduling programs or spreadsheets), a Glossary (FS, SS, FF, SF, lag, float, critical and longest path, baseline, status date, SPI/CPI…), GitHub links. - The link type in the details pane reads "FS · Finish-to-Start", with a ? button that opens the Glossary. A cleaner ribbon, Setup in the sidebar, full control of columns, and printing that includes every column. - The Task tab is split into three: Task (clipboard, font, alignment, insert, properties), Schedule (links, outline, manual/auto, split, leveling, critical and longest path, find, global change), and Progress (% complete, Mark on Track, Update Progress, status date, reporting periods, baselines, snapshots, progress reports). - No more sideways scrollbar. On a narrow window the ribbon tightens, then shows icons only, so every command stays in view and group names are no longer cut off. - New icons for Setup and Notes. - Setup is now the first icon in the left sidebar and opens as a page, not a panel over the plan. New plans open on it. Skip or Done takes you to your chosen view. - Fixed: the Insert Column categories (General, Schedule, Progress…) now open their list of fields. Menus can have any number of levels. "Search all fields…" is at the top. - Right-click a column heading:

heading: Changelog › 0.3.8 — 2026-10-24
text: Changelog › 0.3.8 — 2026-10-24. - Hide Column (the column stays in the table, hidden); - Unhide Columns ▸ (lists the hidden ones, or Unhide All); - Delete Column (with undo). For a custom or formula column it asks whether to remove it from the table or delete the field and all its values. - New Columns… dialog (heading menu, View › Data, Format › Columns): all fields on the left; the table's columns on the right with Show, width, order and remove. - Every column of the table prints by default (Task Name, Duration, Start, Finish, Predecessors, Resources, % Complete…), not just the first three. - Fixed: the chart no longer overlaps the last table columns. - A table wider than the page continues on the next page without cutting a column in half. ID and Task Name repeat on every page. - "Fit timescale to N pages wide" now really fits: it shrinks the page when the table is wide. - Page Setup › View: - choose and order the columns to print; - text size and row height; - shrink columns to fit; - wrap long task names; - print task notes on the last pages. Printing and PDF done properly, text formatting (bold, colours, fonts), and a clearer Options page.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.8 — 2026-10-24
text: Changelog › 0.3.8 — 2026-10-24. Print and PDF (File › Print, Ctrl+P, or Report › Page Setup) - A new Print page: settings on the left, a live preview of every page on the right. - Print the entire project or specific dates (from and to), and all pages or only some (e.g. 1-3, 5). - Paper A4, A3, A2, A1, Letter, Legal or Tabloid, landscape or portrait. - Scaling: adjust to a percentage, or fit the timescale to a number of pages wide. - Margins in millimetres. - Header and footer with left, centre and right parts. Codes for page number, total pages, date, project, company, client, manager, status date, project start and finish. The company logo and a client logo can go on either side. - Legend on every page, the last page or none, with your own text. - Columns: all of them or the first few, repeated on every page or only on the first. Gridlines, ID column and timescale units are adjustable. - Pages are drawn as vector graphics, so the Gantt chart and text stay sharp in PDFs. Choose "Save as PDF" in the print window. - The page setup is saved with the plan. Text formatting (Task tab › Font and Alignment)

heading: Changelog › 0.3.8 — 2026-10-24
text: Changelog › 0.3.8 — 2026-10-24. - Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, font size, font colour, fill colour, and left, centre or right alignment for selected cells. Select whole rows to format the row. - Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I and Ctrl+U, Clear Formatting, and Format Painter (Clipboard group). - Works the same in the task sheet and in Sheets tabs. The formatting is saved with the plan and printed. - Fixed the Options page, where the labels and boxes had swapped places. - Grouped into sections, each with an explanation. - New options: reopen the last plan at start; the view plans open in; manual or auto scheduling for new tasks; the week-end and month-close day for reports; default paper and orientation; choose the workspace folder directly. Fix (critical): in 0.3.2, after the first click the task sheet kept the same row selected. Clicking another cell only changed the column, so you could not select, edit or work on other tasks. Clicking now selects the cell you click. An automated test clicks cell after cell and edits one, so this can't come back unnoticed.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.2 — 2026-10-24
text: Changelog › 0.3.2 — 2026-10-24. Progress updating, a report builder and power tools, plus the fixes from your 0.3.1 screenshots. - The big Gantt Chart and Task buttons are now split buttons: click the top half to run, the arrow below for the menu. - Icons on every right-click menu item (column headings and tasks). - The Format tab sits under its own "Gantt Chart Tools" label, no longer squeezed together. - The Gantt Chart Style gallery is back on the Format tab (10 styles), with Bar Styles and Gridlines. - The File page sidebar is blue again (it had turned black). - The Sheets view no longer fails on plans without sheets. - Update Progress (Report › Update Progress or the sidebar): every task due in the period with planned vs actual; enter actual start and finish, % complete, remaining and a note; "Set all to planned %"; Close Period stores a snapshot. - Report Builder: build your own report from sections (key figures, S-curve, period bars, tables with chosen columns and filters, notes, behind-schedule list). Templates: Weekly management, Monthly client, Schedule health, Cost report. Print to PDF or save as HTML. - Relationship Diagram (View tab): the selected task with its predecessors and successors; driving links in bold; click a box to follow the chain.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.2 — 2026-10-24
text: Changelog › 0.3.2 — 2026-10-24. - Recurring tasks (Task › Recurring Task): every n days, weeks or months, for a number of occurrences. - Global Change (Task tab or a heading's menu): set one field to a value for every selected task or every task in the view, as one undo step. - Conditional formatting per column: colour cells by rules (font colour, fill and bold), e.g. negative float in red. - Portfolio shows plans in subfolders as an EPS tree. - Excel export keeps formulas: formula columns stay live formulas in the workbook, dates and durations are typed, sheet tabs and a Plan sheet are included. - Automated UI tests run on every build.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.1 — 2026-10-24
text: Changelog › 0.3.1 — 2026-10-24. A rebuilt foundation: a real spreadsheet grid, spreadsheet formulas, period reporting and a cleaner look. A task sheet that works like a spreadsheet - The task sheet is rebuilt. Header and rows share one scroll area, so columns always line up (fixes the misaligned headings). - Select cells as in a spreadsheet: click and drag, Shift+click, Ctrl+click for several ranges, click a column heading for the whole column or the ID column for whole rows, Ctrl+A for everything. - Delete clears the selected cells (Delete on whole rows, or Ctrl+−, deletes tasks). Type and press Ctrl+Enter to fill every selected cell. Ctrl+D fills down, and the fill handle at the corner of a selection drags values down. - Copy and paste blocks of cells to and from other spreadsheets. Pasting below the last task adds new tasks. - Formula bar above the sheet shows the active cell, and Sum, Average and Count of the selected numbers. - Double-click any column heading to rename it. Right-click a task and choose Rename Task, or press F2. - Filter buttons on every heading: sort, tick the values to show, custom filter. - The task name and ID columns stay in view when you scroll sideways. Formula columns (spreadsheet formulas, one per column)

heading: Changelog › 0.3.1 — 2026-10-24
text: Changelog › 0.3.1 — 2026-10-24. - New Formula Column (right-click a heading, the fx button or Format › Formula Column): name it, choose Number, Text, Date, Duration, Cost or Yes/No, and write a formula that refers to other columns by name, e.g. =[% Complete]-[Baseline % Complete] or =IF([Finish]>[Baseline Finish],"Late","On time"). It is calculated for every task. - Powered by the GridCraft engine: about 400 spreadsheet functions (IF, IFS, SUMIFS, XLOOKUP, WORKDAY, NETWORKDAYS, TEXT, ROUND, LET…). Formula columns can use each other. - New fields: Baseline % Complete (where the baseline says a task should be at the status date) and % Complete Variance. Sheets: spreadsheets inside your plan - Add sheet tabs for quantities, estimates or progress measurement, with spreadsheet formulas, number formats, copy and paste. - Sheets read your tasks through the Plan sheet, e.g. =SUMIF(Plan!I:I,100,Plan!M:M). Progress reporting by period - Reporting periods are yours to set per plan: the weekday a week ends on, the day a month closes, and how progress is weighted (duration, cost, hours or physical %). Set them in Project Setup or Project › Reporting Periods.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.1 — 2026-10-24
text: Changelog › 0.3.1 — 2026-10-24. - Weekly and monthly Progress report for any period: actual and planned progress with the change since last period, progress this period vs planned, variance, forecast finish, SPI and CPI; charts; progress by phase last period vs this period; completed, started, in progress, behind baseline, look-ahead and milestones. - Notes for each period: executive summary, progress, issues, actions, look-ahead and photos, saved inside the plan and printed with the report. S-curves and charts - Interactive charts in a clean, scientific style: hover anywhere to read every value, a status-date line, colour-blind-safe colours, and a PNG button on every chart. - S-curves page: project progress, progress per period, cost and hours S-curves, one S-curve per phase, and the data table; weekly or monthly, weighted as you choose. - The Dashboard now shows KPIs with the change since last period, the project S-curve, progress per period, progress by phase, cost and earned value, and a manpower histogram. - Reports saved as HTML keep their charts as pictures. Look and feel - A calmer design on the familiar ribbon layout: IBM Plex fonts, a calmer palette and square, clean controls. - Light, Dark and Auto themes (Auto follows Windows). Switch from the title bar or File › Options. - Right-click menu commands did nothing in 0.3.0; they work now.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.0 — 2026-10-24
text: Changelog › 0.3.0 — 2026-10-24. The biggest release so far: a familiar ribbon layout with advanced scheduling, rebuilt from the engine up. Everything planned for 0.2.1 to 0.5.2 is in this one release, including the network diagram. A new window (SolidJS) - The ribbon: Task, Resource, Report, Project, View and the Gantt Chart Tools Format tab, with dropdown and split buttons (Gantt Chart, Filter, Group by, Sort, Tables, Outline, Timescale, Baseline, Export). - Tell Me (Ctrl+K or Alt+Q) searches every command. Quick access toolbar with Save, Undo, Redo and Print. - A compact task sheet (20 px rows): drag columns to reorder, resize, double-click a heading for Field Settings, right-click a heading to insert, hide, sort, group or filter, and an "Add New Column" picker over about 450 fields. - Inline editing with choice lists, Tab/Enter navigation, type-to-edit, a blank row for new tasks, indicators for late and manual tasks, and a task mode column. - Status bar with filter state, task count, project figures, view shortcuts and a zoom slider. Fields, custom fields and formulas - About 450 task fields: general, schedule, progress, work and cost, 11 baselines (start, finish, duration, cost, work), variances, earned value, and custom Text1–30, Number1–20, Flag1–20, Date, Cost, Duration, Start, Finish and Outline Code fields.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.0 — 2026-10-24
text: Changelog › 0.3.0 — 2026-10-24. - Custom Fields dialog: rename (alias), lookup tables with restricted values and defaults, classic formulas (IIf, Switch, ProjDateDiff, DateAdd, 34 functions, [Field] references), summary rollups and graphical indicators. - Activity codes with values and colours: show as columns, group and filter by them. - Inspect shows every field of a task. - Gantt Chart and Tracking Gantt with critical path, slack, late bars, baseline 0–10, splits, deadlines, today and status lines, bar labels, and drag to move, resize, link or set progress. - A timeline across the top. - Network Diagram (boxes, critical links, progress crosses, milestones). - Calendar, Task Usage, Resource Usage (days, weeks, months, quarters; work or cost; overallocation in red), Resource Sheet, Resource Graph and Team Planner. - Tables: Entry, Schedule, Tracking, Cost, Work, Variance, Earned Value, Summary, Baseline and Activities, plus your own. - Filters (20 built-in plus your own, with and/or conditions, related summaries and highlight mode), groups (several levels, with rolled-up dates and costs) and sorts that keep the outline. Outline levels, expand and collapse, project summary task. - Details pane with tabs: General, Status, Resources, Predecessors, Successors (with driving links and float), Codes, Steps (weighted physical %), Notebook, Expenses, WPs & Docs, Custom Fields, Risks and Notes.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.0 — 2026-10-24
text: Changelog › 0.3.0 — 2026-10-24. - Activity types (task dependent, resource dependent, level of effort, start/finish milestone, WBS summary) and % complete types (duration, units, physical). - Schedule options: retained logic or progress override, critical by float or longest path, lag calendar, float paths, schedule from finish, open ends. - Elapsed durations (3ed), percentage lags (2SS+50%), task splits, priorities and leveling delay. - Resource leveling (standard, priority or ID order, within slack) and clearing it. - Task types: fixed duration, fixed units and fixed work, effort driven. Costs, progress and earned value - Cost rate tables A–E with dated rate changes, overtime rates, availability periods and resource calendars. - Fixed costs and expenses with start, prorated or end accrual. - 11 baselines, Update Project, Store Period Performance (snapshots) and trend reports. - Earned value per task and project: PV, EV, AC, SV, CV, SPI, CPI, BAC, EAC, VAC, TCPI. - Currencies: any ISO 4217 code, chosen per plan, with symbol and decimals. Reports and dashboards - Dashboard: complete, finish, cost, SPI, CPI, late and critical counts, cost S-curve (planned, forecast, earned, actual), progress and cost by phase, milestones and late tasks. - Report gallery: Project Overview, Weekly/Monthly Progress, Earned Value, Cost Overview with cash flow, Work Overview, Critical Tasks, Late & Slipping, Milestones, Upcoming Tasks and Trend.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.0 — 2026-10-24
text: Changelog › 0.3.0 — 2026-10-24. - Your logo and company name on every report. Print or save as PDF, save as HTML, save the Gantt chart as a PNG picture. - Check Schedule: the DCMA 14-point assessment plus further checks (long lags, SF links, soft constraints, manual tasks, summary links, out of sequence, missed deadlines), with your thresholds; click a check to filter its tasks. - Risk register with probability × impact scoring, a heat map and links to tasks. - Compare Projects: added, removed and changed tasks against another .dplan, XML or XER file. - Portfolio: every plan in a folder with its dates, progress, cost, SPI, CPI and late tasks. - Project Setup panel on the right (skippable): project details, Activity ID numbering (A1000, step 10), calendar, currency, WBS typed as an indented list, resources, and branding. - Change Working Time, Project Information (with statistics), Resource Information (costs, availability, notes) and Task Information dialogs. - New export formats: PMXML (.xml), MPX, iCalendar (.ics), HTML and JSON. Excel and CSV export the current table's columns. - JSON import. Plans from 0.2 open as before; a copy is kept as name.backup.dplan before they are upgraded. - Opt in to beta versions in Options. Under the hood

heading: Changelog › 0.3.0 — 2026-10-24
text: Changelog › 0.3.0 — 2026-10-24. - The engine computes every field, filter, group and sort, so the window stays fast with large plans (20,000 tasks schedule and display in about 0.15 seconds). - 18 engine tests, including earned value, formulas, leveling, splits, schedule from finish and the schedule checks. Coming in 0.3.1: report designer, Page Setup, bar and text style editors, recurring tasks, Relationship diagram, global change, an EPS tree, and custom fields and codes in XER and project XML files.

heading: Changelog › 0.2.0 — 2026-10-24
text: Changelog › 0.2.0 — 2026-10-24. A big step for the scheduling engine: real calendars, constraints, resources, progress tracking, baselines, file exchange, and a lot more control in the grid and the Gantt chart. Scheduling engine (to the minute) - Durations in minutes, hours, days, weeks or months (4h, 2.5d, 2w, 1mo). Lags take units too (3SS+4h). - Calendars with working hours per day (for example 08:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00), holidays and special working days. A plan can have several calendars, and each task can use its own. - All constraints: As Soon/Late As Possible, Start/Finish No Earlier/Later Than, Must Start/Finish On. Deadlines, with negative float when they are missed. - Manually scheduled tasks, inactive tasks, and links to and from summary tasks. - A status (data) date: completed work keeps its actual dates and remaining work moves after the status date. - Actual start and finish, remaining duration, and Mark on Track. Setting % complete fills in the actual dates. - Milestones sit at their predecessor's finish. Resources and costs - Resource Sheet: work, material and cost resources, groups, max units, standard rate, cost per use and material labels. - Assign resources in the Resource Names column (Engineer[50%], Concrete[12]) or in the details pane. New names are added to the sheet.

heading: Changelog › 0.2.0 — 2026-10-24
text: Changelog › 0.2.0 — 2026-10-24. - Work, cost and overallocation are calculated. The Workload view shows hours per week or per day, with over-capacity in red. Baselines and tracking - Set or clear a baseline for the whole project or for selected tasks. - Baseline bars in the Gantt chart, baseline columns, start and finish variance, and a baseline curve on the dashboard. - Show any of about 30 fields: right-click a header or use "Add New Column". You can also hide, move, resize and reset columns, and the layout is saved with the plan. - Cut, copy and paste tasks (Ctrl+X/C/V). Paste rows straight from a spreadsheet. - Fill down (Ctrl+D), move rows up and down (Alt+Shift+↑/↓), and Find, Find Next and Replace (Ctrl+F, F3, Ctrl+H). - Right-click menu for tasks. Indicators for manual scheduling, notes and constraints. Inactive tasks are struck through. - A timeline strip above the Gantt: add tasks with right-click › Add to Timeline, and click it to jump to a date. - Drag the progress line inside a bar to set % complete. Dragging one bar onto another creates a link. - Deadline markers, a status date line, manual task bars, and resource names next to the bars.

heading: Changelog › 0.2.0 — 2026-10-24

heading: Datum Plan: notes for Claude
text: Datum Plan: notes for Claude. Read docs/MEMORY.md first. It is the project's memory: architecture, decisions, roadmap, and a log of every session. At the end of every session that changes anything, update docs/MEMORY.md: - tick the roadmap - add a session-log entry - record any new decisions - refresh the architecture section if files moved - Rust and Tauri 2, small and efficient code, Windows first. - Ship in small numbered releases (0.1.0, 0.1.1, …). Every release appears in the in-app updater. - A light theme with blue accents (since 0.1.1), a ribbon layout with the task sheet and Gantt chart side by side, advanced scheduling features (activity codes, steps, longest path, earned value, risk), and an icon sidebar for the views. - Keep code compact and match the surrounding style. Engine logic belongs in crates/core (pure Rust, unit-tested), not in the UI. - The UI is SolidJS + Vite in ui/src/*.tsx (built to ui/dist). State lives in ui/src/store.ts; the engine computes all values, the window only shows them. Checks before pushing: - cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings - cargo test --workspace - npm run check:ui, then npm run build:ui and the UI tests (node tests_ui/run.cjs)

heading: Datum Plan: notes for Claude
text: Datum Plan: notes for Claude. - For changes to the grid, the Gantt or what the engine sends per edit: npm run perf:ui (the window with 100,000 rows) and npm run bench (engine times, edit cycle and memory at 100,000 tasks) - cargo deny check (licences, advisories, sources; CI runs it) Releasing: 1. Bump the version in src-tauri/Cargo.toml, crates/core/Cargo.toml and crates/cli/Cargo.toml. 2. Add a CHANGELOG section, and keep docs/site.json true to the release (about, steps, highlights, roadmap; no commercial product names). 3. If the release changes how something is used, update the guide (docs/guide/en.md and zh.md, both languages), then npm run build:ui && npm run guide (screenshots and PDFs; needs Playwright and cargo run -p datum-core --example dump guide > tests_ui/guide_fixture.json and ... dump tutorial > tests_ui/tutorial_fixture.json). The release attaches docs/guide/pdf/*.pdf. 4. Push the tag vX.Y.Z, or run release.yml with workflow_dispatch when tag pushes are blocked. The workflow creates the tag and publishes the installer.

heading: Datum Plan
text: Datum Plan. Plan, schedule, track and report your projects: one small, fast app for Windows.

heading: Datum Plan › Why Datum Plan
text: Datum Plan › Why Datum Plan. Datum Plan is a complete project scheduling and control tool, written from scratch with its own scheduling engine in Rust. It brings planning, scheduling, resources, costs, progress tracking, reporting and spreadsheets together in one window. You don't need several tools and exports. - Small and fast. About 3.6 MB to install. It opens in a moment and stays smooth with large plans. - Everything included. Network logic, resource levelling, earned value, S-curves, dashboards, printing and spreadsheet formulas are all built in. - Easy to learn. A ribbon, a sheet that works like a spreadsheet, plain-language help, a glossary of planning terms, and templates with real teams and man-hours. - Private. Plans are .dplan files on your own computer. The only network call is the update check. - Dates you can trust. Every release is checked against hand-worked scheduling cases, plan files that carry their own dates, and thousands of random plans and damaged files. - Always improving. Small releases, installed with one click from inside the app.

heading: Datum Plan › Features › Plan
text: Datum Plan › Features › Plan. - A task sheet that works like a spreadsheet: - drag-select ranges and select whole rows and columns; - copy and paste with other spreadsheets, with Paste Special (values, formats, transpose); - a fill handle that continues series; - Sum, Average and Count of the selection; - fonts, colours, fill and alignment. - Outline (WBS) with summaries, milestones, recurring tasks, manual or automatic scheduling, inactive tasks and splits. - Links of every type (Finish-to-Start, Start-to-Start, Finish-to-Finish, Start-to-Finish) with lags and leads in days, hours or percent. - About 450 fields; rename any column, and hide, unhide, delete or reorder columns with the Columns dialog. - Formula columns in spreadsheet syntax that refer to other columns, e.g. =[% Complete]-[Baseline % Complete] or =IF([Finish]>[Baseline Finish],"Late","On time"), with about 400 spreadsheet functions. - Sheets: spreadsheet tabs inside the plan for your own reports, quantities, estimates and vendor lists. Click cells into a formula, 490 functions suggested as you type, AutoSum, fill and paste that move references, insert and delete rows and columns. They read the plan live by name (Tasks[Finish], Resources[Country], ProjectFinish, SPI), Plan Data puts a live list of milestones or late tasks in one click, and countries show their flags.

heading: Datum Plan › Features › Plan
text: Datum Plan › Features › Plan. - Your own dashboards: several per plan, made of tiles you lay out: numbers and progress rings from formulas (green or red by a rule), the plan's charts and lists, charts and tables from sheets, and country flags. Templates for a client dashboard, weekly progress and vendors. - Project Setup walks you through a new plan: details, Activity IDs, calendar, currency, WBS, team and branding. Templates for engineering, EPC, construction, software and research come with people, rates, assignments and costs.

heading: Datum Plan › Features › Schedule
text: Datum Plan › Features › Schedule. - A critical path engine that works to the minute, with working calendars, holidays, task and resource calendars, all constraint types, deadlines and elapsed durations. - Resource calendars that drive task dates (optional): each person's own working week and leave decide when their work is done; a task finishes when the last person on it does. - Projects made of plans: a master plan and its subplans, in order and in a hierarchy, with their tabs grouped in one colour and the whole project in the master's Gantt (subplans as rows you can expand); New Subplan, Open All Subplans and Close Project. - Several plans in tabs, with links between them: a main schedule and its subplans in their own files; a task can wait for a task in another plan, Linked Plans shows what has moved, and Update Links brings every open plan up to date. File › Linked plans (example) opens a four-plan example. - Longest path, float paths, free and total float, retained logic or progress override, scheduling from the finish. - Resource levelling (all tasks or a selection), with a preview of which tasks move and the new finish before anything changes, and clearing it again.

heading: Datum Plan › Features › Schedule
text: Datum Plan › Features › Schedule. - Schedule risk analysis: the plan runs a thousand times with uncertain durations and the risks from the register, to show the chance of finishing by each date (P50, P80, P90), the likely cost, how often each task is critical, and which tasks drive the finish. - A schedule health check with drill-down to the tasks behind each finding.

heading: Datum Plan › Features › Resources and cost
text: Datum Plan › Features › Resources and cost. - Work, material and cost resources, with groups, rates over time, overtime, cost per use, availability, and 8-hour days or any calendar you set. - Man-hours and costs per task, resource and period; resource usage, histograms and overallocation warnings, per person or per trade (in hours or people); Team Planner. - Fixed costs, expenses, any currency, and cash flow.

heading: Datum Plan › Features › Track progress
text: Datum Plan › Features › Track progress. - Status date, % complete, actual dates, remaining duration, Mark on Track, Update Progress for a whole period, and Close Period with snapshots. - 11 baselines and the Tracking Gantt: baseline bars under the current bars, the done part solid, and % labels. - Earned value (SPI, CPI, EAC, TCPI) and earned schedule (SPI(t) and the finish at the current pace), period-by-period comparison, S-curves (planned, actual and forecast) whose actual line follows the progress stored at each period close, and milestone tracking. - Progress measured by rules of credit (weighted steps such as pulled, terminated, tested) or by installed quantities (200 m of cable, 50 m pulled). - A look-ahead of the next 2 to 6 weeks with a constraint log (materials, drawings, permits, access, people), showing which tasks are ready to start. - Manpower by trade: people planned, work done and forecast per week or month.

heading: Datum Plan › Features › Report, print and share
text: Datum Plan › Features › Report, print and share. - Dashboard with key figures and charts, Progress reports for any week or month with notes and photos, S-curves, and a Report Builder with templates (weekly management, monthly client, schedule health, cost). - Print to paper or PDF from every view: paper size, orientation, scaling or fit to pages, margins, date ranges, page ranges, headers and footers with your logo and your client's, page numbers and a legend. - Excel (.xlsx) export keeps formulas and formatting. Also exports to CSV, HTML, iCalendar and JSON, and imports and exports the common project exchange files (XML, XER, PMXML, MPX). Every import ends with a report of anything changed or left out, and whether every task gets the same dates as in the file.

heading: Datum Plan › Features › Views
text: Datum Plan › Features › Views. Gantt Chart · Tracking Gantt · Schedule Risk · Look-ahead · Manpower · Network Diagram (whiteboard canvas, legend, WBS bands, mini-map, path highlight) · Calendar · Timeline with a zoom box · Task Usage · Resource Sheet · Resource Usage · Resource Graph · Team Planner · Relationship Diagram · Sheets · Dashboard · Progress · S-Curves · Checks · Risks · Portfolio.

heading: Datum Plan › Features › Help when you need it
text: Datum Plan › Features › Help when you need it. Tell Me (Ctrl+K) finds any command. Help › Getting Started and a searchable Glossary explain every term. Light, dark or automatic theme.

heading: Datum Plan › Install
text: Datum Plan › Install. 1. Download DatumPlan-x.y.z-setup.exe from Releases. 2. Run it. It installs for your user account, with no administrator rights needed. The installer is not code-signed yet, so on the first install Windows may show *"Windows protected your PC"*. Click More info › Run anyway. 3. Later versions install from inside the app: File › Home › Update now, or click the amber Update available badge. Every download is checked against its SHA-256 checksum.

heading: Datum Plan › The guide
text: Datum Plan › The guide. The Datum Plan Guide walks through everything step by step, with pictures: English (PDF) · 中文 (PDF). In the app: Help › Guide.

heading: Datum Plan › Your first plan in five minutes
text: Datum Plan › Your first plan in five minutes. 1. File › New and pick a template (or Blank Project), then follow Setup. 2. Type task names, durations (5d, 2w, 0 for a milestone) and predecessors (3, 4SS+2d). 3. Indent tasks to build the outline; assign people in the Resource Names column (Design Engineer[50%]). 4. Progress › Set Baseline, then record progress as work happens and open the Tracking Gantt. 5. Report › Dashboard or File › Print to share it.

heading: Datum Plan › Roadmap
text: Datum Plan › Roadmap. See the changelog for every release and the roadmap for what is next: schedule quality and what-if scenarios, a combined view of linked plans, a shared resource pool across plans, portfolio dashboards, signed installers, and working together on shared plans. Datum Plan is part of Datum; see its page: docs/FAMILY.md describes the shared design.

heading: Datum Plan › Command line and AI assistants
text: Datum Plan › Command line and AI assistants. datum-cli (on the Releases page) works with plans without the window: datum-cli mcp is a Model Context Protocol server: an AI assistant can open or start a plan, read the schedule, change it with the same named operations the window uses, run the risk analysis and save it. Nothing is written unless it is asked to save.

heading: Datum Plan › Build from source
text: Datum Plan › Build from source. You need Rust (stable) and Node.js 20+. On Linux, also install libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libgtk-3-dev librsvg2-dev. The engine (scheduling, resources, costs, reports, file formats) is in crates/core; the desktop shell in src-tauri; the window in ui/src. Architecture and decisions are in docs/MEMORY.md.

heading: Datum Plan: brainstorm and plan
text: Datum Plan: brainstorm and plan. Update: decisions made after this brainstorm (a Rust engine instead of porting the earlier web planner's engine, a custom updater, the release plan) are in MEMORY.md. This file stays as the original feature map. Goal: a desktop project scheduler that covers everyday desktop planning and large enterprise schedules in one app. You install it once from a GitHub Release .exe, and every later version installs itself from an Update button on the Home screen. This document is for discussion. Nothing here is fixed until we agree on it.

heading: Datum Plan: brainstorm and plan › 1. Lessons from what you have already built
text: Datum Plan: brainstorm and plan › 1. Lessons from what you have already built. Repo ; What we reuse ; What we change ; Earlier web planner (v0.8) ; About 7,000 lines of tested TypeScript scheduling engine: calendars, FS/SS/FF/SF links with lags, constraints, critical path and float, task types, effort-driven work, leveling, baselines, earned value, timephased work, formulas, plus project XML, XER, MPX, XLSX and CSV import/export. The engine has no UI code, so it can move over as it is. ; The web planner used a menu bar and plain-language names. Datum Plan uses a ribbon, standard scheduling terms, and a multi-project database. ; CentriForge (Compressor Suite) ; The launcher layout (version, *What's new*, update panel), the release workflow that builds on windows-latest from a v* tag, and release notes taken from CHANGELOG.md. ; CentriForge bundles Python with PyInstaller and Inno Setup, and the update downloads the whole installer. Tauri has a built-in signed updater, and the installer is about 10 MB instead of about 150 MB. ;

heading: Datum Plan: brainstorm and plan › 2. Architecture
text: Datum Plan: brainstorm and plan › 2. Architecture. "Tauri6" is probably Tauri 2, which is the current major version. It uses a Rust backend and the system WebView2 on Windows for the frontend. Main decisions (proposed): 1. Where the engine runs. Port the earlier web planner's TypeScript engine and run it in a Web Worker so the UI stays responsive. Its tests come with it. We would move the CPM pass to Rust only if profiling shows it is needed, for example above 50,000 activities. Those tests would then check that the Rust engine gives the same results. This is the fastest route to a working 0.1 without giving up performance later. 2. A multi-project database plus single-project files. Use a local SQLite database that holds many projects (EPS tree, shared resource pool, global calendars and codes). Also add File › Save As .dpln: a single-project SQLite file you can email. 3. Strict TypeScript everywhere: strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, ESLint, Vitest. Rust uses clippy -D warnings. CI runs all of these on every push. 4. Rendering. The Gantt and grids use canvas and virtualisation, not DOM nodes for each row. The web planner's DOM rows slow down at about 5,000 tasks, and large projects regularly reach 20,000 activities.

heading: Datum Plan: brainstorm and plan › 2. Architecture › The update flow (what you asked for)
text: Datum Plan: brainstorm and plan › 2. Architecture › The update flow (what you asked for). - Home screen shows: logo, current version, Check for updates, recent projects and a *What's new* card. - Clicking *Check for updates* makes the app read latest.json from the newest GitHub Release. If a newer version exists, a dialog shows the version, date, size and changelog, with Update now and Later buttons. - Update now downloads, verifies the signature, installs silently and restarts. There is no uninstalling or reinstalling, and your projects and settings stay where they are. - It can also check quietly on startup, at most once a day, and show a badge on the Home tab. - Release pipeline: bump the version, then git tag v0.2.0 && git push --tags. GitHub Actions builds the NSIS .exe, signs the update bundle, writes latest.json, and publishes the release with notes from CHANGELOG.md. - One-time setup on your side: generate an updater signing key. I can give you the exact commands. Store it as two GitHub secrets: TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY and its password. - Windows SmartScreen: without a paid code-signing certificate, Windows shows *"Windows protected your PC"* on the first install. Click *More info › Run anyway*. Updates after that do not show the warning. We can add a certificate later (Azure Trusted Signing costs about $10 a month).

heading: Datum Plan: brainstorm and plan › 4. UI concept
text: Datum Plan: brainstorm and plan › 4. UI concept. Dark-blue theme. A ribbon over a grid-and-Gantt view, with detail tabs below: - File page (full window): New, Open, Save As, Import/Export, Print, Options, About and Updates. - Home tab as the start screen: recent projects, templates, *What's new*, Check for updates. - Palette: navy #0B2A5B, primary #1F4E9A, accent sky #8FB8F2, milestone/attention amber #F2B233, critical red #E04F4F. There will be a light theme too. - Logo (draft above): a calendar with binding rings, Gantt bars linked by arrows, and an amber milestone diamond. Feedback welcome. Notes on your own workflow would help a lot: which views you use most (Gantt, task details, options, activity lists with detail tabs, saved layouts) and what you need from each. heading: Datum Plan: project memory › 1. Architecture
text: Datum Plan: project memory › 1. Architecture. - The UI never calculates dates, values or filters. Every edit is an Op; the core applies it to a copy, normalises, schedules and keeps it only if valid. - After an edit apply returns Out (project settings without tasks + Summary). The window then calls query(Query) for the rows it shows; Calc (fields.rs) evaluates any field for any row. - Window-only settings (saved filters, extra tables) live in Project.ui; the Entry table's columns in Project.columns.

heading: Datum Plan: project memory › 1. Architecture › Time model (since 0.2)
text: Datum Plan: project memory › 1. Architecture › Time model (since 0.2). - Instants are minutes since 1970-01-01 00:00 local time. Durations and lags are working minutes. - Project.day_min (default 480) converts days. A week is 5 days and a month is 20 days. - Task.unit remembers how the duration was typed (h, d, w, mo) so it is shown the same way. - Calendars: week: [Vec ; 7] (Monday first) plus exceptions (date ranges; empty hours mean not working). - The project calendar is Project.calendar. Each task can use its own Task.cal. - Forward pass: ES = max(link requirements, constraints, data date), snapped to working time. Milestones may sit at the end of a shift. - Backward pass: works on late dates, which SNLT, FNLT, MSO, MFO and deadlines all limit. - Lags count on the successor's calendar. - Total float = working time between EF and LF. - A link to or from a summary applies to every leaf task under it. - normalize() drops links between a task and its own ancestors. - Progress: an actual finish fixes the task. An actual start with % < 100 puts the remaining work after the status date (status date + 1 day, 00:00). Unstarted tasks cannot start before the status date. Setting % fills in actual dates; 0% clears them.

heading: Datum Plan: project memory › 1. Architecture › How we work (the workflow, since session 1)
text: Datum Plan: project memory › 1. Architecture › How we work (the workflow, since session 1). 1. The user reviews the last release in the app and sends screenshots with bugs and wishes. 2. Diagnose first. Reproduce the problem in the test harness or the real app before changing code. Small fixes go straight to a release. 3. Bigger asks get a plan file (docs/PLAN-x.y.z.md): feedback, diagnosis, proposal by area, size, and questions. The plan is logged in this file and pushed. Build only after the user answers. 4. Build in small steps, engine first (crates/core, with a unit test), then the UI. Keep code compact and in the surrounding style. 5. Check in the real app under Xvfb (scratchpad/app.sh restarts Xvfb and the app, opens the Engineering template and skips Setup), with screenshots of each change. Fix what looks wrong. 6. Add a UI test for every reported bug and new feature (tests_ui/run.cjs, Playwright against ui/dist with the dump fixture). Make sure it fails on the old code where possible. 7. Run the checks: clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, npm run check:ui, and the UI tests after npm run build:ui + cargo run -p datum-core --example dump > tests_ui/fixture.json. 8. Release: bump both Cargo.toml files, write the CHANGELOG (it becomes the in-app "What's new"), update this file (version, roadmap, files, decisions, session log, limits), commit, push, run release.yml (workflow_dispatch), then watch CI + Release

Plan: one shared grid component for both (0.4.x), keeping the scheduler's task rows. See decision log.

heading: Datum Plan: project memory › 4. Session log › 2026-10-29: Session 14 (0.4.2, hardening, command line, print)
text: Datum Plan: project memory › 4. Session log › 2026-10-29: Session 14 (0.4.2, hardening, command line, print). - User: build 0.4.2 and 0.4.3 together overnight, with a complete security, robustness and hardening pass of the whole app. - Audit and fixes. Probing hostile values found panics in calendar arithmetic (huge durations, lags, splits, delays) and a divide-by-zero (zero-length day); fixed with clamping in normalize, a calendar horizon and saturating dates. A battery (hardening::exercise) now runs every engine function on hostile plans, extreme edits and the random plans; it found the S-curve freezing on century-long plans (fast whole-week between, weekly fallback). Also: atomic saves, 300 MB read limit, unwind + guard() + crash.log (release builds aborted on any panic), updater requires checksums (it installed unverified without SHA256SUMS.txt), stricter CSP (and blob: images: progress-report photos were blocked), CSV formula injection, ics line breaks, allowed_url, npm audit in CI. Hostile sheet formulas were already safe (#CIRC!, #NUM!). - Built ops.rs (catalogue), crates/cli (datum-cli + MCP server, tests drive a whole assistant session), money to the cent, the release ships datum-cli-X.Y.Z.exe. Print: the three views printed the Dashboard (fixed); risk charts full width on paper; last risk run in project.ui.risk. Found on the way: "-0 hrs" on an empty plan (float sum of nothing is -0).

heading: Datum Plan: project memory › 5. Known limits and next steps › Pending and next (written at the end of 0.3.8)
text: Datum Plan: project memory › 5. Known limits and next steps › Pending and next (written at the end of 0.3.8). Bugs found while taking the 0.3.8 README screenshots (fix first, 0.3.10): 1. ✅ (0.3.10) Print, "Fit timescale to 1 page wide": when the table takes most of the page (the templates now have Man-hours and Cost columns), a second near-empty page appears. Cause: the shrink in print.tsx layout() aims at 35 % of the *old* width for the chart, but the chart minimum is 30 % of the *new* width. Use W = TW / (fit − 0.35) when TW > (fit − 0.35) × W. 2. ✅ (0.3.10) The Network Diagram's completed-task cross is too heavy and runs over the text: lighten it (opacity) or use a corner tick. 3. ✅ (0.3.11) The Dashboard shows "Actual progress 0 %" when no status date is set even though tasks are done: fall back to today (or the latest actual date) and say so. 4. ✅ (0.3.11, blur after the pick; still to confirm on Windows) On Linux the date picker stays open after a pick: check on Windows and close it after choosing. Not yet checked on a real Windows PC or against real files: - Print to PDF in WebView2 for every view (flowing report pages, page numbers from @page margin boxes).
