heading: Datum Plan 0.3.1+: spreadsheet core, CentriForge design, period reporting › 1. What went wrong in 0.3.0 (honest diagnosis)
text: Datum Plan 0.3.1+: spreadsheet core, CentriForge design, period reporting › 1. What went wrong in 0.3.0 (honest diagnosis). Symptom the user saw ; Root cause ; Cells misaligned between header and rows ; Header and rows are separate DOM flex rows with their own borders, padding and scrollbars. Widths drift by a pixel or two, and more when the vertical scrollbar appears. ; Cannot select many cells, drag a range, delete or fill a block ; The grid has only a row selection and one "current cell". There is no range model. ; No obvious place for a formula (e.g. % complete − baseline %) ; Formulas exist only inside Custom Fields → Formula, with classic formula syntax. There is no formula bar and no way to type = into a cell. ; Reports feel thin ; Reports are lists of tables. They have no period model (last week vs this week), no narrative or notes, and the charts are weak. ; UI "not up to the mark" ; It mixes a ribbon, a sidebar and a bottom pane, all with different styles. It is not the clean, consistent CentriForge look. ; Bugs ; It was tested by hand only. There are no automated UI tests in CI. ; Lesson: we built many features on a weak base. 0.3.1 rebuilds the base: the grid, the design and the reporting model. Then features go on top.

heading: Datum Plan 0.3.1+: spreadsheet core, CentriForge design, period reporting › 2. Direction › A. A real spreadsheet core (using Gridcraft)
text: Datum Plan 0.3.1+: spreadsheet core, CentriForge design, period reporting › 2. Direction › A. A real spreadsheet core (using Gridcraft). Gridcraft (storytold/gridcraft, MIT or Apache-2.0, pure Rust) is a complete spreadsheet engine split into small crates with few dependencies: Gridcraft crate ; Size ; What we use it for ; formula + functions + calc + core + numfmt ; ~30k lines ; Spreadsheet formulas (about 400 functions: IF, SUMIFS, XLOOKUP, NETWORKDAYS, WORKDAY, dates, statistics, LET/LAMBDA), dependency recalc, spreadsheet number formats ; model ; 3.6k ; A sheet model for free spreadsheet tabs ; xlsx ; 25k ; Real Excel (.xlsx) export and import with formulas, formats and outline (replaces our minimal xlsx writer) ; pdf, chart ; 1.3k / 4.4k ; True PDF output for reports and server-side charts (later) ; We add these as Cargo dependencies pinned to a commit (no copy-paste fork), with attribution in NOTICE. Our scheduling engine stays our own: Gridcraft does not schedule.

heading: Datum Plan 0.3.1+: spreadsheet core, CentriForge design, period reporting › 2. Direction › A. A real spreadsheet core (using Gridcraft)
text: Datum Plan 0.3.1+: spreadsheet core, CentriForge design, period reporting › 2. Direction › A. A real spreadsheet core (using Gridcraft). How the plan uses the spreadsheet engine: 1. Formula columns, spreadsheet style. Type = in any custom column, e.g. =[% Complete]-[Baseline % Complete] or =IF([Finish]>[Baseline Finish],"Late","OK"). [Field] names map to task fields. All Gridcraft functions work. The classic formula syntax ([Field], IIf) still loads, translated on open. 2. A formula bar above the grid shows and edits the current cell's value or formula. 3. Sheet tabs inside the plan (workbook style): free spreadsheets for quantities, estimates, rate build-ups and progress measurement. Cells can reference plan data (=TASK("A1040","Finish")) and tasks can pull from sheets. 4. Excel (.xlsx) export with live formulas (variance columns stay formulas in the file).

heading: Datum Plan 0.3.1+: spreadsheet core, CentriForge design, period reporting › 2. Direction › B. A new grid, built like a spreadsheet
text: Datum Plan 0.3.1+: spreadsheet core, CentriForge design, period reporting › 2. Direction › B. A new grid, built like a spreadsheet. One component used everywhere: the task sheet, resource sheet, usage, sheets and report tables. - Canvas-rendered body and headers from the same column metrics, so they always line up. Frozen ID and name columns. 100k rows smooth. - Range selection: click-drag, Shift+click, Shift+arrows, Ctrl+click for several ranges, row and column headers to select whole rows or columns, Ctrl+A. - Range operations as one undo step: Delete clears, typing + Ctrl+Enter fills the selection, fill handle drag (series for dates and IDs), Ctrl+D and Ctrl+R, copy and paste TSV ranges to and from spreadsheets, paste special (values only). - Spreadsheet keys: F2, Enter or Tab moves, Esc cancels, Ctrl+arrows jump, Home/End, PageUp/Down, Ctrl+Z/Y. - Status-bar aggregates for a selection (Sum, Average, Count). - Column header filter buttons (AutoFilter), sort, resize, drag-reorder, freeze. - Conditional formatting: data bars and colour rules (e.g. negative float in red). - Engine: new ops SetRange, FillRange, ClearRange, PasteRange, all applied as one batch.

heading: Datum Plan 0.3.1+: spreadsheet core, CentriForge design, period reporting › 2. Direction › C. CentriForge design system (one family of apps)
text: Datum Plan 0.3.1+: spreadsheet core, CentriForge design, period reporting › 2. Direction › C. CentriForge design system (one family of apps). Use the same look as Compressor Engineering Suite, so Datum Plan is clearly from the same developer: - Tokens: --bg #f2f3ef, --panel #f8f8f5, --ink #0c1a2b, --accent #0b5cad, --accent-2 #22b8e6, pass/fail/attention colours, a dark theme (Theme · Auto/Light/Dark). - Type: IBM Plex Sans for text, IBM Plex Mono for uppercase spaced labels, tabs, buttons, numbers and IDs. Square corners and 1 px lines, no shadows. - Shell: top bar DATUM PLAN ; FILE ▾ ; LAUNCHER ; WORKSPACE ; product strap ; THEME. - Launcher (home): hero with version, updates and news; the current project's KPIs; module tiles in workflow order, each with "How to use", a status pill and OPEN. - Workspace: a left nav grouped by stage, a sticky header with crumb, plan title, revision and a primary action (e.g. RECALCULATE / UPDATE PROGRESS).

heading: Datum Plan 0.3.1+: spreadsheet core, CentriForge design, period reporting › 2. Direction › C. CentriForge design system (one family of apps)
text: Datum Plan 0.3.1+: spreadsheet core, CentriForge design, period reporting › 2. Direction › C. CentriForge design system (one family of apps). - Modules (left nav), in workflow order: 1. INPUTS: Project setup · Calendars · Codes & custom fields 2. PLAN: WBS & tasks (sheet + Gantt) · Network · Calendar view 3. RESOURCES: Resource sheet · Usage & histogram · Team planner · Leveling 4. heading: Datum Plan 0.3.1+: spreadsheet core, CentriForge design, period reporting › 2. Direction › D. Progress periods and reporting (what makes Datum Plan stand out)
text: Datum Plan 0.3.1+: spreadsheet core, CentriForge design, period reporting › 2. Direction › D. Progress periods and reporting (what makes Datum Plan stand out). - Reporting periods are first-class. A weekly or monthly calendar of cut-off dates. Update progress walks you through the period: tasks due, started, finished and in progress, each with actual dates, %, remaining and a comment. Closing the period stores a snapshot automatically. - Period comparison everywhere: previous period, this period and variance for planned %, actual %, earned, cost, finish date, float and milestones. - Report structure (the user's order): 1. Dashboard (KPIs with arrows vs last period) → 2. Charts (S-curve planned/actual/forecast cumulative %, period progress bars, manpower histogram, cost and EV curves, milestone trend chart, float erosion) → 3. Tables (completed this period, started, slipped, critical changes, 2–4-week look-ahead, progress by WBS this vs last period) → 4. Notes (editable narrative sections: summary, issues, risks, actions, photos), saved per period with the plan. - Report builder: pick sections, reorder, brand them (logo, colours), save as templates (Weekly, Monthly, Client, Management). - Output: real PDF (Gridcraft pdf or the print engine), Excel (.xlsx) with formulas, HTML.

heading: Datum Plan 0.3.1+: spreadsheet core, CentriForge design, period reporting › 2. Direction › E. Python: recommendation
text: Datum Plan 0.3.1+: spreadsheet core, CentriForge design, period reporting › 2. Direction › E. Python: recommendation. Python libraries (pandas, matplotlib, reportlab, numpy) are excellent, but bundling Python in the app means: - about 30–60 MB more per install and per update, and a slower start (we are at 2.6 MB today); - a second runtime and language to package, sign and debug on Windows. Everything we need is already available in Rust or in the browser: - formulas and statistics: Gridcraft; - Monte Carlo schedule risk: a few hundred lines of Rust, faster than numpy for this; - charts: SVG in the window; - PDF: Gridcraft pdf, or WebView print. Recommendation: no Python in 0.3.x. Keep the door open for an optional "Python scripts" add-on (0.5+): the user's own Python runs against an exported plan for custom analytics. That only makes sense if you want scripting.

heading: Datum Plan 0.3.1+: spreadsheet core, CentriForge design, period reporting › 6. Risks
text: Datum Plan 0.3.1+: spreadsheet core, CentriForge design, period reporting › 6. Risks. - Gridcraft is young and moves fast (v0.11). heading: Datum Plan 0.3.1+: spreadsheet core, CentriForge design, period reporting › 7. Questions for the user
text: Datum Plan 0.3.1+: spreadsheet core, CentriForge design, period reporting › 7. Questions for the user. 1. Ribbon: replace the ribbon with the CentriForge command bar (cleaner, matches the suite), keep the ribbon, or offer both (ribbon off by default)? 2. Theme: add a dark theme with Auto/Light/Dark like CentriForge? 3. Formula syntax: spreadsheet functions with field names in brackets (=[% Complete]-[Baseline % Complete]), plus A1 references in sheet tabs. OK? 4. Sheet tabs inside a plan (free spreadsheets next to the schedule): wanted in 0.3.3, or not needed? 5. Python: agree with "no Python in 0.3.x, optional scripting add-on later"? Or do you have a specific Python library or feature in mind? 6. Reporting periods: does the week end on Friday or Sunday? Monthly cut-off on the last day of the month or a fixed date (e.g. the 25th)? 7. Progress measure for S-curves: duration-weighted, cost-weighted, hours-weighted or physical %, and selectable per plan? 8. Photos and attachments in notes: store them inside the .dplan file (larger files) or next to it in a folder? 9. Steps: release 0.3.1 → 0.3.2 → 0.3.3 as above (recommended), or one big release? 10. Your bug and missing-feature write-up and screenshots: please send them. They become the 0.3.1 acceptance list.

heading: Datum Plan 0.3.5: cleaner ribbon, Setup in the sidebar, column control, full printing › 2. Diagnosis
text: Datum Plan 0.3.5: cleaner ribbon, Setup in the sidebar, column control, full printing › 2. Diagnosis. - Print defaulted to "first 3 columns" and skipped the Task Mode column, so only Name, Duration and Start printed. The Start column is drawn under the chart's first weeks (the shading and lines overlap its text). - "Hide Column" removes the column from the table and keeps no record, so it is really a delete with no undo path in the menu. There is no list of columns to bring back. - The Task tab has 9 groups (View, Clipboard, Font, Alignment, Schedule, Tasks, Insert, Properties, Editing). At 1920 px it overflows. Nothing collapses, so the ribbon scrolls sideways. - Project Setup is a fixed 380 px panel over the right side of the work area.

text: Datum Plan 0.3.5: cleaner ribbon, Setup in the sidebar, column control, full printing › 3. Proposed changes › A. Ribbon: more tabs, no sideways scrolling. heading: Datum Plan 0.3.5: cleaner ribbon, Setup in the sidebar, column control, full printing › 3. Proposed changes › B. Project Setup in the left sidebar

heading: Datum Plan 0.3.5: cleaner ribbon, Setup in the sidebar, column control, full printing › 3. Proposed changes › C. Columns: delete, hide, unhide, choose
text: Datum Plan 0.3.5: cleaner ribbon, Setup in the sidebar, column control, full printing › 3. Proposed changes › C. Columns: delete, hide, unhide, choose. Heading right-click menu: - Delete Column: takes the column out of this table, with undo. heading: Datum Plan 0.3.5: cleaner ribbon, Setup in the sidebar, column control, full printing › 3. Proposed changes › D. Printing: complete, then better
text: Datum Plan 0.3.5: cleaner ribbon, Setup in the sidebar, column control, full printing › 3. Proposed changes › D. text: Datum Plan 0.3: brainstorm and plan › 1. Honest audit of 0.2.0. Area ; What is wrong today ; Look ; It does not feel like a dense, professional scheduler. heading: Datum Plan 0.3: brainstorm and plan › 2. Design principles for 0.3
text: Datum Plan 0.3: brainstorm and plan › 2. Design principles for 0.3. 1. A familiar ribbon layout first, advanced scheduling underneath. Clear ribbon tabs, dialogs and right-click menus, so schedulers find everything where they expect it. 2. One click to information. - Double-click a task → Task Information (tabbed). - Double-click a resource → Resource Information. - Double-click a column header → Field Settings. - Double-click a bar → Format Bar. - Double-click a link → Task Dependency. 3. Everything is a view. View = table (columns) + filter + group + sort + screen (Gantt, Usage, Network…). All views are saved in the plan, with built-ins kept in a global template. 4. Every ribbon button works. Dropdowns and split buttons where useful, and a contextual Format tab for the active view. 5. Engine in Rust. Fields, formulas, filters, timephased data, leveling, earned value and network layout are all core code with tests. The UI only draws. 6. Fast with 10,000+ tasks. The core sends only the visible columns and rows.

heading: Datum Plan 0.3: brainstorm and plan › 3. Feature catalogue for 0.3 › B. Grid, fields and custom fields
text: Datum Plan 0.3: brainstorm and plan › 3. Feature catalogue for 0.3 › B. Grid, fields and custom fields. - Field catalogue, about 450 fields grouped by kind: - Task: dates, durations, work, cost, progress, baselines 0–10, earned value, constraints, IDs and codes, flags, resources, notes, links… - Resource fields and assignment fields. - Each field has a type: text, number, duration, date, cost, flag, percentage or list. - Custom fields: Text1–30, Number1–20, Flag1–20, Date1–10, Cost1–10, Duration1–10, Start1–10, Finish1–10, Outline Code1–10, for tasks and resources. The Custom Fields dialog (as in your screenshot) has: - Lookup table with default value and "restrict to list" - Formula with a field picker and functions: - arithmetic and comparison operators - IIf, Switch, Choose, ProjDateDiff, ProjDateAdd, DateDiff, Now, Abs, Round, Len, Left, Mid, InStr, IsNull, Format - Rollup for summaries (Max, Min, Sum, Average, Count, or use the formula) - Graphical indicators (rules → icons/colours, separately for tasks, summaries and the project summary) - Column header menu: Cut, Copy, Paste, Paste Special, Wrap Text, Insert Column, Hide Column, Font, Text Styles, Field Settings (title, alignment, width, header wrap), Custom Fields, Data Type. - Column dropdown arrows (AutoFilter): sort A→Z / Z→A, group by this field, filter by values, date ranges and custom conditions. - Tables (saved column sets): Entry, Cost, Schedule, Tracking, Variance, Work, Summary, Baseline, Earned Value, Constraint Dates, Delay, plus your own.

text: Datum Plan 0.3: brainstorm and plan › 3. Feature catalogue for 0.3 › C. Information dialogs (one click to everything). - Task Information: General · Predecessors (editable grid) · Resources (editable grid) · Advanced (constraint, deadline, task type, effort-driven, calendar, WBS code, earned value method, mark as milestone) · Notes · Custom Fields. heading: Datum Plan 0.3: brainstorm and plan › 3. Feature catalogue for 0.3 › D. Scheduling engine
text: Datum Plan 0.3: brainstorm and plan › 3. Feature catalogue for 0.3 › D. Scheduling engine. - Task types: Fixed Units, Fixed Work and Fixed Duration, with effort-driven scheduling (duration × units = work). - Activity types: - Activity types: task-dependent, resource-dependent, level of effort, WBS summary, start milestone, finish milestone - Duration types - % complete types: physical, duration, units - Steps with weights - Elapsed durations (3ed), % lags (2FS+50%), recurring tasks, split tasks (drag to split), and schedule from the finish date. - Resource calendars, availability over time, and rate tables A–E over time. Overtime work and cost. - Resource leveling: - Leveling Options dialog: automatic/manual, look-for-overallocation basis, order (ID / Standard / Priority), level only within available slack, allow splitting, priority 0–1000 - Level Selection / Resource / All, Clear Leveling, Next Overallocation - Leveling Gantt showing the delay - Advanced scheduling options: - retained logic vs progress override - "critical = total float ≤ x" or the longest path - free/total float computed from finish or start - open-ended tasks warning - Longest path and multiple float paths: number of paths, and free-float or total-float based. - Move Project, Calculate (F9), and automatic or manual calculation.

heading: Datum Plan 0.3: brainstorm and plan › 3. Feature catalogue for 0.3 › P. Datum scheduling style (our own)
text: Datum Plan 0.3: brainstorm and plan › 3. Feature catalogue for 0.3 › P. Datum scheduling style (our own). Goal: ease of use with scheduling rigour, without common traps. Defaults for every new plan (each one can be changed in Schedule Options): Topic ; Datum default ; Why ; Words ; Plain names with the common alternative term in brackets, e.g. "Status date (data date)", "Slack (total float)" ; Easy to learn, and the vocabulary is recognisable to every scheduler ; Task type ; Fixed duration; adding people changes work, not dates (effort-driven off) ; Avoids a common surprise, where adding a resource shortens the task ; % complete ; One Progress field. It defaults to duration-based, with a per-task switch to physical or units ; A single number for most users, precision when needed ; Actual dates ; Filled in automatically from progress and the status date; editable ; No missing-actuals errors ; Out-of-sequence progress ; Retained logic ; The realistic forecast ; Critical ; Slack ≤ 0, with one click to switch to Longest path ; Clear for everyone, rigorous on demand ; Lag calendar ; Successor's calendar ; Predictable ; Deadlines vs constraints ; A deadline only warns (red marker, negative slack); hard constraints need a confirmation ; No silent date locks ; Calculation ; Automatic, with an Explain panel ("why this date") and a message bar for conflicts ; Never a silent change ; Entered

heading: Datum Plan 0.3: brainstorm and plan › 3. Feature catalogue for 0.3 › Q. New project workflow (step one for every plan)
text: Datum Plan 0.3: brainstorm and plan › 3. Feature catalogue for 0.3 › Q. New project workflow (step one for every plan). - New project opens a Project Setup panel docked on the right (like the details pane, not a pop-up). You can skip it at any point and come back from Project › Project Setup. 1. Project: name, code, description, client, manager, location, start date (or schedule from finish), priority. 2. Calendar and units: project calendar (Standard / 6-day / 24-hour / custom), hours per day, week start, holidays. 3. Currency and costs: the full ISO 4217 currency list (about 180, searchable, symbol and decimals), default rates. 4. Structure: WBS levels or phases, from a template or empty. 5. Resources: add people, equipment and materials now or later. 6. Branding: company name and logo upload for reports and printouts, and header/footer text. 7. Finish → opens the schedule (Gantt) with the WBS ready. - The default currency, logo and company name are user preferences in Options, applied to new projects. Each project can override them.

heading: Datum Plan 0.3: brainstorm and plan › 6. Decisions (answered 2026-10-24)
text: Datum Plan 0.3: brainstorm and plan › 6. Decisions (answered 2026-10-24). - UI technology: SolidJS + Vite (Astro was considered and rejected: it is a site/content framework for server-rendered pages and would still need a UI library inside it). - Multi-project: local files only. Each project is a .dplan file, and a workspace file lists them. Nothing is hosted; everything stays on the user's computer (open source, local-first). - Beta channel: yes, opt-in through the updater. - Priority: everything. Reports, network diagram and earned value matter most. If something slips, it moves to 0.3.1 and is listed there. - Feature write-up: received; its behaviour rules are in scope (section 3.T). - Scheduling style: our own Datum style, simple and rigorous (section 3.P). - Currency: all ISO 4217 currencies; a user preference with a per-project override. - New project workflow: a skippable Project Setup panel docked on the right comes before the schedule (section 3.Q). - Activity IDs: auto-numbered (A1000 + 10). Network diagram: boxes with links. Plan size: as large as possible (target 20k smooth, 100k workable). Fonts: dense, clean style. Language: English. - Branding: logo upload and company name, for reports and printing. Beta backups: yes. - Next: the user says "yes" to start the 0.3 build (beta.1).

heading: Datum Plan 0.3: brainstorm and plan › 6. Decisions (answered 2026-10-24) › Original questions
text: Datum Plan 0.3: brainstorm and plan › 6. Decisions (answered 2026-10-24) › Original questions. 1. UI technology. I recommend moving the screen layer from hand-written HTML strings to a small component library, SolidJS (about 7 KB), with a bundler. The engine and all logic stay in Rust. This is what lets dialogs, ribbons and the report designer reach professional quality without the code becoming fragile. The alternative is to stay as we are: possible, but slower and buggier at this size. 2. Multi-project storage: a workspace file plus .dplan files (recommended: portable, works with cloud folders and email), or a single database file. 3. Beta channel: OK to ship betas through the updater (opt-in) while 0.3 is being built? 4. Priorities if something must wait for 0.3.1: which of reports, network diagram, leveling, earned value or EPS matters most for your daily work? 5. Screenshots that would help most: - Task Information (all tabs), Field Settings, the Lookup/Formula/Graphical Indicators dialogs, Bar Styles, Timescale, Page Setup, the Report gallery and a report in the designer, the Network Diagram, the Team Planner, Resource Usage, the View ▾ dropdown, the status bar, and Timeline Format. - Activities with the bottom tabs, Layout options, Activity Codes, Schedule Options, and Check Schedule.

heading: tagline
text: tagline. Plan, schedule, track and report your projects: one small, fast app for Windows.

heading: about
text: about. Datum Plan is a desktop scheduler for project managers, planners, engineers and contractors. You enter tasks in a sheet that works like a spreadsheet, link them, and the engine works out the critical path to the minute, with working calendars, constraints, every link type and resource levelling. As the work goes on, you record progress and actuals against up to 11 baselines and see where the project stands: a tracking Gantt, earned value and earned schedule, S-curves built from each period's progress, manpower by trade, a look-ahead with a constraint log, a dashboard and progress reports. A schedule risk analysis runs the plan a thousand times to show how likely each finish date is and which tasks drive it. Sheets inside the plan work like a spreadsheet and read the schedule live by name, for your own reports and vendor lists (with country flags), and dashboards of your own lay them out on one page, so nothing is copied by hand. Plans open from common scheduling files (XML and XER) or from Excel and CSV sheets, export to Excel with formulas as well as XML, XER and MPX, and every view prints to PDF.

heading: steps
text: steps. Type tasks, durations and resources into the sheet, or open an existing plan. Link the tasks; the engine works out dates, float and the critical path. Save a baseline, record progress, and print the Gantt, the S-curve and the reports.

heading: highlights
text: highlights. A task sheet that works like a spreadsheet, with formula columns and Sheets tabs. Critical path to the minute: calendars, constraints, all link types, levelling with a preview of what moves. Resources, man-hours and costs with workload and manpower by trade; Tracking Gantt with 11 baselines; earned value, earned schedule and S-curves from each period's progress. Schedule risk analysis: how likely each finish date is (P50, P80), criticality and the tasks that drive the finish. A 3-week look-ahead with a constraint log; progress by rules of credit or installed quantities. Dashboard, progress reports and a report builder; print to PDF from every view; printed Gantt text sized in points, by row type or row by row, with columns that fit their text. Network Diagram on a whiteboard canvas; timeline with a zoom box; Excel (.xlsx) export with formulas. A command line and an MCP server, so scripts and AI assistants can build and update plans with the same operations as the window. A step-by-step guide with pictures, in English and Simplified Chinese (Help › Guide). A guided tutorial: an example plan that uses every view, with a note on each saying how it was filled in (Help › Tutorial). Sheets with the tools of a spreadsheet (fonts, borders, merged cells, cell styles, row heights, pictures) that read the plan live:

heading: highlights
text: highlights. click cells into formulas, 490 functions suggested as you type, plan data by name (Tasks[Finish], ProjectFinish, SPI), live task lists, country flags, notes, filters, data validation, links, defined names and a Format Cells dialog, each sheet's own print setup with pages set by dragging the page breaks, and zoom. Your own dashboards: numbers, progress rings, charts, tables and country flags from the plan and your sheets, laid out as you like, several per plan. Resource calendars that drive task dates: each person's own working week and leave decide when their work is done, when you switch it on. Logos and pictures kept in the plan file, by party (client, your company, vendors, sub-vendors), for print headers, dashboards and sheets. Projects made of plans: a master plan and its subplans in a hierarchy, grouped tabs, the whole project in the master's Gantt, and links between the plans kept up to date, with a four-plan example; the master gives its details, logos, print header, calendars and codes to its subplans in one step. Modules a plan takes on only when it needs them: Contract Dates & Payments (contract dates against the forecast, delay damages, payments and cash in), a Document Register (review cycles in working days on the plan's or their own calendars, return codes, client delay, weighted progress) and a Procurement

heading: highlights
text: highlights. Register (orders from enquiry to delivery, the vendor's promise against the date the plan needs it, expediting, optional links to vendor documents). A portfolio of every plan in a folder, with a timeline, the modules' figures and a shared resource pool: each resource's work across all plans against its capacity, and plans that take their rates and units from the pool.

heading: roadmap
text: roadmap. Contract dates against the forecast, delay damages and payments (0.6.0). A document register: classes, issue purposes, return codes, review cycles in working days, a transmittal log, weighted progress and its S-curve (0.6.1). A procurement register: sub-orders from enquiry to delivery, required against promised dates, an expediting log, linked to the vendor documents when you choose (0.6.2). Portfolio, quality and hardening One resource pool shared by several plans, a portfolio dashboard (0.7.0). A schedule health score with its trend, ghost bars and a log of logic changes. What-if scenarios and delay analysis: as-planned against as-built, time impact, windows. Smooth with 100,000 tasks (0.7.1); a signed installer (no Windows warning) before 1.0. Shared plans in a shared folder, with check-out per WBS so no one overwrites anyone. Comments on tasks, an audit trail, progress updates from a phone. Text styles by task type, saved custom views, a user guide, a frozen file format.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.19 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.3.19 — 2026-11-07. Embedded graphs: the fixes from testing. - Double-clicking an embedded graph works. In 0.3.18 it failed ("the server application … returned an unknown error", or nothing at all): Datum Plot started and read the graph, but could not reach its window from the thread the document called on. Every call from the document now comes to the window's thread. - Double-clicking an embedded graph in a document opens Datum Plot on that graph, with the bar "Editing a graph embedded in …" and its Update button. In 0.3.18 the window could open on the Home page instead, hiding the graph and the bar. - The bar now stands out (teal, with a white Update button), and Graph › Share › Update Document does the same. - Help › Check Embedded Graphs starts Datum Plot the way a document does and says what happened, step by step; every step is also written to embed.log in Datum Plot's data folder, for reporting a problem.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.18 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.3.18 — 2026-11-07. Embedded graphs: edit a pasted graph again in Datum Plot (Windows). - Graph › Copy Embedded (also in the graph's and the navigator's right-click menus) copies the graph with its data. Paste it into a document, slides or a workbook: it looks like the picture. - Double-click it there and Datum Plot opens it. Change anything, then click Update in the bar at the top (or press Ctrl+S, or close the window and choose Update and Close): the graph in the document changes. - The data is kept inside the document, so anyone with Datum Plot can open the graph from it. - Copy Picture stays as before: a plain picture. - Windows only, like other programs' embedded objects: on a Mac or in a browser the graph shows as its picture. This is the first version of embedded graphs: please tell us how it works in your office programs.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.17 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.3.17 — 2026-11-07. - On a narrow window (a laptop screen), ribbon groups fold from the right into one button each that keeps the group's name, such as Style ▾. heading: Changelog › 0.3.16 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.3.16 — 2026-11-07. Organising the navigator. Select several items - Ctrl+click adds items to a selection; Shift+click selects a run. Right-click the selection to delete them together (one undo step), move them to a folder or colour their names. Delete deletes the selection; Esc clears it. Folders and colours - Right-click › Move to Folder › New Folder… groups tables, results, graphs or layouts under a folder you name. Click a folder to open or close it; right-click it to rename it or remove it (its items stay). - Right-click › Colour: red, orange, green, blue, pink or grey names, to find things at a glance. - Folders and colours are saved with the project. A table's family - Right-click a data table › Show Only This Family: the navigator shows just that table, its results, its graphs and the layouts that show them. Show All brings back the rest.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.15 — 2026-11-07

An empty project shows how to add a table or import data. - Format Graph › Data Sets › Order: move data sets earlier or later on a column, grouped, pie or nested graph; the table keeps its own order. - Fill and Border colours for bars, boxes and violins, separate from the symbols. heading: Changelog › 0.3.14 — 2026-11-03
text: Changelog › 0.3.14 — 2026-11-03. Fixes from users. - Choosing Error Bars from the ribbon no longer switches Each Replicate off on column and grouped graphs. - Groups with many values spread their dots evenly across the group's width instead of piling the extra dots in a column at one edge. - The Format Graph window always works on the graph you are looking at: open another graph and it follows it, on the same page; open a table, results or a layout and it closes. heading: Changelog › 0.3.13 — 2026-11-02
