heading: Changelog › 0.1.11 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.1.11 — 2026-11-01. Complex numbers and units, completed: AC circuits in the frequency domain, Bode plots, and any result in any unit of its kind. - Phasors as magnitude and angle: V = 230 V∠-30° (∠ is on Math › Complex; or type /_). A bare number after ∠ is in degrees (230∠-30). ∠ binds before × but not inside a power: 2*10∠90° is 20j, 10^2∠30° is 100∠30°. - par(Z1, Z2, …) puts impedances in parallel; db(H) is a ratio in decibels, 20·log₁₀ ; H ; . - sin, cos, tan, sinh, cosh and tanh work on complex values (transmission lines, cosh(γl)), as exp, ln and sqrt already did. - Tables hold complex values: a formula column such as R + j*2*pi*f_t*L gives an impedance per frequency, and a cell can be typed as 3 + 4j with the column's unit. - Log frequency axes: plot db(H(f)), arg(H(f)) for f in 10 Hz .. 100 kHz log draws a Bode plot, with points spaced evenly in decades and the decades labelled. - New calc pack (20 in all): RC low-pass filter, with its cut-off frequency, gain and phase at a frequency to suppress, and both Bode plots; checked against a hand calculation. Units: one kind, several meanings

heading: Changelog › 0.1.11 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.1.11 — 2026-11-01. - ω = 2*pi*f (and 2*pi/T) shows in rad/s, and ω/(2*pi) in Hz again; 1/(2*pi)*sqrt(k/m) is a natural frequency in Hz. Nothing worked out from ω, such as ωL/R or 1/(1 + jωτ), is mistaken for an angle. A plot over ω, or of ω and f together, reads in the axis' own unit. - Hz counts cycles and rpm revolutions: 50 Hz shown in rpm is now 3000 rpm (it read 477.5), and 314.2 rad/s shown in Hz is 50 Hz. rad/s is in the unit menu of every frequency. - A kind with no usual unit of its own is written in named units instead of base units: W/m, m·K/W, J·s, N·s, V/m, W/K (it was kg·m/s³ or m²·kg/s). Every such label can be typed back as a unit, including 1/(m·s) and powers written as m⁴. Heat flux shows in W/m² (BTU/(h·ft²) in US units), mass flux in kg/(m²·s), a moment of inertia in kg·m². - Any result can be shown in any unit of its kind: its unit menu › Other unit…, then type it (kN*mm, lbf*in, W/(m^2*K)). A unit that does not fit says so on the line.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.11 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.1.11 — 2026-11-01. - 57 engine tests (new: angular frequency and named units, complex AC analysis with ∠, par, db, complex trigonometry and complex tables, the RC filter with its log plots; every automatic label for 624 kinds typed back), 89 UI tests (Other unit…, Bode plots on a log axis, the Complex keys). Every earlier pack prints exactly as in 0.1.10. 18,000 more random sheets with the new syntax. An independent review of the changes found seven issues before release (among them 1/(2π)·√(k/m) shown in rad/s, and a plot over ω scaled by 2π); all fixed, with tests.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.10 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.1.10 — 2026-10-30. Unsaved work is safer: New, Open and an update ask first. Fixes found by an independent review of 0.1.8 and 0.1.9. - New, Open, a calc pack, a recent sheet, Getting Started and installing an update now ask “Save changes?” when the sheet has unsaved changes. Before, they replaced it without asking; only closing the window asked. - An update writes a recovery copy of unsaved work before the window closes, so the new version offers it back (not when you chose Don't save). - An update installs only once its checksum has been compared with SHA256SUMS.txt. - The recovery box names the copy it offers, and Recover or Discard acts on that copy only. With two copies and two windows starting together, Discard in one window could delete a copy the other had not shown. - A window that cannot lock its recovery copy tries another name, and a lock made in the last minute is never cleaned away, so a running window's copy never looks abandoned. - A sheet saved under a name typed without .dcalc gets the extension, so Explorer opens it with Datum Calc; it never replaces an existing file without asking.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.10 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.1.10 — 2026-10-30. - A torque typed with its unit (50 N*m) keeps reading in N·m in later lines (M2*2 = 100 N·m, not 100 J); 50 J stays an energy. A torque times an angle is work, in J. - A unit after brackets gives a plain or complex number its unit, (8 + 6j) Ω; on a value that already has units, such as (F/A) MPa, it is an error that points to the unit menu, as before 0.1.8. - A complex number written out (Z = (8 + 6j) Ω) is an input, so its value is not repeated; 0j is real. - Getting Started shows torque and complex numbers. - 54 engine tests and a shell test, 86 UI tests (Save changes? before New, a pack and a recent sheet; Cancel and Don't save). Recovery tried again in the real window with two copies and two windows. 12,000 more random sheets.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.9 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.1.9 — 2026-10-30. Safer recovery when several sheets are open, two more calc packs, and smaller fixes. - Each Datum Calc window keeps its own recovery copy. Two sheets double-clicked in Explorer run as two windows; before, they shared one copy, and closing or saving one deleted the other's. A copy is offered again only when the window that kept it is no longer running (closed without saving, or crashed). - Discard in the “Recover unsaved work?” box now deletes the copy; closing the box with × keeps it for next time. A copy kept by 0.1.8 is still offered. More calc packs (19 in all) - Heat loss from an insulated pipe: radial conduction through the insulation and the outer surface coefficient in series, the heat lost per metre and along the line, and the surface temperature for personnel protection. - Fillet weld in shear: the simplified method for a pair of fillet welds, with the minimum throat and length. - Each is checked against a hand calculation in the tests. - j (or i) is drawn upright in equations when it is the imaginary unit, as in the results; a name of the sheet called j stays italic. - A check on absolute temperatures (29.6 °C ≤ 60 °C) shows no utilisation; a ratio of kelvins meant nothing.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.9 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.1.9 — 2026-10-30. - 54 engine tests, 82 UI tests (Discard and × in the recovery box); 18,000 more random sheets. Recovery was tried in the real window: a crashed window's copy offered and recovered, a running window's copy never offered, Discard, a copy from 0.1.8, and two windows at once.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.8 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.1.8 — 2026-10-30. What visitors asked for: complex numbers for AC circuits, and torque in N·m. - Type 4j (or 4i) for an imaginary number, and j (or i) on its own for the imaginary unit: Z = R + j*omega*L. A name on the sheet called j or i takes their place; 4j stays imaginary. - A unit after brackets applies to all of them: Z = (8 + 9.42j) Ω. - +, −, ×, ÷ and powers work on complex values, as do sqrt, exp, ln, abs (the magnitude), sum and mean. New functions: re, im, arg (the angle), conj and polar(r, θ). - Results show as (3 + 4j) Ω, or as magnitude and angle (5∠53.13° Ω) with View › Polar, saved with the sheet. Equations with their numbers show the complex values too. - Checks, comparisons, solve, plots, ranges and tables work on real values and say so: compare abs(I), plot abs(Z) or arg(Z). - New calc pack (17 in all): AC circuit, an R–L load with a capacitor in parallel for power-factor correction, with its impedance, current phasor, complex power and power factor checked against a hand calculation.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.8 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.1.8 — 2026-10-30. - A force times a length shows in N·m (lbf·ft in US units), and so does a power over a speed: 120 N × 0.35 m = 42 N·m, not 42 J. A power times a time still shows in J. - N·m, kN·m, N·mm, MN·m, lbf·ft, lbf·in and kip·ft are in the unit menu of every torque and energy result. - 52 engine tests (three new ones for complex numbers, torque and the AC pack, with the hand values first), 80 UI tests. The random-sheet test now also writes complex numbers and units after brackets; 24,000 more random sheets came through without a fault.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.6 — 2026-10-28
text: Changelog › 0.1.6 — 2026-10-28. Safer saving, three more calc packs, a summary of checks on the printed sheet, figures per sheet, Duplicate and Insert Above. More calc packs (16 in all) - Pipe wall thickness for internal pressure, with corrosion allowance and mill tolerance, against the nominal wall of the schedule. - Column buckling (Euler): critical load, critical stress, slenderness, the load against the critical load with a safety factor, and whether Euler's formula applies. - Cable voltage drop (three-phase): from resistance and reactance per km, as a percentage of the line voltage, against a limit. - Each is checked against a hand calculation in the tests. - Print › Summary of checks at the start: a box at the top of the first page lists every check with both values, the utilisation and PASS or FAIL, and says whether all pass. It is saved with the sheet. - View › Figures sets how many significant figures this sheet shows (3 to 6); the engine always works at full precision. - Duplicate (Ctrl+D) copies a region below it with its style and unit; Insert Above (Ctrl+Shift+M) adds an equation above the selected one. Both are on Home › Arrange. Results that read better - A check reads in the unit its value is shown in: 0.95 % ≤ 3 %, not 0.0095 ≤ 0.03.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.6 — 2026-10-28
text: Changelog › 0.1.6 — 2026-10-28. - An input whose unit has no counterpart in the other unit system keeps its own unit (0.193 ohm/km on a US sheet). Electrical units and cP are used the same way in both systems. - Specific energy and head on a US sheet show in BTU/lb. - Saving writes to a temporary file first and then replaces the sheet in one step, so a crash or a full disk never leaves a half-written sheet. - Files over 64 MB are refused; bytes that are not text are replaced, so a damaged sheet still opens as far as it can. Very long texts, huge pictures and oversized tables in a file are cut to the limits; an edit beyond them is refused with a message. - If one region (or the Variables panel) ever cannot be drawn, it shows a short note and the rest of the window keeps working. A utilisation that is not a number shows nothing instead of stopping the panel. - Every pack is saved, reopened and damaged hundreds of times in the tests; another 72,000 random sheets ran without a failure.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.5 — 2026-10-28
text: Changelog › 0.1.5 — 2026-10-28. A bigger release: equations shown with their numbers, three more calc packs, a list of every check, and a round of hardening that found and fixed four ways the engine could fail. Equations with their numbers (View › Numbers) - Each equation is shown a second time with the values put in, as on a hand calculation: P = ρ g Q H/η = 998 kg/m³ · 9.807 m/s² · 120 m³/h · 45 m / 0.75 = 19.57 kW. Each value appears in the unit it is shown in on its own line. The setting is saved with the sheet and printed. More calc packs (13 in all) - Shaft torsion: torque from power and speed, shear stress, the smallest diameter for an allowable stress, and the angle of twist (shown in degrees). - Tank volume, liquid mass, bottom pressure and fill time (times of an hour or more show in hours). - Thermal expansion of a pipe: free growth, and the stress and force if it were fully restrained, with a FAIL that shows why the line needs a loop. - Each is checked against a hand calculation in the tests, like the first ten. - The side panel lists every check with its utilisation and PASS or FAIL; click one to go to it.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.5 — 2026-10-28
text: Changelog › 0.1.5 — 2026-10-28. - On a check line the badge now comes straight after the check, before its note. - A line with thousands of brackets or signs inside each other could stop Datum Calc; lines are now limited (60 levels, 1,000 symbols) with a clear message, and the sheet is worked out on its own thread with plenty of room. - A range with a tiny step (x = 0, 1e-300 .. 1) could stop Datum Calc; it now says a range holds at most 100,000 values. - A unit power such as m^999 was quietly cut to m^127; powers of units above 60 now give a clear message. - Results beyond about 10³⁰⁸ now say so instead of showing nothing; numbers too small to matter (below 10⁻³⁰⁰) show as 0. - A square or cube root of a value carrying rotation (such as a torque worked out from rpm) no longer gives a units error. - Over 100,000 random sheets (random equations, units, tables, checks, solve and plot) and 20,000 random unit strings and numbers are now worked out in the tests, in both build types, without a failure. - Degrees read 0.22° (no space). The Home tile counts the packs. Pasted pictures are limited to 4 MB.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.4 — 2026-10-28
text: Changelog › 0.1.4 — 2026-10-28. A Getting Started sheet, inputs that keep their units, clearer numbers, and calc packs that convert to US units. - File › Home › Getting Started (and Help › Getting Started) opens a short sheet that shows how Datum Calc works by example: inputs with units, equations and results, temperatures, a check, a function with solve and plot, and a table. Change any line and watch the rest follow. - An input keeps the unit you typed it in: I = 8356 cm^4 shows 8356 cm⁴, not 83.56×10⁶ mm⁴. In a sheet set to US units, metric inputs are shown in US units (and the other way round). - Large numbers keep only their significant figures and are grouped in threes: a Reynolds number shows as 274 900. - In a sheet set to US units, every pack result converts (psi, ksi, in, ft, gpm, hp, °F). Moments stay in kN·m, torque in N·m and apparent and reactive power in kVA and kvar, because those units cannot be told apart from energy and power automatically.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.3 — 2026-10-28
text: Changelog › 0.1.3 — 2026-10-28. Ten ready calc packs, notes on every line, copying results and CSV export: the convention build. Calc packs (File › New from pack) - Rotating equipment: pump power, efficiency and motor size; NPSH available against NPSH required; pump curve against system curve (the operating point, plotted and solved); compressor polytropic head and power. - Process: pipe pressure drop (Darcy–Weisbach with the Colebrook friction factor solved); heat exchanger duty and LMTD. - Mechanical: thin-walled pressure vessel (hoop and longitudinal stress, required thickness); beams (simply supported and cantilever deflection and bending stress); bolt preload and tightening torque. - Electrical: motor full-load current, apparent and reactive power, starting current. - Each pack has its inputs at the top (highlighted), results and checks below, and its textbook or standard at the end. Each is checked against a hand calculation in Datum Calc's tests. Notes on a line - Text after # describes the line and shows beside it: Q = 120 m^3/h # rated flow. - Right-click a region: Copy Result (19.61 kW, to paste into a spreadsheet or a report), Copy as LaTeX, Mark as Input, Move, Delete. - File › Export › Inputs and results (CSV): every named value with its unit and whether it is an input or a result, and every check with PASS or FAIL and its utilisation.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.2 — 2026-10-28
text: Changelog › 0.1.2 — 2026-10-28. Tables, pictures and the list of every unit; a fix for gravity after a unit. - Insert › Table: a small grid with a name and a unit for each column, such as a pump curve from its data sheet. Each column becomes a vector you can use below it: H_at(q) = interp(q, Q_d, H_d). - A cell without a unit takes the column's unit; a column with a formula (rho*g*Q_d*H_d) is worked out value by value and shown in its unit. - Double-click a table to edit it: type from cell to cell, Enter moves down (and adds a row at the bottom), + Row and + Column grow it, Done saves it as one change you can undo. - Insert › Picture adds a sketch or a photo, such as a free-body diagram, with a caption. Paste a picture (Ctrl+V) to add it straight away. Format › Picture sets its size. Units, constants and functions - Units › All Units lists every unit by kind with its name and SI units; Math › All Functions lists the functions and constants. Search, then click one to type it into the region you are editing. - Tables and pictures print with the sheet; a region that does not fit moves to the next page instead of being cut.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.1 — 2026-10-28
text: Changelog › 0.1.1 — 2026-10-28. The engine arrives: every equation is worked out with its units, shown as maths, and checked. - About 200 units: SI with prefixes and US customary (m, mm, in, ft; kg, lb; N, kN, lbf, kip; Pa, kPa, MPa, bar, psi; J, kWh, BTU; W, kW, hp; m³/h, gpm, L/s; rpm, rad/s; and many more). Every factor is tested against the published NIST value. - Write units after a number: 120 m^3/h, 2.5 kN*m, 1.2 W/(m^2*K), 9.81 m/s². - Adding metres to seconds is an error on that line, and the wrong part of the line is underlined. - Temperatures in °C and °F are handled correctly: 20 °C − 10 °C is a difference of 10 K, the mean of two temperatures stays a temperature, and −40 °C is −40 °F. - Results are shown in a sensible unit (18.4 kW, 2.5 MPa, 250 mm) for the sheet's unit system (SI or US). Click ▾ after a result to show it in another unit. - Every line is drawn as maths: fractions, roots, powers, subscripts (sigma_allow → σ with “allow” below) and Greek letters by name. - + − × ÷, powers, brackets; sqrt, sin, cos, tan (in radians, or with deg), ln, log, exp, min, max, abs, round, if, sum, mean, interp, hypot.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.1 — 2026-10-28
text: Changelog › 0.1.1 — 2026-10-28. - Your own functions: f(x) = 3*x^2 + 2. Ranges: x = 0, 0.1 .. 10. - Constants: g, π, e, R, σ_SB (Stefan–Boltzmann). A name on the sheet takes the place of a constant. - A name used before it is defined says so, and an error never stops the rest of the sheet. Checks, solve and plot - check sigma <= sigma_allow shows a green PASS or a red FAIL with both values and the utilisation (0.82 means 82 % used). - solve … for x in a .. b finds the value that makes both sides equal in the range, for example the Colebrook friction factor or a pump's operating point. - plot H_pump(Q), H_sys(Q) for Q in 0 m^3/h .. 150 m^3/h draws the curves, with a crosshair and a PNG button. - A Variables panel lists every name with its value and unit; click one to go to its line. The checks that pass and the lines with errors are counted there and in the status bar. - The printed calc sheet shows the maths, the results and the PASS/FAIL badges.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.0 — 2026-10-28
text: Changelog › 0.1.0 — 2026-10-28. The first release of Datum Calc: the window, the calc sheet, saving and opening, printing, and updates from day one. The calc sheet - A page (A4 or Letter) with a title block: project, calc number, title, prepared by, checked by, date and revision, your company and logo. - Math, text and check regions, read top to bottom like a calculation on paper. Ctrl+M adds an equation, Ctrl+T a text region; Enter ends an equation and starts the next one. - Mark regions as inputs (highlighted), headings, notes or references. - Move regions with Alt+↑ and Alt+↓; undo and redo every change. - The Math tab types Greek letters, operators and functions into the region you are editing; the Units tab types units. - This release keeps what you type; the engine that works out the results with their units arrives in 0.1.1. - Sheets save as .dcalc files. A damaged file opens with every region that can still be read. - A recovery copy is kept while you work; recent sheets are listed on the File page. - File › Print shows the pages: the title block on every page, "Page x of y" at the bottom and the references at the end. Choose Save as PDF to make a PDF. The family window

heading: Changelog › 0.1.0 — 2026-10-28
text: Changelog › 0.1.0 — 2026-10-28. - Ribbon (Home, Insert, Math, Units, Check, View, Help, and Format for the selected region), Tell me (Ctrl+K), a ? beside every tool, Options, light, dark and auto themes. - File › Updates checks GitHub for new versions and installs them after checking their SHA-256 checksum.

heading: Datum Calc: notes for Claude
text: Datum Calc: notes for Claude. Read docs/MEMORY.md first. It is the project's memory: architecture, decisions, roadmap, and a log of every session. At the end of every session that changes anything, update docs/MEMORY.md: - tick the roadmap - add a session-log entry - record any new decisions - refresh the architecture section if files moved The family design guide is FAMILY.md in the hub (Edgar-Mendonca/Datum); docs/FAMILY.md links to it. Datum Plan (Edgar-Mendonca/Datum-Plan) is the reference implementation: copy from it rather than reinventing. - Rust and Tauri 2, small and efficient code, Windows first. - Ship in small numbered releases (0.1.0, 0.1.1, …). Every release appears in the in-app updater. - Amber accent (#A8650F); warnings use the warning colours with an icon, never the accent alone. - Keep code compact and match the surrounding style. Engine logic belongs in crates/core (pure Rust, unit-tested), not in the UI. - The UI is SolidJS + Vite in ui/src/*.tsx (built to ui/dist). State lives in ui/src/store.ts; the engine computes all values, the window only shows them. - Public words (FAMILY §13): describe what Calc does; never name, compare with, or say it copies or replaces a commercial product, in any file, commit, release note or the site. Checks before pushing: - cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings - cargo test --workspace

heading: Datum Calc: notes for Claude
text: Datum Calc: notes for Claude. - npm run check:ui, then npm run build:ui and the UI tests (cargo run -q -p datum-core --example dump > tests_ui/fixture.json && node tests_ui/run.cjs) - cargo deny check (licences, advisories, sources; CI runs it) Releasing: 1. Bump the version in src-tauri/Cargo.toml and crates/core/Cargo.toml. 2. Add a CHANGELOG section (## x.y.z — date), and keep docs/site.json true to the release (about, steps, highlights, roadmap; no commercial product names). 3. Push, then run release.yml with workflow_dispatch (or push the tag vX.Y.Z). The workflow creates the tag and publishes DatumCalc-x.y.z-setup.exe and SHA256SUMS.txt.

heading: Contributing › How the code is laid out
text: Contributing › How the code is laid out. - crates/core: the engine in pure Rust (units, expressions, evaluation, solving, LaTeX, the sheet document, calc packs). All logic lives here, with tests. - src-tauri: the desktop shell (commands, files, updater). - ui/src: the window (SolidJS + TypeScript). It shows what the engine computes and sends edits back as operations. - docs/MEMORY.md: architecture, decisions, roadmap and a log of every session. Read it first.

heading: Contributing › Before you send a change
text: Contributing › Before you send a change. Keep code compact and in the style around it. A new engine feature comes with a test; a new window feature with a UI test where it can. A unit added to the table comes with its factor test against a published value. By contributing you agree your work is released under the MIT licence.

heading: Datum Calc › What it does
text: Datum Calc › What it does. Datum Calc is a desktop app for engineering calculation sheets. You write the calculation top to bottom, as on paper: an equation per line with its units, text for headings and references, and checks against your limits. It prints as a clean calc sheet with a title block and page numbers, ready to hand in. 1. Write the equations. Q = 120 m^3/h, H = 45 m, P = rho*g*Q*H/eta. Greek letters and subscripts are typed simply (sigma_allow). 2. Check the results. Every answer carries its unit (a torque in N·m, an AC current as a complex phasor such as (12.04 − 3.346j) A or 12.5 A∠−15.53°, ω = 2πf in rad/s; any result in any unit of its kind), and check sigma The printed calc sheet: title block, maths, results, PASS/FAIL checks, page numbers. Inputs with units and descriptions; every name, value and unit in the Variables panel. It is for mechanical, process, structural and electrical engineers, students and lecturers: everyone who writes calculations. It is part of the Datum family of free, open-source desktop tools for engineers and scientists; its page on the family site is edgar-mendonca.github.io/Datum/apps/calc.

heading: Datum Calc › Install
text: Datum Calc › Install. Download DatumCalc-x.y.z-setup.exe from the latest release and run it. It installs for your user only, in seconds, and updates itself from File › Updates. Each release has a SHA256SUMS.txt to check the download. Datum Home (from the family site) can install and update it too. Free and open source (MIT). Windows first. No accounts, no telemetry: your files stay on your computer, and the only network call is the update check.

heading: Datum Calc: project memory › 1. Architecture › Release flow
text: Datum Calc: project memory › 1. Architecture › Release flow. 1. Bump src-tauri/Cargo.toml and crates/core/Cargo.toml; CHANGELOG section ## X.Y.Z — date; update this file and docs/site.json. 2. Commit and push to the working branch. 3. Run release.yml (workflow_dispatch; it creates the tag vX.Y.Z and the GitHub Release with the installer and SHA256SUMS.txt). 4. Users get it from File › Updates; Datum Home installs it from the same release.

heading: Datum Calc: project memory › 1. Architecture › How we work (the workflow, from Datum Plan)
text: Datum Calc: project memory › 1. Architecture › How we work (the workflow, from Datum Plan). 1. The user reviews the last release and sends screenshots with bugs and wishes. 2. Diagnose first. Reproduce in the test harness or the real app before changing code. 3. Bigger asks get a plan file (docs/PLAN-x.y.md). For 0.1 the brief already answered every question, so the plan was written and building started at once. 4. Engine first (crates/core, with a unit test), then the UI. 5. Check in the real app under Xvfb (build target/debug/datum-calc, start it on :99, drive it with xdotool, screenshot with import -window root). 6. Add a UI test for every bug and feature (tests_ui/run.cjs). 7. Run the checks: clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, npm run check:ui, the UI tests, cargo deny check. 8. Release (above), then watch CI and the release run. 9. Report to the user in plain language: what changed, what was checked, what is not done.

heading: Datum Calc 0.1: plan › What 0.1 is
text: Datum Calc 0.1: plan › What 0.1 is. Engineering calculation sheets. You type equations with real units; Datum Calc shows them as readable maths, works out the answers with units, checks them against limits (PASS/FAIL with a utilisation ratio) and prints a clean, referenced calc sheet with a title block. - The worksheet: a page (A4 or Letter) of regions, top to bottom, evaluated in order. Region kinds: math, text, check, solve, plot, table, image. - Units: a dimension vector (7 SI base exponents + an angle tag), about 200 units (SI with prefixes, US/imperial), absolute and difference temperatures, a chosen display unit per result and a sheet-wide unit system (SI or US). - Maths: + − × ÷, powers, roots, functions (trig with degrees or radians, ln, log, exp, min, max, abs, round, if), ranges and vectors (x = 0, 0.1 .. 10), sum, mean, constants (g, π, e, R, σ), user functions, Greek and subscripts typed simply (sigma_allow → σ_allow). - Solve: Brent's method in a range; "no root in range" is said clearly. - Calc packs: ten ready, referenced sheets (File › New from pack), each also an engine test against a hand calculation. - Printing: the calc sheet as PDF with a title block (project, calc number, title, by, checked, date, revision), "Page x of y" and the references at the end.

heading: Datum Calc 0.1: plan › Architecture (from the brief, §3)
text: Datum Calc 0.1: plan › Architecture (from the brief, §3). Plan's formula columns use the GridCraft crates (spreadsheet formulas), which have no units. Calc's grammar is different (units on numbers, assignments, ranges, user functions), so its parser is a small hand-written Pratt parser in the same compact style; the idea taken from Plan is "the engine computes, the window only shows" and the error-per-cell behaviour. No GridCraft dependency in Calc.

heading: tagline
text: tagline. Engineering calculations with real units, as readable maths, with checks and a printable calc sheet.

heading: for
text: for. Mechanical, process, structural and electrical engineers, students and lecturers: everyone who writes calculations.

heading: about
text: about. Datum Calc is a desktop app for engineering calculation sheets. You type equations with their units, such as Q = 120 m^3/h or P = rho*g*Q*H/eta; Datum Calc shows them as readable maths, works out each answer with its unit, and catches mistakes such as adding metres to seconds on the line where they happen. Checks compare results with their limits and show PASS or FAIL with the utilisation. The sheet prints as a clean, referenced calc sheet with a title block (project, calc number, by, checked, date, revision) and page numbers, ready to hand in. Ready-made calc packs for pumps, pipes, compressors, heat exchangers, tanks, pipe walls, pipe insulation, vessels, beams, columns, shafts, bolts, welds, thermal expansion, motors, cables, AC circuits and filters start you off. Complex numbers (3 + 4j) work out AC circuits, shown as 3 + 4j or as magnitude and angle.

heading: steps
text: steps. Type each equation with its units, top to bottom, as on paper; the maths is shown as you would write it. Every answer carries its unit; checks against your limits show PASS or FAIL with the utilisation ratio. Print the calc sheet Fill in the title block and print or save a PDF with page numbers and references.

heading: highlights
text: highlights. Equations with real units: about 200 units, SI with prefixes and US customary, absolute and difference temperatures, torques in N·m, angular frequencies in rad/s, any result in any unit of its kind, dimension errors caught on the line. Readable maths: what is shown is drawn from the same expression the engine computes. Checks with PASS or FAIL and the utilisation ratio. Solve for the value that makes an equation zero within a range, plot functions such as a pump curve against the system curve, and tables with units per column. Twenty ready calc packs, each with its reference and a test against a worked example. Complex numbers for AC circuits in the frequency domain: impedances such as (8 + 9.42j) Ω, phasors as 230 V∠-30°, impedances in parallel, complex power, and Bode plots on a log frequency axis. Each equation can be shown again with its numbers put in, as on a hand calculation. A printable calc sheet with a title block, a summary of checks, page numbers and references; inputs and results export as CSV.

heading: Changelog › 0.9.0 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.9.0 — 2026-11-07. Impact: fast events in a meshed solid, stepped in time. - Solve › Analysis › Impact (explicit dynamics), for meshed solids (modelled or imported): a load put on suddenly (or following a factor against time), or a solid that starts moving, stepped through time by central differences with lumped masses. The time step is found from the mesh's highest frequency and kept at 90 % of the stable limit; set how long to follow it in Solve › Steps (milliseconds: waves cross steel at about 5 km/s). - Supports & Loads › Velocity: the whole solid (or one face, ▾) starts moving: a bar hitting a wall, a part dropped onto a fixed face. - The player shows the solid moving in time; the stresses shown are at the moment it moves most, with the balance of loads, inertia forces and reactions then. Results › In Time graphs the largest movement and the energy moving, stored and together. - New benchmark 37: a bar hit by a sudden end load (the end moves out to twice the static movement at 2L/c, within 1 % and 2 %; the energy kept within 0.1 %), and a block in free flight (exact). - Our own solver (Bathe §9.2; lumped masses by HRZ), no outside code.

heading: Changelog › 0.9.0 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.9.0 — 2026-11-07. - In the real app a 200 mm steel bar hitting a wall at 10 m/s: the free end moved 0.375 mm (1D theory, 0.40 mm), the stress about ρcv ≈ 400 MPa, the energy kept to 100 %. - Switching a step to Impact gives it an impact's own time (1 ms, the stable step) instead of 2 s, which would take millions of steps. - Contact, yielding and large movements in time (crash): explicit steps are elastic and small-strain for now.

heading: Changelog › 0.8.0 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.8.0 — 2026-11-07. Contact: solids that touch can press on each other and slide, held back by friction. Contact between solids - Supports & Loads › Contact: pick two solids that touch and a friction coefficient. They are meshed apart (before, touching solids were always joined) and every pair of faces where they meet gets a contact, listed under Contacts in the tree; the Inspector sets the friction and which face is kept out of which. - Where the faces press they push each other apart; where they would pull they part; along each other they hold until the friction reaches μ times the pressing force, then slide (Coulomb). A solid held only by friction stays held; one held only by frictionless contact is reported as free. - Results › Contact pressure, and a Contact table under Tables (the force through each contact, its friction, how many nodes touch and slide, the largest pressure and overlap). - Our own solver: node to surface with a penalty (the faces may overlap by about a thousandth of the movement), friction as a return mapping, found by solving again until which nodes touch and slide stops changing.

heading: Changelog › 0.8.0 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.8.0 — 2026-11-07. - New benchmark 36: a block pressed onto another through meshes that do not match (the force through the contact exact, the stress in both within 2 %), a block dragged over another (friction μN within 0.2 %), and one pushed by less than μN (it holds; the friction is the push). - Help › Contact between solids. - Contact is solved in one linear step: not yet with yielding, large movements or crushing (the folds of a crushed tube pressing on each other), nor bolt pretension; those come with the next steps.

heading: Changelog › 0.7.7 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.7.7 — 2026-11-07. Loads off the part, a finer mesh where it matters, and more ways to read the results. - Supports & Loads › Remote Force: a force and a moment acting at a point off the face (a pin, a shaft's coupling, a load on a bracket's arm), carried onto the face you click. The face takes the force, and the moment the force makes from that point, spread as a traction that varies linearly over it, so it stays free to deform. It starts at the face's centre; move its point in the Inspector. It is drawn as an arrow at the point with a line to the face. - New benchmark 35: a cantilever loaded through a remote force half a metre beyond its tip (deflection within 1 % of beam theory, bending stress within 2 %), and a square bar twisted by a remote moment (twist within 3 % of Saint-Venant torsion), each in equilibrium. - Mesh › Finer Near a Face: click a face and the solids are meshed again with elements a quarter of the size near it, growing back over a few elements; click it again to take it off. Its size is in the tree under Mesh, and it follows the face when the solids change.

heading: Changelog › 0.7.7 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.7.7 — 2026-11-07. - Results › Along a Line: the result shown, graphed along a straight line through the solid (from one side to the other through its middle to start; type the ends). - The section view under the results is labelled X, Y and Z as the view shows them (Z up). - The report of a modelled solid names its solids and features, and says how it was meshed (it called the tetrahedra wedges before).

heading: Changelog › 0.7.6 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.7.6 — 2026-11-07. More modelling, files in and out, and buildings laid out by level. - Sweep: a closed profile carried along a path drawn in another sketch, with an optional twist and a scale at the end (pipes, rails, springs). - Loft: a solid through closed sections on different planes (a square base to a round top). - Draft: click a side face to slope it by the draft angle, as a moulded or cast part needs. - Split: a solid cut in two by a plane square to X, Y or Z; the pieces are meshed joined. - Measure: click a face or an edge for its area, length, diameter or radius; click a second for the distance and angle between them. Mass lists each solid's volume, area, centre of mass and mass from its material. - New Sketch ▾ lists the planes you have made (Offset Plane, Levels). - Import › STEP brings in the solids of a STEP file from another CAD program, ready to mesh and analyse (mesh files and DXF sections are under its ▾). - Export saves the solids as a STEP file or an STL surface.

View › Section shapes turns it off. Primitives and Combine - Box, Cylinder, Cone and Sphere (Geometry › Primitives) are made in one go from a point and their sizes, and land in the history like any feature. - Combine joins solids into one, cuts some out of another, or keeps only what they share.
