The two earthquake examples played their peak values as if they grew with a load: a response spectrum is not played now; its modes are (Results › Modes). Heat on the modelled solids

heading: Changelog › 0.7.3 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.7.3 — 2026-11-07. The solids you model can now be analysed: meshed, held, loaded and solved. Analysis of the modelled solids - Go to Supports & Loads (or Mesh, or press Solve) and the solids are meshed by themselves into 10-node tetrahedra by Gmsh, which is now installed with Datum Mesh. The bar over the view says how many elements and nodes. - Click a face to hold it (Fixed, Pinned, Roller, Symmetry, Held directions) or to load it (Force, Pressure, Face force). A force on a face is shared over the face. - Faces are named after the step that made them: "Body1: Extrude1 top", "Extrude1 side 3". Supports and loads stay on their faces when you change the design: it is meshed again before the next solve. - Results as for any solid: von Mises, principal stress, displacement and safety factor in colour on the deformed shape, the cut plane, the probe, the player and the equilibrium check. - Step 1 shows the solids as modelled; the later steps show the mesh. Mesh › Element Size sets the size; Mesh › Show Elements draws them. Crushing and collapse (brought forward from 0.7.4)

heading: Changelog › 0.7.3 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.7.3 — 2026-11-07. - A new step, Crushing and collapse: yielding with large movements, so a part can be followed past its peak load as it folds. Supports & Loads › Move a Face pushes a face by a set amount, like a crusher's platen; Results › Load–Deflection then draws the force on it against its movement. - New example, Tube crushed until it collapses: an aluminium tube pushed down 6 mm. The force peaks at its squash load σy A (57.3 kN) and falls as the wall folds. Examples modelled with the new tools - A bracket with a hole, a stepped shaft (revolved), the crushed tube, and a steel strip's natural frequencies. Each opens with its history, mesh, supports, loads and steps, ready to solve. No more 3D / Section switch - The view is always 3D. Solids made the older way (a section extruded or turned) have Edit Section to change their outline, and Finish Editing to come back. - The File page's Roadmap icon is the same colour as the others. How it is built

heading: Changelog › 0.7.3 — 2026-11-07
text: Changelog › 0.7.3 — 2026-11-07. - Gmsh (GPL) is installed beside Datum Mesh in its own folder and run as a separate program; Datum Mesh writes the solids out for it and reads back the mesh it makes. Checked: a steel cantilever modelled, meshed and solved agrees with beam theory to within 4 %. - Crushing: total Lagrangian with small strains and large rotations (Bathe, *Finite Element Procedures* §6.6), von Mises yielding with the consistent tangent (Simo and Hughes). New benchmark 34: a cantilever bent far against the elastica (within 1 %), and a bar pulled past yield by its end face against the exact force (within 0.01 %). - Folds pressing on each other need contact (0.8): the tube is crushed 6 mm, not flat. Natural frequencies and heat work on the modelled solids (the strip example); buckling of solids and more examples come in 0.7.4. Finer mesh near chosen faces comes with the interactions in 0.7.7.

heading: Changelog › 0.7.2 — 2026-11-06
text: Changelog › 0.7.2 — 2026-11-06. Modelling that feels right: a history you can edit, sketching on any plane with the view turning to it, a grid that follows the zoom, and no leftovers of the old section view. - The tree lists every feature in order (Sketch1, Extrude1, Hole1…), and a timeline under the 3D view shows the same, with buttons to step back and forth. - Right-click a feature: Edit Feature (its sizes, changed in place), Edit Sketch, Rename (F2), Suppress, Roll Back Here, Roll to the End, Delete (Del). Double-click edits. Right-click a solid, in the tree or the 3D view: Sketch on a face of it, Rename, Delete. - The browser's own right-click menu never shows any more. - A feature picked in the history shows in the inspector, with Edit, Suppress and Delete. Sketching on a plane - New Sketch asks for a plane: click one of the three planes at the origin, or a flat face of a solid, or choose Floor, Front or Side. - The view turns smoothly to face the plane, and you draw on it over the 3D view. Finish Sketch turns the view back to 3D, framing what was drawn.

heading: Changelog › 0.7.2 — 2026-11-06
text: Changelog › 0.7.2 — 2026-11-06. - A closed shape finished goes straight on to Extrude: the solid is made at once, and the Extrude panel changes it as you type the distance, press − and +, or turn the mouse wheel over it; Out, In or Both ways; OK keeps it, Cancel takes it away. - The floor grid has big squares with small squares inside, sized to how close you are looking and centred under the view. The sketch sheet uses the same rule. - A solid made with the modelling tools has no 3D/Section bar and no section, thickness or sweep settings: those belonged to the old extruded-section solids, which keep them. - Supports, loads, meshing and solving on the new solids come in 0.7.3, laid out as the usual analysis steps.

heading: Changelog › 0.7.1 — 2026-11-06
text: Changelog › 0.7.1 — 2026-11-06. The Datum window again, laid out in numbered steps, with full sketching and 3D modelling. - The tree on the left is laid out in the order a model is made: 1 Geometry, 2 Properties, 3 Supports & Loads, 4 Mesh, 5 Analysis, 6 Results. Each step shows ✓ when it is done or says what it still needs; click it and the ribbon shows that step's tools. - New Properties step: materials (with Assign to the selection) and sections. Sketching (Geometry › New Sketch, on the floor, front or side plane, on a face of a solid, or on an offset plane) - Create: line; arc by 3 points or by centre and ends; circle by centre and radius, 2 points or 3 points; rectangle by 2 corners, centre and corner, or 3 points; polygon inside or around a circle or by one side, any number of sides; slot centre to centre or overall. Each shape's ▾ lists its ways; the way last used stays on the button. Construction lines (dashed guides). - Modify: trim, extend, offset, fillet, chamfer. Pattern: mirror, circular, rectangular.

heading: Changelog › 0.7.1 — 2026-11-06
text: Changelog › 0.7.1 — 2026-11-06. - Constrain: dimensions typed on the drawing (lengths, diameters, radii, distances and angles, or named parameters such as W / 2); coincident, tangent, parallel, perpendicular, equal, concentric, collinear, midpoint, symmetry, horizontal or vertical, fix. Free curves are drawn blue, fully defined ones black. - Sketch report, parameters, snapping to the grid and to ends, a preview of each shape as it is placed. - Create: extrude (out, in or both ways), revolve, hole (through or to a depth). Shapes drawn inside a closed shape become holes. - Modify: fillet and chamfer (click an edge), shell and press pull (click a face). - Arrange: move, turn or copy; mirror; pattern in rows and columns or round an axis. Construct: offset plane. - The sketches and solids are kept in the .dmesh file, with autosave and recovery. How it is built - Sketching and solids come from SolidCraft's open-source geometry engine (MIT or Apache-2.0), working behind the Datum window; nothing of its own window is used. - Supports, loads, meshing and solving on these new solids come in 0.7.2 (the solids of 0.6 and the frames still analyse as before).

heading: Changelog › 0.7.0 — 2026-11-05
text: Changelog › 0.7.0 — 2026-11-05. Withdrawn on 2026-11-06. This release was the open CAD program it was built on, renamed, rather than a Datum app; it is no longer offered. 0.7.1 brings the Datum window back, laid out in numbered steps, with the CAD program's geometry engine working behind it. A new start: Datum Mesh is now a full 3D modeller with the analysis laid out in steps. A new program - Datum Mesh is rebuilt on SolidCraft, the open-source CAD program (MIT or Apache-2.0), in the Datum look: the crimson accent and the Datum mark. It is quick and smooth, and it has a full set of modelling tools. - Sketch tools with their variants: - line and arc chains; - circle by centre, by two points or by three points; - rectangle by two corners, by three points or by its centre; - polygon with any number of sides, drawn inside or outside a circle or by one edge; - Dimensions and constraints are typed, and the sketch is solved as you draw. - 3D tools: extrude, revolve, sweep, loft, fillet, chamfer, shell, hole, patterns and mirror, with a history timeline you can edit. Parts can be joined into assemblies, and STEP files can be opened and saved.

heading: Changelog › 0.7.0 — 2026-11-05
text: Changelog › 0.7.0 — 2026-11-05. - Design files are .dmx. Files from 0.6 and earlier (.dmesh) do not open in this version; 0.6.4 stays on the releases page for them. Simulation, step by step - The Simulation workspace (the workspace menu, top left) puts the analysis in order on one bar: 1. Material: pick it from the library. 2. Supports & Loads: click faces, then Fixed, Roller or Symmetry, or a force (kN, along X, Y, Z) or a pressure (MPa). Each set shows as a chip, and × removes it. 3. Mesh: the element size (or automatic), then Mesh. 4. Solve: says what is still missing, then solves. 5. Results: von Mises stress or movement in colour bands, on the deformed shape, with a legend. - The study is saved in the design and follows its faces by name. - Parts are meshed into ten-node tetrahedra by Gmsh. Gmsh is installed beside the program and always runs as a separate program (GPL). The solve uses Datum Mesh's own verified engine and checks equilibrium every time. Not in 0.7.0 (they return in 0.7.x) - Frames, trusses and plane parts. - Natural frequencies, buckling, heat, yielding, large deformation and time histories. - The results player. - The report.

heading: Changelog › 0.6.4 — 2026-11-04
text: Changelog › 0.6.4 — 2026-11-04. Results that move: play any solved result. - A bar over the drawing of every solved result: Play and Pause, back to the start, a slider to any moment, the speed (0.25× to 4×) and Loop. - A linear result grows from no load to the whole load: the shape, the colours and the diagrams in proportion, against the whole result's colour scale. - A nonlinear result (yielding, large deformation, large deflection, past the limit) plays through its increments, the slider showing the load factor; its colours (von Mises stress) grow as it yields. - A time history plays through its times, the slider showing the time. - A natural frequency or buckling mode swings, at the speed set; the slider holds it at any point of its swing. - Nonlinear solves and time histories keep up to 60 frames for playing: the movements of the drawn points (and von Mises stress for parts and solids) at each.

heading: Changelog › 0.6.3 — 2026-11-03
text: Changelog › 0.6.3 — 2026-11-03. Basic modelling: shape and arrange parts in 3D. - Finish Sketch on a new part opens the Extrude panel over the 3D view: extrude or revolve, the distance or the angle, and which way (out of the sketch, into it, or both ways evenly). A preview follows as you type; OK keeps it. Geometry › Extrude (or Extrude… in the Inspector) opens it again for the part selected. The Inspector also has Which way. Sketch on a face - New Sketch, then click a flat face of a part: the new part starts on that face and goes out of it. On a front or back face, Cut Through on the sketch bar cuts the sketch's outlines right through the part: a hole where an outline lies inside it, a notch where it runs across its edge. Features (Geometry › Features) - Hole: set Ø and click a part's front or back face; the hole goes right through. - Fillet and Chamfer: set the size and click a part near an edge along its depth; that edge is rounded or bevelled all the way along. - Cut: select a part and cut it right through another; its outlines become holes there. Arrange (Geometry › Arrange)

heading: Changelog › 0.6.3 — 2026-11-03
text: Changelog › 0.6.3 — 2026-11-03. - Move or Copy (a row of copies), Turn or Pattern (about an axis through a point; copies round it make a ring), Mirror (in a plane, as a copy or in place). Steps, points and axes are typed with Z up. Parts are picked by clicking them in 3D (Shift or Ctrl to add); the ones picked are tinted. Volume and mass - The Inspector gives each part's volume and mass, worked out exactly from its sketch (area × depth, or Pappus' theorem when turned). - Benchmark 33: a reversed block, a plate cut through, drilled, rounded and notched, a ring and a torus turned, a mirror copy and a ring of copies; exact volumes and meshed volumes against hand formulas. - A selected part was let go of after every change. - An automatic element size gave every part about 15 000 tetrahedra, so three small copies went over the node limit; the parts now share one budget by volume. - When the parts cannot be meshed together, the 3D view shows their outlines (and the bar says why) instead of a misleading picture. - A garbled file whose part's material was dropped would not open.

heading: Changelog › 0.6.2 — 2026-11-03
text: Changelog › 0.6.2 — 2026-11-03. Sketch on a plane: drawing in 3D starts with a sketch, square to you, on a plane you pick. - Geometry › New Sketch, then click one of the three squares at the origin (Front X-Z, Side Y-Z, Top X-Y) or a button on the bar. The view turns square to the plane and the sketch lies over the model, lined up with it, so what you draw sits where it goes in 3D. - A Sketch tab opens with the drawing tools, and Finish Sketch and Cancel. Finish keeps what you drew; Cancel takes back every change made while sketching. - The sketch bar names the plane, moves it along its normal (type the offset, or pick a plane that already has nodes), takes typed points (across, up, or @d-across, d-up from the last point), and turns the view: Turn the View looks round the model in 3D with the sketch kept open, starting from the sketch's side; Look At comes back square to it. - A line nearly level or upright with the last point snaps level or upright. Sizes are typed, not solved: there are no sketch constraints to keep.

heading: Changelog › 0.6.2 — 2026-11-03
text: Changelog › 0.6.2 — 2026-11-03. - New Sketch makes a new part on the plane picked and opens its sketch with the Rectangle tool; Finish selects the part so its depth or revolve angle can be set in the Inspector; an empty sketch makes no part. Edit Sketch in the Inspector opens a part's sketch the same way. - Beams, truss bars, nodes and plates are drawn in a sketch on a plane too (the Sketch tab has Line (Beam), Truss Bar, Node and the plate tools). The Front/Side/Plan bar above the 3D view, Tab to turn the plane, and the 3D typed X, Y, Z point give way to the sketch. - While sketching, the pointer and the status bar give coordinates with Z up.

heading: Changelog › 0.6.1 — 2026-11-03
text: Changelog › 0.6.1 — 2026-11-03. A cleaner start: examples in their own place, and 3D with Z up, a view cube and planes to draw on. - File › Home shows the blank models to start from; the worked examples have their own page, File › Examples, under headings (frames and trusses, 3D frames, plane parts and heat, 3D solids and assemblies, nonlinear, dynamics), each from simple to harder. The Examples button on the Home tab lists them by heading too. 3D, Z up - 3D models are shown with Z up, as CAD programs do: the floor is the X-Y plane. Coordinates, loads, supports, part placement and results are shown and typed that way. Files are unchanged, and plane frames and sections keep x across and y up. - A view cube at the top right: click Front, Back, Left, Right, Top or Bottom to look from that side; the house goes back to the corner view. An axes key at the bottom left turns with the view. - A floor grid that stays the same size as you draw and fades into the distance, with the axes at the origin. - 3D models open in the 3D view. A blank 3D solid offers a new part; a blank 3D frame shows three small planes at the origin. Drawing 3D frames

heading: Changelog › 0.6.1 — 2026-11-03
text: Changelog › 0.6.1 — 2026-11-03. - Pick Beam, then a plane to draw on: one of the three squares at the origin (Front X-Z, Side Y-Z, Top X-Y), or the bar above the view. The view turns to face the plane, and still turns freely. The plane is drawn at a fixed size, faint, and the rest of the model stays in view.

heading: Changelog › 0.6.0 — 2026-11-02
text: Changelog › 0.6.0 — 2026-11-02. Parts and assembly: 3D models made of several parts. - Geometry › New Part adds a part and opens its sketch. Draw its outline and holes with the usual tools, then extrude it by a depth or revolve it about its axis (a full turn for a ring, a tube or a shaft). - Each part has its own material and element size, and is moved and turned into place in the Inspector. The tree lists the parts; 3D shows each in its own colour; Sketch shows the sketch of the part picked beside it. - Parts that touch are tied together where they touch, so they act as one. Supports and loads go on a part's faces: click the face in 3D. - Static stress, natural frequencies, heat and plasticity solve the whole assembly. Each part is meshed into tetrahedra on its own and the parts are joined. - A new example: an aluminium tube standing between two steel plates, the first step towards crushing a tube. - Opening a saved 3D frame dropped every member running along z (depth), and the loads on them: a member's ends were compared by x and y only. Every example now opens exactly as it was saved, checked by a test.

heading: Changelog › 0.6.0 — 2026-11-02
text: Changelog › 0.6.0 — 2026-11-02. - An empty 3D frame showed a large tilted grid off to one side: the floor and the work plane now cover the same space, and the plane stands on the floor. - Help › Verification: 257 checks, all passing. New: benchmark 32, assemblies: a cantilever sketched, extruded and turned into place (within 0.8 % of beam theory), the same cantilever as two parts tied end to end (within 0.02 % of one part), a bar of steel and aluminium in series (exact to 2 × 10⁻⁶), a thick cylinder's wall revolved as a part (Lamé, 2 × 10⁻⁶), and heat through two parts of different conductivity (3 × 10⁻⁶).

heading: Changelog › 0.5.9 — 2026-11-02
text: Changelog › 0.5.9 — 2026-11-02. Easier to find your way, and 3D frames drawn in 3D. Draw 3D frames in the 3D view - Pick Beam, Truss or Node and click in the 3D view. Points snap to nodes, else to the grid on a work plane; each click goes on from the last point, and the plane moves through it. - Tab turns the work plane (Front, Side, Plan) through the last point, so the next member can go off in any direction, along z too. - Type a point and press Enter: x, y, z, or @dx, dy, dz from the last point. The point under the pointer shows its coordinates and the member's length. Esc stops at the last point. - An empty 3D frame opens on a view of a few metres of space, ready to draw in. Front, Side and Plan still show one plane flat, for drawing many members on it. Icons coloured by meaning - Supports are green, loads red, heat orange, geometry and parts blue, the mesh teal, materials amber, solving green and results in their own colours, in the ribbon and the model tree alike.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.9 — 2026-11-02
text: Changelog › 0.5.9 — 2026-11-02. - Product and file-format names are trademarks of their owners and are used only to describe file compatibility (README, NOTICE). The checks that keep commercial product names out of the app's text now cover its documents and the whole window.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.8 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.8 — 2026-11-01. 3D frames turn far. Large rotations in 3D frames - A large-deflection step on a 3D frame now follows large rotations in space: every beam is cut into pieces that turn as rigid bodies and bend a little on their own (corotational beams), so bending both ways, twist and their coupling are all taken in. Before, a 3D frame's large-deflection step was second order (P-delta) only. - Past limit loads (arc length) works for 3D frames too, so snap-through shows in 3D as it does in plane frames. - Results › Load–Deflection for 3D frames: the load against the movement in x, y or z of the node the step follows, or how far it has turned; the deflected shape is drawn true to size. Send to Datum Plot takes the curve. - A new example, the curved cantilever bent out of its plane: a 45° bend pushed down at its tip, bending and twisting far. - With plates in the model, a large-deflection step on a 3D frame stays second order (P-delta), as before.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.8 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.8 — 2026-11-01. - Help › Verification: 246 checks, all passing. New: benchmark 31, large rotations in 3D frames: a cantilever rolled a quarter turn about either axis (within 0.05 % of the elastica), a skew cantilever bent far by a load across it (within 0.1 %), a bar twisted 2 rad (exact), and the 45° bend of Bathe and Bolourchi (within 1.1 % of the published tip, whose sources differ by about 1 %). Lee's frame built in 3D snaps through at the plane frame's limit load.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.7 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.7 — 2026-11-01. Imported meshes yield and stretch. Nonlinear steps on imported meshes - Solve › Steps on a mesh of tetrahedra: an elastic-plastic step (von Mises with hardening, up to collapse) or a large-deformation step (rubber, and parts that move far), as for swept 3D solids, with the plastic strain, the load–deflection curve and true-size drawing. - The same solvers serve swept and imported solids: they now take any mesh's integration points, so each improvement reaches both. - Help › Verification: 233 checks, all passing. New: benchmark 30, the earlier nonlinear answers on 10-node tetrahedra: the thick cylinder's collapse pressure (within 0.3 % of Hill), a bar hardening past yield (exact), a rubber bar stretched to twice its length (exact), and a cantilever bent far (within 0.12 % of the elastica). Benchmarks 26 and 27 give the same numbers as before to the last digit.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.6 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.6 — 2026-11-01. Imported meshes vibrate and conduct heat. Natural frequencies of imported meshes - Solve › Natural Frequencies on a mesh of tetrahedra: the lowest frequencies and their mode shapes, with consistent masses (each material's density), shown swinging in 3D. Heat conduction in imported meshes - Set Analysis to 3D heat conduction (Inspector, nothing selected): fixed temperatures, heat flux and convection on the mesh's faces, heat made inside; temperatures, heat flux and the heat balance. - New example: the pipe elbow carrying hot oil, cooled by air. - Help › Verification: 226 checks, all passing. New: benchmark 29: a bar's stretching vibration (exact to 2e-8), a cantilever's bending vibration (within 0.3 % of beam theory, its two equal modes equal), a plate with heat made inside (exact), and radial conduction through a thick cylinder wall (temperature within 0.003 %, heat flow within 0.001 %). - The colour bar labelled a narrow range with the same number on every band (114.1 to 114.5 °C read 114): its labels now carry the digits that tell them apart. - The model's name could be crowded out of the top of the tree by its analysis.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.5 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.5 — 2026-11-01. Parts of any shape: tetrahedra and imported meshes. Import a mesh - Geometry › Import › Mesh (or File › New › 3D solid › From a mesh file): a tetrahedral mesh made in a mesher, as Gmsh .msh (ASCII, format 2.2 or 4.1) or .inp in the CalculiX input format (C3D4 and C3D10), in the length unit you choose. - The outer surface is split into faces where it turns more than 35°, and the file's named surfaces (Gmsh physical surfaces, *SURFACE and *NSET) keep their names. The faces are listed in the tree and shown in 3D. - Supports (fixed, pinned, roller, symmetry, held directions) and loads (pressure, face forces, gravity) go on faces: pick the tool, click a face. The mesh's material is chosen in the Inspector. - Solved with our own 4-node and 10-node tetrahedra for static stress: contours, deformed shape, cutting plane, probe, reactions and the equilibrium check, as for every 3D solid. - New example: a steel pipe elbow meshed in 10-node tetrahedra. - Help › Verification: 219 checks, all passing. New: benchmark 28, tetrahedra: a bar pulled (exact for both elements), a cantilever against beam theory with shear (within 0.8 %, its clamped root a little stiffer), and a thick cylinder against Lamé (hoop stress within 0.1 %, bore growth within 0.02 %).

heading: Changelog › 0.5.4 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.4 — 2026-11-01. Datum Mesh talks to the rest of the family. - Results › Send to Datum Plot: a load–deflection curve, a time history or the natural frequencies, as a table (SI units) that opens in Datum Plot for graphs. - Results › Send to Datum Calc: the largest stress, movement, moment or temperature, the smallest safety factor and the lowest frequency, as values with units for a hand check. - Materials › From Datum Atlas…: a material sent from Datum Atlas joins the model with its values and source, checked first. - When the other app is not installed, the data is saved and copied, ready to paste, and the message says where to get it. The packet format is shared by all eight Datum apps (docs/LINKS.md). - Clearer icons for tools that looked alike: plane stress and plane strain, heat in 2D and 3D, temperature change and edge temperature, rollers along x and y, the moment, shear and axial diagrams, utilisation, mesh quality and mesh lines, reports. - Fixes: on the Loads tab the loads group's name was pushed out of sight by its column of four buttons. - Every packet read from another program is checked; a fuzz test throws 3 000 damaged ones at the reader.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.3 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.3 — 2026-11-01. A clearer model tree, and a guided start. The model tree - Every branch and every item has its own icon (beams and truss bars, nodes, shapes and holes, materials, sections, each kind of support and load), and each branch folds with a guide line down its items; long lists start folded. - Each branch says whether it is done (✓) or needs something (!), and why when you point at it: no supports yet, no loads, a material without the yield strength an elastic-plastic step needs, results out of date. - An empty branch shows what to add and starts the right tool when clicked. - New branches, in the order a model is built: loads grouped by load case, combinations, the analysis steps, and the results (the drawing, the tables and equilibrium, the report). - Right-click an item to delete it. The ? and + on every branch stay. - File › New (Ctrl+N) asks what you are analysing (a 2D truss, 2D frame, 3D frame, 2D part, 3D solid, or heat in a part or solid), which kind (plane stress, plane strain or turned; extruded or revolved) and what you want to know (static, large deflection, plastic, rubber, earthquake…), then makes the model with that analysis set up and the right drawing tool ready.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.2 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.2 — 2026-11-01. Rubber, and 3D solids that move far. Large deformation of 3D solids - Solve › Steps › Add a large-deformation step on a 3D solid: it is followed through large movements and strains, every material a neo-Hookean solid with its own E and ν. Rubber stretches and squashes as it really does; steel parts bend far while staying elastic. Newton's method on the deformed solid (total Lagrangian), the load in increments. - The deformed shape is drawn true to size; stresses are true stresses on the deformed solid; Results › Load–Deflection draws the load against the largest movement. - Help › Rubber and large deformation. - New example: a soft rubber finger curling down under a push at its tip. - Help › Verification: 208 checks, all passing. New: benchmark 27, a rubber bar stretched to twice its length and squeezed to 0.6 of it (stretch, thinning and true stress exact to 1e-14 against the neo-Hookean answer), and a slender cantilever bent far by an end load against the elastica (tip within 0.1 % down and 0.4 % in), balanced about the bent shape.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.1 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.1 — 2026-11-01. 3D solids that yield. Plasticity in 3D solids - Solve › Steps › Add an elastic-plastic step now works on 3D solids too, extruded or revolved: von Mises with each material's hardening, the load in increments, each solved by Newton's method with the consistent tangent; B-bar keeps the wedge elements from locking as they yield. If the solid cannot carry the whole load it collapses, and the solve says at what share of it. - Results: Equivalent plastic strain on the 3D view, and Results › Load–Deflection for 3D solids. - New example: a holed steel plate in 3D pulled past yield, the plastic zones spreading across the net section from the hole. - Help › Verification: 197 checks, all passing. New: benchmark 26, plasticity in 3D solids: the collapse pressure of a thick cylinder held between its end faces (within 0.4 %) and of a thick sphere revolved a slice (within 0.6 %) against Hill's limit analysis, and a bar pulled past yield with hardening (stretch and plastic strain exact, balanced to 3e-13).

heading: Changelog › 0.5.0 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.0 — 2026-11-01. Parts that yield: the first nonlinear material. - Solve › Steps › Add an elastic-plastic step on a part (plane stress, plane strain or axisymmetric): the load goes on in increments and, where the von Mises stress reaches a material's yield strength, it yields, hardening as its new Hardening value says (Materials; 0 for perfectly plastic). The stress spreads to the rest of the part. - Each increment is solved by Newton's method with the consistent tangent of the von Mises return mapping; plane strain and turned parts use B-bar so yielding, which keeps the volume, does not lock the elements. If the part cannot carry the whole load it collapses, and the solve says at what share of it. - Results: Equivalent plastic strain contours, and Results › Load–Deflection: the load against the largest movement, with when it first yields. - New example: a thick steel tube yielding under internal pressure. - Help › Verification: 192 checks, all passing. New: benchmark 25, the collapse pressure of a thick cylinder in plane strain (within 0.4 %) and of a thick sphere (axisymmetric, converging to within 0.6 %) against Hill's limit analysis, and a strip pulled past yield with hardening (stretch and plastic strain exact).

heading: Changelog › 0.4.5 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.4.5 — 2026-11-01. Rigid end zones at joints. Member end offsets - Inspector › Rigid end at the start / end: the length of a beam inside a deep column (or of a column inside a deep beam) where it cannot bend. The member bends only between its rigid zones, which are drawn thick; a hinge sits at the face of the joint. They act in every solve: static, second order, large deflection, natural frequencies, buckling and dynamics, plane and 3D. - The frame in an earthquake now has rigid ends of half a column's depth on its beams. - Time histories keep their balance check sharp on frames with very stiff parts (rigid zones, rigid floors): each step is refined with the same factors. - Help › Verification: 188 checks, all passing. New in benchmark 24: a cantilever with a rigid zone at its root (tip deflection over its flexible length, within 0.001 %; root moment exact) and a 3D beam fixed at both ends with rigid zones under a uniform load (within 0.001 %, balanced).

heading: Changelog › 0.4.4 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.4.4 — 2026-11-01. Rigid floors for buildings. - Model › Rigid floors (3D frames): every floor, the nodes at one height above the lowest, moves as one rigid plate in its own plane, sliding along x and z and turning about y together, as a concrete floor ties a building's columns. It acts in static solves, second order, natural frequencies and dynamics, so floors sway and twist as one in an earthquake. - New example: a three-storey steel building in 3D with rigid floors and their masses, shaken by a design spectrum: its modes sway along z, twist, and sway along x. - Results › Dynamics shows modes that move no mass along the shaking as 0, not as round-off. - Pictures for the newer examples on the start page. - Help › Verification: 184 checks, all passing. New in benchmark 24: four cantilever columns tied only by a rigid floor and pushed at one corner, against rigid-diaphragm statics (the floor's sway and twist, within 0.0001 %), and the floor's ties balance among themselves.

heading: Changelog › 0.4.3 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.4.3 — 2026-11-01. Structural details: bracing that only pulls, supports that settle, and second order in 3D. Members that only pull or only push - Inspector › Carries: tension only (a rod, a cable, a slender brace) or compression only (a strut on a bearing). Under the loads, a member that would carry the other kind of force drops out and the frame is solved again, until nothing changes. Slack members are drawn dashed and counted under the drawing. - New example: a two-storey frame braced with crossed rods that only pull, under wind, with one support settled. - Loads › Settlement: a support that sinks or slides by a set amount, in the directions it holds; the moments and reactions it causes are in the results. It belongs to a load case and is scaled by combinations. Plane and 3D frames. Second order in 3D frames - A large-deflection step on a 3D frame now solves it to second order (P-delta): every member's axial force softens or stiffens it, found again until it settles; the frame balances in its deflected shape.

heading: Changelog › 0.4.3 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.4.3 — 2026-11-01. - Help › Verification: 181 checks, all passing. New: benchmark 24, an X-braced panel with tension-only braces against statics (exact, both ways), a beam on a compression-only post that lets go (exact), a propped cantilever whose prop sinks, plane and 3D (exact), and a 3D flagpole bent about its weak axis to second order against the closed form (within 0.0001 %), balanced in its deflected shape.

heading: Changelog › 0.4.2 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.4.2 — 2026-10-31. Dynamics for structures: response spectrum and time history. - Loads › Mass: a mass at a node, for natural frequencies and dynamics (it is in every load case and adds no weight to a static solve). Natural frequencies now include point masses, also on weightless members. - Solve › Steps › Add a response spectrum: shake a frame (plane or 3D, with its plates) along x, y or z by a design spectrum you type as (period, acceleration) points; choose the damping, the number of modes and CQC or SRSS. The peak forces, moments, movements and reactions are combined from the modes. - Solve › Steps › Add a time history: a factor on a load case against time, or the ground's acceleration against time, followed step by step (Newmark's average acceleration, Rayleigh damping at the first two modes). The model shows the results at the time of the largest movement, with the inertia forces among the loads so the reactions balance. - Results › Dynamics: a spectrum's modes with their periods, spectral accelerations, participation and share of the mass (aim for 90 %); a time history's movement against time and every node's largest movement. - New example: a three-storey steel frame in an earthquake.

heading: Changelog › 0.4.2 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.4.2 — 2026-10-31. - Help › Verification: 170 checks, all passing. New: benchmark 23, a mass on a cantilever column against the closed forms (frequency exact; a step load's peak 2H/k, the ground stepping, resonance with 5 % damping, all within 0.01 %; a flat spectrum's movement and base shear exact), a two-storey shear frame's frequencies and spectrum (within 0.003 %), and the dynamic balance of a time history on the floor slab with its plates. - Random dynamic steps on every frame example solve and balance, or say why.

heading: Changelog › 0.4.1 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.4.1 — 2026-10-31. Plates and shells: slabs, walls and panels in 3D frames. - On a working plane of a 3D frame (Front, Side or Plan, at a depth), Geometry › Plate: draw a rectangular, polygonal or round plate, with openings. Set the thickness for new plates on the ribbon, or each plate's in the Inspector. - Plates bend (thin-plate theory) and carry forces in their own plane, and join the frame: frame nodes on a plate become its mesh nodes, and beams along a plate's edge are joined to it all along. Plates on different planes join along an edge they share. - Supports on a plate's edges (fixed or pinned), Loads › Plate Pressure on the whole plate, and self-weight. Plates are meshed into triangles automatically (Mesh › Element Size). - Results: in the 3D view the plates are coloured by von Mises stress (the worse face), movement, moments or membrane forces, on the deflected shape; the Results page lists their largest and smallest values and where. Natural frequencies include the plates, and their mode shapes move in the 3D view. - New example: a floor slab on four columns with edge beams.

heading: Changelog › 0.4.1 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.4.1 — 2026-10-31. - Help › Verification: 157 checks, all passing. New: benchmark 22, square plates simply supported and clamped (Navier's series and Timoshenko's tables, within 0.6 %), a panel bent in its own plane (exact elasticity, 0.5 %), the Scordelis–Lo roof (0.8 %) and the pinched cylinder (0.4 %) from the standard shell problems, a slab drawn in a 3D frame (0.3 %, its edge reactions exact), and the slab's first natural frequency (0.3 %). - Random plates on random planes, with random edge supports and pressures, solve and balance or say why.

heading: Changelog › 0.4.0 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.4.0 — 2026-10-31. The engine grows a core: analysis steps, and frames that bend far. Large deflection and P-delta for frames - Solve › Steps: solve a plane frame in steps. A large-deflection step applies the load in increments and finds the frame's balance in its deflected shape: second-order (P-delta) effects, large rotations, and the loss of stiffness as a frame nears the most it can carry. A step past limit loads follows the path by arc length, over the largest load and down again, so a frame that snaps through shows it. - Each step has its load (a case, a combination, or the one picked on the Loads tab) times a factor, its increments, how many pieces each beam is cut into, and the node its curve follows. Steps carry on from where the one before ended. - Results › Load–Deflection: the load against a node's movement or rotation through the solution, with the first limit load named and the unstable part of the path marked. - The deflected shape of a large-deflection solution is drawn true to size; the diagrams, reactions and equilibrium check are for the deflected frame. - New example: a snap-through frame (Lee's frame), solved past its limit load.

heading: Changelog › 0.4.0 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.4.0 — 2026-10-31. - One engine of a core and modules: the core (sparse solver, eigenvalues, load cases, and a new path solver: Newton and arc length) with frames and solids as modules on it. The vision for what comes next is in docs/VISION.md. - Help › Verification: 149 checks, all passing. New: benchmark 21, a beam-column and a flagpole against the closed-form second-order answers of AISC 360 (within 0.13 %), a cantilever rolled into a full circle by an end moment (NAFEMS NL5; the tip comes back to the root exactly), a column bent far past buckling against the exact elastica (NAFEMS NL6, within 0.2 %), and Lee's frame snapping through (NAFEMS NL7: first limit PL²/EI = 18.56 against 18.54). - Damaged files with bad steps or a revolve angle out of range open with the bad values put right, and say so.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.5 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.3.5 — 2026-10-30. Sections from CAD. - Geometry › DXF: import a part's section drawn in CAD (ASCII DXF). Lines and arcs that meet end to end, polylines with their arcs, and circles become outlines; outlines inside others become holes; arcs stay arcs. Units come from the drawing or are picked when importing. Splines, ellipses, text and blocks are left out, and the import says how many. One step to undo. - File › Export › Section as DXF: the part's outline and holes as closed polylines and circles in millimetres, for CAD. - Tools marked as planned no longer give release numbers that have passed. - Help › Verification: 134 checks, all passing. New: benchmark 20, every example's section written to a DXF and read back (areas the same to 10⁻⁹), and a drawing of loose lines and arcs in inches joined into a plate with a slot and a hole (areas exact). - Damaged DXF files (cut short, lines dropped, numbers garbled or swapped: 300 of them) are read as far as they go or refused with a reason, never a crash, and nothing read is not a number.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.4 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.3.4 — 2026-10-30. 3D solids conduct heat and vibrate. 3D heat conduction - Home › 3D Heat: a part's section extruded or revolved, as for a 3D solid, solved for steady heat conduction. Fix temperatures on faces, add heat flux, convection to air (on side faces and the back and front faces) and heat generation, by clicking faces in the 3D view or edges in Section. - Temperatures and heat flux (in x, y, z and its size) coloured over the part, with the cutting plane to see inside, the probe, and a Results page with the largest and smallest values and the heat flowing through each fixed temperature and each load, adding up to the heat balance. - New example: the heat sink as a 3D solid, cooled by air on every face. Natural frequencies of 3D solids - Solve › Natural Frequencies now works for 3D solids, extruded or revolved, with consistent masses: the lowest frequencies are listed under the 3D view and each mode swings on the part's surface. Six frequencies of the 3D L-bracket (18 000 unknowns) take about 2 s.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.4 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.3.4 — 2026-10-30. - Help › Verification: 131 checks, all passing. New: benchmark 19, a wall with fixed face temperatures (exact), a pipe wall revolved a quarter turn (temperature and heat flow within 0.001 %), a pin fin cooled by air against the fin equation (0.03 %), a slab heating itself (exact), and three vibrations: a bar's axial frequency (exact to 10⁻⁸), a 3D cantilever's bending frequency (0.03 %) and a revolved shaft's (0.1 %). - Random 3D solids, extruded and revolved, now also conduct heat (their heat always balances) and vibrate (their frequencies positive and rising), or say why they cannot.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.3 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.3.3 — 2026-10-30. Frames for everyday structural analysis: load cases and combinations, hinges, steel section tables. Load cases and combinations - Loads › Cases and Combinations: name load cases (dead, imposed, wind, …) and build combinations of them, each case times your own factor. The loads already drawn go into the first case. - Pick a case or a combination on the Loads tab: only its loads are drawn, new loads go into the picked case, and Solve (and Buckling) solve it. The legend says which one the results are for. A load's case can be changed in the Inspector. - Results › Envelope: every combination solved in turn, with each member's largest and smallest axial force, its largest shear, moment, twisting and deflection, its largest utilisation and the combination that gives it, and the range of every reaction. - Datum Mesh does not apply a design code: the factors are yours. - A beam can have a hinge at either end (Inspector): it carries no bending moment there, as in a pinned beam-to-column connection. In 3D both bending moments are released; twisting is still carried, unless no rigid beam holds the node (a ball joint). Hinges act in the static solve, natural frequencies and buckling, and are drawn as small circles. Steel section tables

heading: Changelog › 0.3.3 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.3.3 — 2026-10-30. - Sections › From the tables: European rolled IPE, HEA and HEB sections (56 sizes, EN 10365 nominal dimensions). Their properties are worked out from the dimensions with the root fillets (a new root radius for I-sections), and agree with the tables. Examples and fixes - New example: a two-storey braced steel frame with HEB columns, IPE beams pinned at their ends, a braced bay, three load cases and three combinations. - Escape closes a dialog left open under one that has just closed (focus was lost). - Help › Verification: 120 checks, all passing. New: benchmark 18, a beam hinged at both ends between fixed supports (simply supported: wL²/8, 5wL⁴/384EI, its natural frequency and, as a column, π²EI/L²), a beam with a hinge partway (statics), a 3D beam hinged both ways, a combination 1.35 G + 1.5 Q and its envelope against superposition, and the tables' second moments (IPE 300, HEA 200, HEB 200, within 0.01 %) and areas (all 56 within 0.5 %). - Random frames now have hinges, and random load cases always add up: a combination's results equal its cases' results times their factors, in 2D and 3D.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.2 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.3.2 — 2026-10-30. Revolved 3D solids, a cutting plane through the results, and faces picked in 3D. - A 3D solid can now be revolved about the y axis instead of extruded (Inspector, with nothing selected): shafts, hubs, discs and vessels from their half-section, drawn right of the axis. - Turn it a full 360°, or a sector (90°, say) with symmetry on its two cut faces, which are then the back and front faces. The section can reach the axis: the part is solid through its middle. - New example: the pressure vessel revolved a quarter turn. - Held directions: hold only x, y or z of a face (Loads › Hold Directions, or a support's Inspector). - A support can be a line along a face at any fraction of the way through (Inspector › Where), as NAFEMS LE10 asks for. - Click a face in the 3D view to put the support or load picked on it: a side face, or the back or front face. - Cutting plane: once solved, cut across x, y or z (under the view) and slide the plane through the part; the inside is coloured by the result shown.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.2 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.3.2 — 2026-10-30. - Help › Verification: 105 checks, all passing. New: benchmark 17, a closed-end thick cylinder revolved a quarter turn and a full turn against Lamé (hoop stress 0.2 %, axial 0.7 %, bore movement 0.007 %), a round bar through the axis squeezed end to end (exact to 1 part in 10¹³), and NAFEMS LE10, the thick plate under pressure (σyy at D within 1.4 % of −5.38 MPa). - Random 3D solids now include revolved ones (some through the axis, some a full turn), held directions and line supports: all 60 solve with their reactions balancing the loads, or say why they cannot.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.1 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.3.1 — 2026-10-30. Sketch tools: shape a part's section with rounds, bevels, cut-outs and patterns before it is solved. Sketch tools (Geometry, and Format on a selected shape) - Round Corners (fillet) and Bevel Corners (chamfer): any corner between two straight edges, one or all at once, at a typed radius or distance. ⌒ in the Inspector's corner table rounds just that corner. - Union, Subtract and Intersect two shapes: click one, Shift+click the other. Arcs and circles stay true arcs and circles, so a support or load on a round edge is still on one edge. Rings left inside become holes. Supports and loads move to the edges they lie on, and an outline keeps its edge numbers where it can. - Ready-made Slot, Rounded Rectangle and Regular Polygon from typed sizes, as a shape or a hole. - Offset an outline in or out (a wall of a given thickness, a clearance round a hole); arcs keep their centres. - Linear and Circular Patterns: copies of shapes in a row or round a centre (bolt circles), with the supports and loads on their edges. - Every tool is one step to undo, and is in Tell Me (Ctrl+K).

heading: Changelog › 0.3.1 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.3.1 — 2026-10-30. - Help › Verification: 94 checks, all passing. New: benchmark 16, the areas of eight shapes made by the sketch tools against hand formulas (to 1 part in 10⁹), and the plate with a hole again, its hole cut by Subtract, giving the same stress concentration of 3.0. - Random pairs of shapes (60 of them, circles, rectangles, slots and rounded rectangles) are combined all three ways: the areas always add up (union plus intersection equals the two shapes), and every result passes the model's checks and meshes.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.0 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.3.0 — 2026-10-29. 3D solids: a part's outline extruded by its thickness and solved in 3D. - Home › 3D Solid: draw the outline and holes in Section, exactly as for a plane part, and set the thickness; the part is extruded along z and shown in the 3D view. - Supports and loads go on faces: an edge in Section stands for its side face, and the back and front faces have their own buttons while a support or load is being placed. Fixed, roller and symmetry supports; pressures, face forces (now with Fz too) and gravity. - The section's mesh is swept through the thickness in layers of wedges: 18-node wedges from the quadratic mesh (accurate), 6-node from the linear one. Layers are automatic, or set in the Inspector. - Once solved, the surface is coloured by any of 14 results (von Mises, σ1, σ3, each stress and shear, the displacements, the safety factor) on the deformed shape; hover to read a value. The Results page and report give the largest and smallest values anywhere inside, with where, the reactions and the equilibrium check in six sums. - New examples: the L-bracket as a 3D solid, and a blank 3D solid.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.0 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.3.0 — 2026-10-29. - The sparse solver now uses every core of the computer, and big 3D models store half the matrix: about 90 000 unknowns of a 3D solid solve in about 6 s and 1.2 GB on four cores. - A 3D solid is limited to 200 000 unknowns, with a message saying how to make the mesh coarser, so a too-fine mesh cannot run the computer out of memory. - Help › Verification: 85 checks, all passing. New: a 3D patch test (a uniform stress reproduced to 1 part in 10¹⁴, with the thinning), a 3D cantilever against Timoshenko beam theory (0.005 %) and its bending stress, and a thick cylinder in 3D against Lamé (hoop stress 0.5 %, bore movement 0.003 %). - Random 3D solids (40 of them) solve with their reactions balancing the loads in all six sums, or say why they cannot.

heading: Changelog › 0.2.6 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.2.6 — 2026-10-29. 3D frames vibrate and buckle; the app starts lighter and keeps to size and speed budgets. - Solve › Natural Frequencies and Buckling now work for 3D frames: beams bend both ways and twist as they vibrate, and buckle by bending about either axis. The shapes swing in the 3D view; the lists, tables and printed report are as for plane frames. - Truss bars in compression are checked on their own about their weaker axis. - Buckling in 3D is by bending only: twisting and lateral-torsional buckling of open sections (I, channel) are not checked yet, and the Results page says so. Lighter and quicker - The 3D view's code loads only when a 3D frame is shown: the window starts with a third of the code it had (282 kB, was 863 kB). - The fonts are bundled once, not twice (the window is 1.1 MB, was 1.2 MB). - Size budgets checked on every build: the installer stays under 5 MB, the window's startup code under 400 kB. - Solve times are in the verification record: the examples solve in milliseconds, a fine mesh of 141 000 unknowns in about 1.5 s, and six frequencies of a 12-storey 3D building frame (147 000 unknowns) in about 2.3 s.

heading: Changelog › 0.2.6 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.2.6 — 2026-10-29. - Help › Verification: 76 checks, all passing. New: a 3D cantilever's frequencies across its width, across its depth and in twisting; a column buckling about its weak and then its strong axis; and the portal frame in 3D, whose plane frequencies and buckling factors are found again to 1 part in 10¹².

heading: Changelog › 0.2.4 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.2.4 — 2026-10-29. 3D frames: frames and trusses in space, drawn on planes and seen in 3D. - Home › 3D Frame: beams that stretch, twist and bend about both axes of their section, and truss bars, anywhere in space. y is up and z is depth. - Members are drawn on a working plane: Front (x-y), Side (z-y) or Plan (x-z), at a depth you pick or type; members off the plane are shown faint. The status bar reads x, y and z. - The 3D view shows the whole frame with its supports and loads: turn it with the left button, pan with the right, zoom with the wheel; Front, Top and Iso buttons. Click nodes and members to select them, or to put supports and loads on them. - Geometry › Repeat copies the selected members (or the whole frame) a step along any direction, with their supports and loads, and joins the copies with beams or truss bars: draw one frame, repeat it into bays. - The Inspector takes z for nodes, Fz and moments about x, y and z, member loads along z, gravity in z, springs in all six directions, and the roll of a beam's section about its axis.

heading: Changelog › 0.2.4 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.2.4 — 2026-10-29. - Sections give the second moment about the other axis and the torsion constant J (thin-walled formulas for boxes, I and channel sections; your own values for custom sections). Results in 3D - Once solved, the members are drawn on their deflected shape and coloured by utilisation, axial force, torque, either bending moment, shear or deflection, with a colour scale. Hover a member to read N, Vy, Vz, T, Mz, My and the deflection. - The Results page and the printed report have six sums in the equilibrium check, six reactions per support and every member's forces; the report draws the frame isometric. - Help › Verification: 69 checks, all passing. New: a 3D cantilever bending each way, twisting and with its section rolled, under point and member loads; one along z; an L-shaped cantilever bent in plan, where bending and twisting add up; a tripod of truss bars; and the portal frame solved in 3D, giving the plane solver's answers to 1 part in 10¹³. - Random 3D frames (150 of them) solve with their reactions balancing the loads, or say why they cannot. Not yet in 3D: natural frequencies and buckling (plane frames have both).

heading: Changelog › 0.2.3 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.2.3 — 2026-10-29. Buckling of frames: how far the loads can grow before a frame buckles. - Solve › Buckling: the six lowest load factors of a frame or truss and their buckled shapes. Every load on the model, self-weight and warming included, times the load factor buckles it. - The axial forces come from a static solve first; members in compression soften the frame until it buckles. Beams are cut into eight pieces each, so a column drawn as one member buckles as it should. - Truss bars in compression are also checked on their own as pinned struts (π²EI/L²), weakest first, and the bar that buckles before the frame is named. - The load factors are listed on the Results page and in the printed report; a factor below 1 is flagged. Better natural frequencies - Beams are cut into eight pieces for natural frequencies too, so higher modes of frames drawn with few members are now accurate. - Help › Verification: 54 checks, all passing. New: Euler's buckling loads for a column held four ways (pinned, flagpole, fixed and pinned, fixed at both ends) and its second mode, all within 0.05 %; a column held at both ends and warmed; a truss bar checked as a strut.

heading: Changelog › 0.2.2 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.2.2 — 2026-10-29. Natural frequencies: how frames and parts vibrate on their own. - Solve › Natural Frequencies: the six lowest frequencies and their mode shapes, for frames and trusses and for parts in plane stress, plane strain or axisymmetric. - Pick a mode under the canvas to see it move; a frame bends along each member, a part deforms and is coloured by how far it moves. Back to the static results with one click. - Masses come from each material's density (consistent masses: beams, truss bars and triangles); the supports hold the model as for a static solve. A model free to float away, or without density, says so. - The frequencies, periods and ω are listed on the Results page and in the printed report. - Help › Verification: 47 checks, all passing. New: the first three frequencies of a cantilever and of a simply supported beam against beam theory (within 0.05 %), and a plate strip's bending (0.16 % below beam theory, as shear and rotary inertia make it) and stretching frequencies. - The solver is checked against the exact frequencies of a chain of masses and springs, to one part in a billion. - A part's fill no longer covers its mode shape (found in the app).

heading: Changelog › 0.2.1 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.2.1 — 2026-10-29. Axisymmetric solids: pressure vessels, shafts, discs and nozzles solved from their half-section. - Home › Axisymmetric: draw the half-section to the right of the y axis; it is turned a full circle about it. The canvas shows the axis. - Results named as engineers read them: radial, axial and hoop stress (σr, σz, σθ), radial and axial displacement, von Mises, principal stresses and the safety factor. - Points on the axis are held from moving off it by themselves. Loads and reactions are totals for the full circle; the equilibrium check sums the forces along the axis. - Thermal stress works here too: temperatures are solved round the axis, then the stress. - A new worked example, Pressure vessel: a cylinder with a hemispherical head under 2 MPa. The hoop stress in the cylinder agrees with pr/t. - Help › Verification: 39 checks, all passing. New: a long thick cylinder (Lamé) and a thick hollow sphere under pressure (hoop stress and growth of the bore), each on three meshes with the error falling; a round bar pulled along its axis and a free tube warmed evenly, both exact. - The automatic element size is finer for thin parts (about 800 triangles over the part), so a thin wall gets several elements through it instead of one.

heading: Changelog › 0.2.0 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.2.0 — 2026-10-29. Thermal stress: parts and frames that are warmed or cooled push on what holds them. The first release on the way to 3D (see the roadmap). - Temperature Change (Loads tab): the whole model warms or cools by the same amount from its stress-free temperature (20 °C unless you change it, in the Inspector with nothing selected). - In a part, hold edges at temperatures and add convection: Solve finds the temperatures first, on the same mesh, then the stress. Temperature appears among the results, beside the stresses. - Frame members grow by αΔT per length; where they cannot, they push on their supports. - Plane strain holds the length along the body, as it should: σz = ν(σx + σy) − EαΔT. - A new worked example, Heated plate: a steel plate with a hole, fixed at a cool wall and heated at its other edge. - Help › Verification: 32 checks, all passing. New: a bar held at both ends and warmed (σ = −EαΔT), a block held on every side in plane strain (σ = −EαΔT/(1 − 2ν)), a free plate with a temperature varying in a straight line through it (no stress at all), and a beam fixed at both ends and warmed (N = −EAαΔT).

heading: Changelog › 0.2.0 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.2.0 — 2026-10-29. - A part held only by a roller on one curved edge can turn about the edge's centre; it now says the supports barely hold it, instead of giving numbers without a warning. Found by the random-model tests. - Where a round hole crosses a round outline, a tiny triangle could fold inside out; it no longer does. Found by the random-model tests. - Labels of the largest and smallest values near the right edge of the canvas no longer run off it.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.4 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.1.4 — 2026-10-29. Polish: large parts open faster, a pin load for lugs and clevises, members joined where they cross when you ask, and the small problems left over from the 0.1.1 review. Loads and drawing - Pin load: a pin or bolt pulling on the part through a hole. It presses only on the side of the hole it pushes into, most in line with the force, and the part carries exactly the force you give. The lifting lug example now uses it. - Join Where They Cross (Format tab): select members that cross and join them with a node at each crossing; loads along them are split there. Crossing members are otherwise left apart, as X-bracing usually is. - Dragging lands what you grab on the grid, even if it started off the grid. - Load arrows and edge loads move with their node or shape while you drag it. - Results of large parts reach the window about three times smaller: a 25 000-element part sends 6 MB instead of 22 MB. Values keep seven significant digits; the sums behind the equilibrium check keep full precision. - Saving writes a temporary file and then swaps it in, so a crash or a full disk never leaves a half-written model. - Undoing back to the saved model clears the "changed" mark.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.4 — 2026-10-29

heading: Changelog › 0.1.3 — 2026-10-28

Parts are meshed and solved: plane stress, plane strain and steady heat conduction, with stress and temperature contours, a probe, the deformed shape, a materials library and a printed results report. Help › Verification now covers every benchmark in the plan. - Solve (F5) splits a part into triangles automatically, keeping their angles above a minimum (25° by default) and holes and fillets round. - Element size: automatic, coarser or finer (Mesh tab, or type it in the Inspector). Refine Near: click an edge or a point to make the elements a quarter of the size there; they grow back gradually into the rest of the part. - Quadratic 6-node triangles (accurate, the default) or linear 3-node triangles. - The Mesh view shows the triangles coloured by quality (smallest angle), with the numbers of elements and nodes, the smallest angle and the worst aspect ratio. - Plane stress (thin plates, with a thickness) and plane strain (long bodies). - Supports on edges and points: fixed, pinned, roller (sliding along the edge, also on sloping and curved edges) and symmetry. - Loads: pressure on edges, edge forces (the whole force or per length), point forces, and gravity from each material's density. - Heat conduction: fixed temperatures, heat flux, convection to a fluid and heat generated inside; temperatures and heat flux.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.3 — 2026-10-28
text: Changelog › 0.1.3 — 2026-10-28. - The printed report and the new Report view now include, for parts, the mesh and its quality, contour pictures with their scales, the largest and smallest values, the reactions or heat flows and the equilibrium check. - Help › Verification: 27 checks, all passing. New: a plate with a hole (stress concentration 3.0, Kirsch), a thick cylinder under pressure (Lamé), NAFEMS LE1 (the elliptic membrane, 92.7 MPa), a plane wall and a fin cooled by convection, and patch tests for 3- and 6-node triangles in stress, strain and heat. heading: Changelog › 0.1.2 — 2026-10-28
text: Changelog › 0.1.2 — 2026-10-28. A fixes release: thirteen problems found by reviewing and using 0.1.1, each now covered by a test. Results you can trust on screen - The moment, shear and axial diagrams and the utilisation colours now follow when you pan or zoom; before, they could stay behind, away from their members. - The equilibrium check compares against the size of the loads, so loads that cancel out (a moment on its own, a balanced pair of forces) no longer report a huge imbalance, and the moments are now checked as well as the forces. - A model with no loads says so, instead of drawing a meaningless deflected shape. - A load on a node that no member reaches is named in a warning instead of being dropped silently. - Rounding noise such as 1.5e-14 kN·m is shown as 0. - Members divided into many short pieces (a beam in 1 000 parts) are no longer mistaken for a mechanism, and they solve to full accuracy. - A member drawn to the middle of another now joins it there: the member is split, and loads along it are split with it. Before, the two crossed without touching.

heading: Datum Mesh: notes for Claude
text: Datum Mesh: notes for Claude. Read docs/VISION.md and docs/MEMORY.md first. The vision (2026-10-31): one open-source platform for structural and finite-element analysis, our own solver; one engine of a core and modules, organised in analysis steps; the structures side (0.4.x) first, then nonlinear and dynamic solids (0.5+). It is the project's memory: architecture, decisions, roadmap, and a log of every session. The family design guide is FAMILY.md in Edgar-Mendonca/Datum (read-only from here; docs/FAMILY.md links to it). The brief this app started from is briefs/DATUM-MESH.md in the same hub repo. At the end of every session that changes anything, update docs/MEMORY.md: - tick the roadmap - add a session-log entry - record any new decisions - refresh the architecture section if files moved - Rust and Tauri 2, small and efficient code, Windows first. The same look, ribbon, help, printing and updater as every Datum app (FAMILY §2–9); copy from Datum Plan (and Datum Sim, Plan's skeleton for a canvas app) rather than reinventing. - Ship in small numbered releases (0.1.0, 0.1.1, …). Every release appears in the in-app updater. - Engine logic belongs in crates/core (pure Rust, unit-tested), not in the UI. The window never calculates results.

heading: Datum Mesh: notes for Claude
text: Datum Mesh: notes for Claude. - Our own solver: write the mechanics from published methods (Bathe's *Finite Element Procedures*, Simo and Hughes, Newmark/HHT, Crisfield); never port another program's code, even if permissive. Outside code only as infrastructure (faer, METIS). - Modules plug into the core through its small interface (element: stiffness, internal force, mass; material: stress and tangent) and carry their own benchmarks; keep them independent. - The program is the Datum window: SolidJS in ui/, Tauri in src-tauri/ (0.7.0's egui program in app/ was withdrawn in 0.7.1). SolidCraft's crates in app/ are used headless as the geometry engine (crates/cad) and for Gmsh meshing (app/crates/analysis); read app/AGENTS.md before changing them. - The engine and the .dmesh file use SI base units (m, N, Pa, K, W); the window converts for display only (ui/src/units.ts). - Public words (the repo is public: README, CHANGELOG, NOTICE, site.json, help, the window, docs, this file, code comments): never name, compare with, or say the app copies, combines or targets a commercial product (FAMILY §13); no "…-style" or "as … does" comparisons. File-format names only where they name a file the app reads or writes. Open solvers and benchmark sets (CalculiX, Gmsh, NAFEMS) may be named. The names are listed in tools/commercial-names.txt; hardening::public_words_name_no_commercial_product and two window checks enforce it.

heading: Datum Mesh: notes for Claude
text: Datum Mesh: notes for Claude. - Licences: MIT/BSD/Apache/MPL only in the app (check app/ with cargo deny --manifest-path app/Cargo.toml check). GPL solvers and meshers (Gmsh, bundled from 0.7.0) only ever run as separate programs. Record every dependency in NOTICE. Quality bar (brief §5): - Every element and solver path has a test against a known answer; each is a line of the verification report (crates/core/src/bench.rs, written to docs/verification/ and shown in Help › Verification). - Never cut the benchmarks, the equilibrium check or the report. - Report only checks that actually ran; say what was not verified. Checks before pushing: - cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings - cargo test --workspace (includes the hardening tests and the benchmarks) - npm run check:ui, then npm run test:ui (dumps the engine fixture, builds the window, runs the Playwright checks) - cargo deny check (licences, advisories, sources; CI runs it) - The program: cd app && cargo clippy -p datum-analysis -p solidcraft-ui-egui --no-deps -- -D warnings (--no-deps: the inherited crates follow upstream's lints), cargo test -p datum-analysis, and a driven run under Xvfb (--control PORT; docs/MEMORY.md §1) - A change you can see: check it in the real app (cargo build -p datum-mesh && tests_ui/realapp.sh steps.sh shots/) and add a UI check for every bug

heading: Contributing › How the code is laid out
text: Contributing › How the code is laid out. - crates/core: the engine in pure Rust: the model and its edits, sections, meshing, elements, the solver, results and the verification benchmarks. All calculation lives here, with tests. - src-tauri: the desktop shell (commands, files, options, recovery, the updater). - ui/src: the window (SolidJS + TypeScript). It shows what the engine computes and sends edits back as operations. - docs/MEMORY.md: architecture, decisions, roadmap and a log of every session. Read it first.

heading: Contributing › Before you send a change
text: Contributing › Before you send a change. Keep code compact and in the style around it. A new element or solver path comes with a test against a known answer; a new window feature with a UI test where it can. Never link GPL, LGPL or AGPL code into the app. By contributing you agree your work is released under the MIT licence.

Finite-element analysis on the desktop: stresses, deflections and temperatures in parts and frames. Purpose: To show any engineer or student how a part or structure carries load, heat and vibration (where it is stressed, how far it moves, how hot it gets) in a free app they can trust because it proves its own answers. Draw a frame of beams and truss bars, or the outline of a part with its holes; put on the supports and loads; solve, and see the deflections, stresses and temperatures. Datum Mesh is for mechanical, structural, process and aerospace engineers, students and lecturers. It is free and open source (MIT), Windows first, installs in seconds and updates itself. More on the family site: edgar-mendonca.github.io/Datum/apps/mesh.

heading: What it does
text: What it does. - Frames and trusses, solved: draw beams and truss bars on a grid, put on supports and loads, press Solve (F5). See the deflected shape, the moment, shear and axial diagrams, the reactions, stresses and utilisation; hover a member to read the values there. - Plasticity: parts that yield (von Mises with hardening), in increments up to collapse, with plastic strain contours and the load–deflection curve. - Parts, meshed and solved: plane stress, plane strain, axisymmetric solids (vessels, shafts), steady heat conduction and thermal stress on automatic triangle meshes (6-node by default), finer where you ask. Contours of von Mises and principal stress, displacement, safety factor, temperature and heat flux; the deformed shape; hover anywhere to read the values. - Natural frequencies and mode shapes of frames and parts, moving on screen. - Buckling of frames: load factors and buckled shapes, with every squeezed truss bar checked as a strut. - Large deflection and P-delta: plane and 3D frames solved in steps in their deflected shape (large rotations in space for 3D frames), by Newton increments or by arc length past the limit load (snap-through), with the load–deflection curve.

heading: What it does
text: What it does. - 3D solids: a part's section extruded by its thickness or revolved about an axis (shafts, hubs, vessels), solved in 3D for stress, natural frequencies or heat conduction, coloured in a 3D view, with a cutting plane to see inside; faces picked by clicking them. - 3D frames and trusses: drawn on front, side and plan planes, repeated into bays, seen in a 3D view and coloured by their results, with natural frequencies and buckling. - Structural details: tension-only and compression-only members (bracing, cables), support settlement, rigid floors, rigid end zones at joints, and second order (P-delta) in 3D frames. - Dynamics: response spectrum (CQC or SRSS) and time history (Newmark) for frames and plates, with point masses; the modes' share of the mass, and the motion over time. - Plates and shells: slabs, walls and panels drawn on those planes, joined to the beams, coloured by stress, moments or deflection in 3D, and vibrating with the frame.

heading: What it does
text: What it does. - The equilibrium check after every solve (the heat balance for heat models), and Help › Verification: 192 benchmark checks with known answers solved in front of you, from beam theory, Euler columns and 3D frames to the plate with a hole, the thick cylinder, NAFEMS LE1 and LE10, conduction through a fin and the NAFEMS large-deflection beams (NL5 to NL7), plates against Navier's series and the Scordelis–Lo roof and pinched cylinder, dynamics against the closed forms of one and two masses, plasticity against Hill's limit analysis, with mesh convergence. - Materials from Datum Atlas (54 metals and plastics), each with its source. - Sections (rectangle, round bar, tube, box, I, channel, angle, or your own values) with their properties worked out, and European steel tables (IPE, HEA, HEB). - Load cases and combinations with your own factors, an envelope of every member's forces over all combinations, and hinged member ends. - DXF: import a section drawn in CAD (outlines, arcs and holes) and export one back.

heading: What it does
text: What it does. - Drawing parts: rectangles, circles and polygons with arc edges, and holes; slots, rounded rectangles and regular polygons; rounded and bevelled corners; union, subtract and intersect with arcs kept true; offsets and patterns of holes; supports and loads on edges and points, including a pin load that bears on one side of a hole. - Units: SI (mm, kN, MPa) or US (in, kip, ksi); files keep SI. - Worked examples: a portal frame, a roof truss, a braced steel frame with load cases, a snap-through frame, a steel platform in 3D, a floor slab on columns, a frame and a 3D building in an earthquake, tension-only bracing, a thick tube yielding, a lifting lug, an L-bracket with a fillet, a flange plate, a heat sink (also in 3D), a pressure vessel (also revolved in 3D) and a heated plate. - Print to PDF: the model with a title block and a report with the mesh, contour pictures, the largest values, reactions and the equilibrium check; a ? card beside every tool, light and dark themes, recovery of unsaved work, updates from inside the app. Release ; What arrives ; 0.4.3 ; Large deflection in 3D frames, tension-only members, settlements, offsets, rigid floors ; 0.5–0.7 ; Plasticity and rubber, tetrahedra and mesh import, implicit and explicit dynamics, contact ;

heading: Datum Mesh: project memory › Vision (agreed 2026-10-31): read docs/VISION.md
text: Datum Mesh: project memory › Vision (agreed 2026-10-31): read docs/VISION.md. One open-source platform for structural and finite-element analysis, written by us, that proves its own answers. Frames, plates and shells, solids, heat and vibration in one model; linear and nonlinear, static and dynamic, in one engine; small and simple however much it grows. Its scope: structural frame analysis (frames, plates, load cases, P-delta, dynamics; no design codes), nonlinear finite elements (large deflection, plasticity, rubber, contact) and, in time, general and explicit dynamics (steps, impact). It aims at a workflow an experienced analyst finds natural: model, steps, loads, solve, results, in that order. - One engine: a core and modules (core: model, steps, sets, assembly, solvers, Newton/arc-length and time loops, results; modules: frames, plates, solids, materials, heat, contact; bench). Every analysis is a sequence of steps on one model. Modules plug in through a small fixed interface and carry their own benchmarks. - Our own solver: mechanics written from published methods (Bathe's *Finite Element Procedures*, Simo and Hughes, Newmark/HHT, Crisfield); no porting of other programs' code. Outside code only as infrastructure (faer, METIS). GPL tools only as separate optional add-ons. - Order: finish the frames-and-structures side on the new core first (0.4.0 core + P-delta/large-deflection frames, 0.4.1 plates and shells, 0.4.2 dynamics, 0.4.3 structural details), then nonlinear and dynamic solids (0.5–0.7).

heading: Datum Mesh: project memory › Purpose (agreed 2026-10-29; kept, and widened by the vision above)
text: Datum Mesh: project memory › Purpose (agreed 2026-10-29; kept, and widened by the vision above). To show any engineer or student how a part or structure carries load, heat and vibration (where it is stressed, how far it moves, how hot it gets) in a free app they can trust because it proves its own answers. - For: mechanical, aerospace and process engineers checking parts (brackets, lugs, vessels, shafts, heat sinks); students and lecturers learning FEA; small firms without a commercial licence. - Different because: trust you can see (benchmarks solved in the app, the equilibrium check, saying what was not verified); free and open (MIT, no licence server); simple (draw, load, solve, read); honest about its limits. - Frames stay in Datum Mesh (2D and 3D frames and trusses, with frequencies and buckling): they carry the parts engineers check and teach FEA well. They do not grow into building design: no design-code checks or code load combinations. - Not: a design-code checker, a CAD program, or a whole commercial suite on day one. - In the spirit of (agreed 2026-10-30): the analysis side of a structural program for frames, and a general finite-element program for parts; not CAD, not a pre-processor for other solvers. Simple parts are drawn here (2D sketch tools, extrude, revolve); complex ones come from real CAD as STEP (0.4). Plan: docs/PLAN-0.3-0.4.md.
