Tees, reducers, valves and flanged joints, springs, guides, line stops, skewed restraints, constant-force supports and imposed settlements each have a hand-worked case: a spring under a cantilever, a settling anchor, a valve's weight, a tapering reducer, a welding tee's intensification, a nozzle's loads in its own axes, the liberal allowable and the cycle factor. heading: Changelog › 0.1.1 — 2026-10-28

heading: Datum Pipe: notes for Claude
text: Datum Pipe: notes for Claude. Read docs/MEMORY.md first. It is the project's memory: architecture, decisions, roadmap, and a log of every session. The family design guide is FAMILY.md in Edgar-Mendonca/Datum (read-only from here; docs/FAMILY.md links to it). The brief this app started from is briefs/DATUM-PIPE.md in the same hub repo. At the end of every session that changes anything, update docs/MEMORY.md: - tick the roadmap - add a session-log entry - record any new decisions - refresh the architecture section if files moved - Rust and Tauri 2, small and efficient code, Windows first. The same look, ribbon, help, printing and updater as every Datum app (FAMILY §2–9); copy from Datum Plan (and Datum Mesh, the closest app: solver crate, verification, canvas window) rather than reinventing. - Ship in small numbered releases (0.1.0, 0.1.1, …). Every release appears in the in-app updater. - Engine logic belongs in crates/core (pure Rust, unit-tested), not in the UI. The window never calculates results. - The UI is SolidJS + Vite in ui/src/*.tsx (built to ui/dist). State lives in ui/src/store.ts. The 3D view uses three.js (MIT). - The engine and the .dpipe file use SI base units (m, kg, N, Pa, K). heading: Datum Pipe: notes for Claude
text: Datum Pipe: notes for Claude. - Public words (README, CHANGELOG, site.json, help, commits): never name, compare with, or say the app copies or replaces any commercial piping software (FAMILY §13). Standards may be named by number. Say "calculates using the equations of"; never "certified" or "compliant". - Codes: implement the published equations only; never reproduce copyrighted tables or text. Allowable stresses are user inputs, pre-filled with typical values and marked "check against your code edition". - Licences: MIT/BSD/Apache/MPL only. Record every dependency in NOTICE. Quality bar (brief §4): - Every element and solver path has a test against a known answer; each is a line of Help › Verification (crates/core/src/bench.rs, generated from the tests so it is always true for the version running). - Never cut the benchmarks, the equilibrium check, the code checks or the report. - Report only checks that actually ran; say what was not verified. Checks before pushing: - cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings - cargo test --workspace (includes the hardening tests and the benchmarks) - npm run check:ui, then npm run test:ui (dumps the engine fixture, builds the window, runs the Playwright checks; set NODE_PATH=$(npm root -g) if Playwright is installed globally) - cargo deny check (licences, advisories, sources; CI runs it)

text: Contributing › How the code is laid out. - crates/core: the engine in pure Rust: the piping model and its edits, the pipe library, units, the 3D pipe element solver, load cases, code checks, the isometric and the verification benchmarks. All calculation lives here, with tests. - src-tauri: the desktop shell (commands, files, options, recovery, the updater). - ui/src: the window (SolidJS + TypeScript). It shows what the engine computes and sends edits back as operations. - docs/MEMORY.md: architecture, decisions, roadmap and a log of every session. Read it first.

Pipe stress analysis on the desktop: displacements, support loads, nozzle loads and code stresses, with an automatic isometric. Route a piping system in a table, the way a stress engineer marks up an isometric (or import a piping component file); put on its supports, temperatures, pressures, wind and seismic loads; and Datum Pipe works out the displacements, support loads, equipment nozzle loads and code stresses, shows them on the 3D model and on an isometric drawing, and prints a stress report. It is for piping, stress, mechanical, process and plant engineers, consultants and students. It is free and open source (MIT), Windows first, installs in seconds and updates itself. More on the family site: edgar-mendonca.github.io/Datum/apps/pipe. Results must be checked by a qualified engineer. Datum Pipe is a tool to help engineers. Before its results are used for design, fabrication or approval, a qualified engineer must check them against the edition of the code that applies to the project.

heading: What it does
text: What it does. - An element table that draws as you type: From node, To node, DX, DY, DZ, pipe, material, line conditions and component, with values in any unit (20 ft, 150 mm). Node numbers step by 10; new rows copy the row above. Analysis runs again after every edit, and right-click menus in the 3D view add supports and change components. - Pipe data: nominal sizes ½" to 24" in every schedule, your own sizes, corrosion allowance, mill tolerance, insulation, cladding and contents; carbon, low-alloy, stainless 304 and 316 and duplex steels with modulus and expansion against temperature and their sources. - Components: long and short radius bends or your own radius, welding, fabricated and reinforced tees, concentric reducers, valves and flanged joints with their weight, and bellows expansion joints with the maker's rates and their pressure thrust. - Supports: anchors, one-way rests the pipe can lift off, guides, line stops, restraints in any direction (rests, guides, line stops and restraints with gaps and friction), springs, spring hangers sized from your spring table, constant-force supports, nozzle points with the vessel or tank wall's flexibility, and imposed equipment movements.

heading: What it does
text: What it does. - Load cases built for you: sustained, operating, expansion range and hydrotest, editable; wind (one pressure or by height), static seismic and relief valve thrust as occasional cases, wind and seismic in both directions if you choose. - Code stresses: by the process piping code, the power piping code or the European piping standard's equations: hoop stress and minimum wall, sustained longitudinal stress, the displacement stress range and occasional stress (with your occasional factor), PASS or FAIL at every point. - Cold spring and buried pipe: straight pipe made short and pulled together at installation, with its installed case; buried pipe held by soil springs along it from the soil's properties, elastic then yielding, with the soil's load at every point. - Results: displacements, forces and moments, support loads for the civil team, nozzle loads in the nozzle's axes, steam turbine, compressor and pump nozzle checks against their standards' published criteria (coefficients and pump table values are your inputs), flange leakage by the equivalent pressure method, and an equilibrium check after every solve.

heading: What it does
text: What it does. - Pressure vessels: vertical and horizontal vessels with heads, shell courses and cones: thickness for pressure with the liquid's static head, MAWP and MAP, nozzle reinforcement by area replacement, horizontal vessels on two saddles by Zick's method, vertical vessels on a skirt in wind and seismic with their anchor bolts and base ring, bolted flanges and covers, lifting lugs, trunnions and legs, the piping's loads checked on the vessel's nozzles, and external pressure with stiffening rings, hydrotest pressure, volume and weights, drawn to scale and in the report. - Dynamics: natural frequencies and mode shapes with the mass each mode moves, each mode animated in the 3D view; a response spectrum on the modes (CQC), checked as an occasional load; a harmonic load at a frequency, with damping. - Isometric and report: an automatic 30° isometric with dimensions, symbols and result tags (print or SVG), and a printed stress report with the title block, input echo, stress summary, support and nozzle loads, the isometric and the equilibrium checks. - Import and export: plain-text piping component files (.pcf) from design tools, as a new model, and the model's geometry back out as one. - Editing tools: an expansion loop wizard, copy and mirror a section, insert a node, renumber, undo and redo everything.

heading: What it does
text: What it does. - Verified: Help › Verification solves benchmark problems with known answers in front of you: beam theory, heated L-bends, Z-bends and an expansion loop against the flexibility method by hand, a bend's flexibility, the minimum wall equation on straight pipe and at a bend's intrados, pressure elongation, a tee branch's effective section modulus, a one-way rest lifting off, a gap closing, friction sliding and sticking, wind and static seismic on a cantilever and the occasional stress, a spring hanger sized by hand, a steam turbine's nozzle criteria, a flange's equivalent pressure, a relief valve's thrust, and the equilibrium of every example. - Worked examples: a pump discharge with an expansion loop, a compressor suction line, a steam line on a pipe rack (one-way rests, friction, gapped guides, wind and seismic), a tank outlet with settlement and a sized spring hanger, a safety valve vent stack, an expansion joint between anchors, a vertical separator with its inlet line and a horizontal drum on saddles at full vacuum, boiler steam to a header on the power piping code, a buried hot water line, and an L-bend and a Z-bend to check by hand. ; The isometric, drawn from the table ; Code stresses at every point ; The stress report, ready to print or save as PDF ;

heading: What it does › About the code checks
text: What it does › About the code checks. Datum Pipe calculates stresses using the published equations of ASME B31.3 (Process Piping) or, when chosen, ASME B31.1 (Power Piping) or EN 13480-3 (Metallic industrial piping). It does not contain the text, tables or figures of the standard. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by ASME or CEN. The equations come from openly published engineering work: Barlow's thin-wall pressure formula and Lamé's thick-cylinder solution, the membrane theory of a torus for the wall of a bend, von Kármán's and Clark and Reissner's theory of curved tubes, A. R. C. Markl's fatigue tests of piping components (1952), Rodabaugh and George's work on pressure in bends (1957), and standard beam theory. Help › Sources in the app lists each equation with its reference. Some values are tabulated in the standard, such as allowable stresses. In Datum Pipe these are inputs you enter. They are pre-filled with typical values worked out from published minimum material strengths and are marked "check against your code edition". ASME, B31.1 and B31.3 are trademarks of the American Society of Mechanical Engineers. Product and file-format names are trademarks of their owners and are used only to describe file compatibility.

Architecture › Release flow. release.yml (windows-latest): checks a pushed tag matches the version, takes the notes from CHANGELOG, runs the engine tests, builds the NSIS installer, writes SHA256SUMS.txt and publishes the GitHub Release. Run it from the Actions tab (tag pushes are blocked from Claude sessions).

heading: Datum Pipe: project memory › 1. Architecture › How we work
text: Datum Pipe: project memory › 1. Architecture › How we work. 1. The user reviews a release and sends screenshots. 2. Reproduce first. 3. Big asks get a plan file and questions; build after the answers. 4. Engine first (with a test), then the UI. 5. Check every change in the real app (Xvfb screenshots, tests_ui/realapp.sh). 6. Add a UI test for every bug. 7. Run all checks: clippy -D warnings, cargo test (with the hardening tests and benchmarks), the UI type-check and UI tests, cargo deny check. 8. Release. 9. Report in plain language: what changed, what was checked, what is not done.

heading: Datum Pipe: project memory › 3. Roadmap
text: Datum Pipe: project memory › 3. Roadmap. Held for later: the family plant-design workflow (owner, 2026-11-02: "keep this in memory; put it in the roadmap later; finish piping and vessels first"). Datum Schema (P&IDs, line list, specs, DEXPI) → a separate 3D layout app (working name Datum Layout: routing, equipment, its own library, construction isometrics) → Datum Pipe (stress, stress isometrics) → results back. Datum Pipe does no 3D modelling. Files only, never linked code. What Datum Pipe would need: 1. Source IDs and tags kept on elements, supports and nozzles; a line number per element (now one per model). Small. 2. Plant coordinates: a model origin, East/North/Elevation shown in tables and the iso. Small. 3. Richer .pcf import: line number, spec, schedule, material, insulation, temperatures and pressures, support tags and types from the attributes (today geometry only). Medium. 4. A published open JSON interchange file for the family: several lines per system, three operating conditions and hydrotest, density, equipment nozzles with growth, support types, IDs. Medium. 5. Re-import with merge: new geometry from Layout keeps the stress engineer's supports, springs, cases and settings; shows what changed upstream. Large, the most important. 6. Systems of several lines joined at shared points. Medium. 7. Results out (CSV/Excel and the interchange file): support loads and movements by tag, spring data, nozzle loads by equipment nozzle, support changes, stress status

heading: Datum Pipe: project memory › 3. Roadmap
text: Datum Pipe: project memory › 3. Roadmap. - Hydraulics: pressure drop (Darcy–Weisbach, Colebrook), pumps and their curves, pipe networks; line sizing (velocity and pressure-drop limits). - Relief valve sizing (gas, steam, liquid: nozzle-flow physics); control valve sizing (Cv/Kv, choked flow). - Storage tanks: shell courses by the one-foot method, wind girders, tank wind and seismic. - Heat exchanger tubesheets; fitness for service of corroded vessels (only if free public methods exist). - Vessel nozzle local stresses by our own shell finite element model (Datum Mesh's solver), instead of the copyrighted bulletins. - Water hammer and surge (after dynamics); thermowells; orifice plates. - Dynamics, later: missing-mass correction for the spectrum, a frequency sweep and imposed motion for harmonic loads, time history (relief valve opening, water hammer forces), separate spectra per direction, rotary inertia. - Not planned: thermal design of heat exchangers (proprietary correlations); plant 3D layout (we exchange .pcf files instead).

heading: Datum Pipe: project memory › 5. Known limits (0.2.0)
text: Datum Pipe: project memory › 5. Known limits (0.2.0). - One-way supports are rests only (+Y); a guide or restraint with a gap acts both ways. - Friction is the same in every direction across a support (no separate coefficients), and is path-independent: each case slides from the installed position. - Each case finds its own support states; there is no option to use the operating states for the sustained case. - No pressure thrust on straight pipe from bends (only bellows). Wind has no shielding and acts on a bend's chord; seismic is one static vector (both directions as an option, no per-axis cases); occasional loads go with operating case 1 only. - The deformed shape moves arcs' vertices by the chord-interpolated displacement (fine to 45° per arc segment; bends are split in two). - Bends' pressure opening (Bourdon effect of curved pipe) is not modelled; pressure elongation is for straight pipe only and off by default. - Minimum wall: t ≥ D/6 fails rather than using a thick-wall equation; bends are checked at the intrados only. - Two rigid supports holding the same direction at one node share the reaction equally (the true split is indeterminate). - Spring hangers are sized from operating case 1 only, hold vertically only, and use one spring each (no double springs or load-to-travel charts).

heading: Datum Pipe: project memory › 5. Known limits (0.2.0)
text: Datum Pipe: project memory › 5. Known limits (0.2.0). - The .pcf import reads geometry, sizes, in-line items and supports; schedules, materials, temperatures and pressures in the file are not read (set them in Datum Pipe). - Pump nozzle checks are component and resultant checks against the entered table values; the pump standard's combined interaction equations are not applied. - Relief valve thrust is for an ideal gas at an open discharge only (no liquids, two-phase flow or closed discharge systems), acts with operating case 1 only, and is static (times the load factor; no time history). - The .pcf export writes geometry, bores, weights and supports only; expansion joints come back as rigid parts and springs or restraints as rests on import. - Expansion joints: one bellows per element, no hinged or gimbal joints, no movement or cycle check against the maker's limits.

heading: Datum Pipe: project memory › 5. Known limits (0.2.0)
text: Datum Pipe: project memory › 5. Known limits (0.2.0). - Vessels: external pressure by classical buckling with a single design factor (no plasticity interaction beyond the yield cap); cones under external pressure treated as cylinders of their large diameter; wind and seismic are static, not combined, and the larger is used; no wind-induced vibration; skirt-to-head weld and openings in the skirt not checked; saddles: two equal saddles, no wear plates, stiffening rings not themselves checked, compression checked against S (no buckling allowable); nozzle reinforcement without inward projection, same material for neck, pad and shell, nozzles not counted in the weights; heads formed from one plate (no crown/knuckle thickness split); weights from the inside surface times the thickness. - Nozzle flexibility is the user's stiffness values only; vessel local stresses are not calculated. - Response spectrum: no missing-mass (rigid) correction, components combined separately (signs lost), one spectrum for all directions with factors. - European vessel rules: torispherical and ellipsoidal heads by the default rules; no European nozzle (pressure-area), external pressure, flange or saddle rules yet. - Buried pipe: soil springs at segment ends (finer segments for accuracy), elastic–perfectly plastic, path-independent per case; Rankine lateral (no depth factor), no soil overburden on the pipe, no code rules for restrained buried pipe; spectrum and harmonic reactions leave the soil out.

heading: Datum Pipe: project memory › 5. Known limits (0.2.0)
text: Datum Pipe: project memory › 5. Known limits (0.2.0). - Harmonic response: one force and moment at one node at one frequency (no sweep, no imposed displacement), equal damping in every mode; its amplitudes are not stress-checked and nozzle allowables are not applied to them. - Natural modes: lumped translational masses (no rotary inertia), supports linear and touching, no friction; rests and guides do not hold the pipe's rotation about its axis, so long lines can show slow rocking modes. - The equilibrium check cannot find stiffness, SIF or axis mistakes (each element is self-equilibrated); the benchmarks and worked cases test those.

heading: Datum Pipe 0.1: plan
text: Datum Pipe 0.1: plan. Written before building, from the brief (Edgar-Mendonca/Datum › briefs/DATUM-PIPE.md, hub session 16). Every decision there is made; this file says how 0.1 is built and in what order.

heading: Datum Pipe 0.1: plan › Feedback
text: Datum Pipe 0.1: plan › Feedback. The user is a piping and rotating-equipment engineer who has used the commercial pipe stress tools for years and finds them expensive and hard to use. Datum Pipe is the modern, clear, free alternative, built the Datum way from scratch: an element table that draws in 3D as you type, linear supports, the process piping code's equations, support and nozzle loads, an automatic isometric and a stress report, all verified against hand calculations.

heading: Datum Pipe 0.1: plan › Diagnosis: what 0.1 must get right
text: Datum Pipe 0.1: plan › Diagnosis: what 0.1 must get right. 1. Trust. Pipe stress results go into support and nozzle designs. Every element and solver path needs a test against a known answer, an equilibrium check after every solve, and Help › Verification generated from the same tests. 2. The way engineers think. The element table (From, To, DX, DY, DZ, pipe, material, conditions, component) is the model; the 3D view, the isometric and the report follow from it. 3. Units everywhere. SI and US, switchable at any time, every value with its unit. The engine owns the units (Calc's table); the file keeps SI. 4. Public words. Equations of the process piping code (ASME B31.3) only; allowables are user inputs; never name or compare with commercial software.

heading: Datum Pipe 0.1: plan › Proposal: how it is built
text: Datum Pipe 0.1: plan › Proposal: how it is built. - Model (crates/core/src/model.rs): elements reference pipes, materials and line conditions by id; bends and tees sit at an element's To node; supports, nozzles and loads at node numbers. Node positions are laid out from the deltas (the first node of each connected piece keeps its coordinates); a loop that does not close is refused. - Edits (doc.rs): Plan's ops on a copy, kept only when the model lays out and passes check; whole-model undo. - Solver (elements.rs, solve.rs, from Mesh's frame solver): every element's stiffness from its exact flexibility (∫ Bᵀ C B ds along the centreline, so straight pipe, bends with their flexibility factor, reducers and rigid parts share one path; Timoshenko shear included), sparse assembly and faer's Cholesky (Mesh's sparse.rs), supports as stiff springs along their directions (rigid = 1e12 N/m), imposed displacements through the same springs, one factorisation for all load cases, and the equilibrium check (forces and moments) for every case. - Load cases (cases.rs): basic solutions (W, T+D for each case, hydrotest weight) combined linearly: OPE = W + T + D, SUS = W (with pressure for the stresses), EXP = OPE − SUS.

heading: Datum Pipe 0.1: plan › Proposal: how it is built
text: Datum Pipe 0.1: plan › Proposal: how it is built. - Code (code.rs): hoop stress and minimum wall, sustained longitudinal stress with 0.75i, displacement stress range with the in-plane and out-of-plane SIFs, the allowable range with f from the cycles (basic or liberal). Each function cites its equation. - Isometric (iso.rs): a 30° projection with dimension placement and sheet splitting; the window draws it as SVG. - Window: copied from Mesh (Plan's skeleton): ribbon, File page, Options, print, updater; the element table at the bottom, the 3D view (three.js) in the centre, the Inspector on the right, Results, Isometric and Report views.

heading: tagline
text: tagline. Pipe stress analysis on the desktop: displacements, support loads, nozzle loads and code stresses, with an automatic isometric.

heading: about
text: about. Datum Pipe works out how a piping system moves and what it pushes on when it heats up, carries its weight, holds its pressure and meets wind or an earthquake. You type the piping as a table of elements, the way a stress engineer marks up an isometric (or import a piping component file from a design tool), and it appears in 3D as you type: pipes at their true diameter, bends, tees, reducers, valves, flanges and supports. Put on the supports (one-way rests, gaps, friction and spring hangers it sizes for you), the temperatures, pressures and equipment movements; the load cases are built for you. Analyze solves every case with Datum Pipe's own 3D pipe element solver, checks the stresses using the published equations of the process piping code (ASME B31.3), the power piping code (ASME B31.1) or the European piping standard (EN 13480-3), and shows the results on the model, in tables of displacements, support loads and nozzle loads, on an automatic isometric drawing and in a printed stress report. Allowable stresses are your inputs, Help › Verification solves benchmark problems with known answers in front of you, and Help › Sources says where every equation is published.

heading: steps
text: steps. Type each element's From node, To node and lengths in the table, or import a piping component file; pick the pipe, material, line conditions and component (bend, tee, reducer, valve, flange). Type values with their units if you like (20 ft, 150 mm). It draws in 3D at once, and analyses as you go. Support and load it Add anchors, rests (one-way, with gaps and friction), guides, line stops, spring hangers and nozzle points; set up to three operating temperatures and pressures, the hydrotest, equipment movements, wind and static seismic. Analyze, see the stress ratios on the model, read the support and nozzle loads, and print the stress report with the isometric and the equilibrium checks.

heading: Changelog › 0.7.5 — 2026-11-04
text: Changelog › 0.7.5 — 2026-11-04. The electrical load list and data completeness. Lists › Loads. Every piece of equipment that draws electrical power (pumps, compressors, fans, motors, agitators, electric heaters, air coolers) with its driver, rated power, absorbed power, voltage, operation and load, and a total row: - The rated power is the driver's rating, else the equipment's power; the absorbed power is its power, else 80 % of the rating. - The load is the absorbed power for continuous operation, half of it for intermittent and none for standby (set the spare of a pair to Standby); equipment driven by a steam turbine or an engine draws none. - Edit the driver, powers, operation and voltage in the list, in the Inspector (new Electrical section: Operation, Voltage) or in Excel (Read back…). It prints and exports like every list. Lists › Completeness. For each class with objects: how much of the data its own section asks for is filled in (for line numbers, their size, fluid, sequence and class), how many objects are complete, and the fields most often empty. This completes the 0.7 series: insulation and heat tracing, fixes for the checks, every list read back from Excel, loops in one step, the safety analysis, and the load list.

heading: Changelog › 0.7.4 — 2026-11-04
text: Changelog › 0.7.4 — 2026-11-04. What each piece of equipment needs. A table by class says which protections each kind of equipment needs: a pressure vessel high and low pressure, high and low level, and relief; a tank high and low level; a pump low and high pressure; a compressor high and low pressure, high temperature and relief; an exchanger high pressure and relief; a fired heater high temperature, flame failure and relief. A class without a row takes its parent's (a separator takes the vessel's). Options › Safety analysis edits the table. What provides it. A protection counts when, on the equipment or a line on its nozzles, there is: - an instrument whose letters name it: a switch (PSH), an alarm (PAH), a trip (PSHH) or an interlock (PZHH); - an instrument of that variable whose setpoints name it (LIC-101 with "LAH 80 %, LAL 20 %"); - for relief, a safety valve, rupture disc or breather, or a relief path said in the equipment's data. Lists › Safety tabulates every requirement of every piece of equipment with what provides it: Provided, Missing or Not needed. It prints and exports like every list. Check 27 notes the equipment with something missing. Where a protection is not needed, say so in the equipment's *Safety, not needed* field (such as PSL, TSH).

heading: Changelog › 0.7.3 — 2026-11-04
text: Changelog › 0.7.3 — 2026-11-04. Control loops in one step, and valve positions drawn. Instruments › Loops. Select a process line and choose Flow Loop, Pressure Loop or Temperature Loop, or select a vessel and choose Level Loop. The whole loop is placed with one loop number: - Flow: an orifice plate in the line and its flow transmitter beside it. - Pressure, temperature: the transmitter tapped onto the line. - Level: the transmitter on a free nozzle of the vessel. - The controller in the control system, above the transmitter, joined by a signal line. - The control valve in the line (for level, in the vessel's outlet line), with its signal from the controller. The arrow on each button places the measurement and controller only. The transmitter reads its line's conditions for its datasheet, and the loop checks find the loop complete. Then give the valve its fail position and its station (the fixes in the Checks panel offer both). Valve positions drawn. A manual valve's Normal position now shows on the sheet, in print and in DXF: normally closed (NC) and locked closed (LC) valves are drawn filled, and locked valves are labelled LO or LC beneath.

heading: Changelog › 0.7.2 — 2026-11-04
text: Changelog › 0.7.2 — 2026-11-04. Every list read back from Excel. Edit in Excel, read back. Every list and report exported to Excel can now be edited there and read back with Read back… on the same list: the line list, equipment list, instrument index, valve list, stream list, take-off, cable schedule, I/O lists, tag register, datasheet index and your own reports. - A preview first: each changed cell is listed with what the project has now; untick what you do not want. Nothing changes until you read it back, and Undo takes it all back. - Only what the list lets you edit is read: values the drawing works out (velocity, From/To, a sheet number) are left alone. Tags can be changed too. - Units: numbers are in the column's unit as exported (the header says it), or in the unit typed with them (12 bar, 150 psi). A value that is not a number is listed with why. - Rows keep their objects through a last, hidden column in the workbook; a row whose object is gone is listed, and rows added or deleted in the workbook make or delete nothing.

heading: Changelog › 0.7.1 — 2026-11-04
text: Changelog › 0.7.1 — 2026-11-04. Fixes for the checks, and problems marked on the sheet. Fix ▾ on every problem. In the Checks panel each row has a Fix button. It lists the fixes for that problem; the one you choose is made as one edit that Undo takes back: - Duplicate tags: the others take their next free tags. - An open end: closed at a battery limit. - A size or pipe class change with no reducer or spec break: both sides take one side's value. - Flow arrows against the rest of the line: that piece turned round. - A pump with no check valve: one put in its discharge, the right way round. - A vessel with no relief path: its standard arrangement placed (relief valve, vent, gauge, level loop, drain), or its relief said to be elsewhere. - A control valve with no isolation: its station placed (block valves, drain, bypass). - No fail position: FC, FO or FL. - A pipe class that is not a spec: one of the project's specs chosen, or a new class added from the starter. - A line too fast: one common size up. - Insulation and tracing (check 26): insulate it, give the thickness, or say N (none).

heading: Changelog › 0.7.1 — 2026-11-04
