heading: Changelog › 0.7.0 — 2026-11-04
text: Changelog › 0.7.0 — 2026-11-04. Insulation and heat tracing. On every line. A line's insulation is now a type from a list (H heat conservation, C cold, PP personnel protection, A acoustic, F fire protection, N none) with its thickness and material, and its heat tracing a kind (steam, electric, hot water, hot oil, jacketed) with the temperature it holds. - In the line number: two new tokens for Options › Line numbers, (the code and thickness, such as H50) and (ST, ET…), for example - - - - . - Passed along: the valves and fittings in a line take its insulation, as they take its size and pipe class; a valve given its own is listed in To do. - Drawn: a traced line has its tracer beside it, a thin dashed line. - Listed: the line list has Insulation, Insulation thickness and Tracing columns (edit them there); the valve list has Insulation. Check 26. A traced line that is not insulated (a warning); an insulation with no thickness; a line at 60 °C or more, or 0 °C or less, that does not say its insulation (N for none). The exchanger example's steam line is insulated (H, 50 mm). The Excel reader is updated to its latest version (a fix in a part Datum Schema does not use).

heading: Changelog › 0.6.5 — 2026-11-02
text: Changelog › 0.6.5 — 2026-11-02. The tag register. Every tag, drawn or not yet. Lists › Tag Register lists every tagged item in the project (equipment, instruments, valves and the rest) with its class, service, sheets, area and status: *Drawn*, *Not drawn*, or, once the project keeps a register, *Drawn, not in the register*. It prints and exports to Excel and CSV like every list, and can be the source of your own reports. Tags before drawings. *Add tags…* takes tags typed or pasted straight from a spreadsheet (tag, class, service; a header row with a Tag column is understood), or read from an Excel or CSV file. A preview says what happens to each before anything changes: added, already in the project (marked as registered), or left out and why. The class is guessed from the tag's letters when it is left out (P-101 a centrifugal pump, V-101 a vessel, FT-101 a field instrument, FV-101 a control valve, PSV-101 a safety valve), or given by a class or symbol name. Drawn later as the same object. Click a tag that is not drawn in the register, then click on the sheet: it becomes a symbol of that object, with its tag and data, exactly as from the Plant panel.

heading: Changelog › 0.6.4 — 2026-11-02
text: Changelog › 0.6.4 — 2026-11-02. One set of process values per case. Every stream, line and piece of equipment keeps its process values for each case: Normal, Maximum and Minimum to start with, and any you add (start-up, turndown, winter…). The values kept per case are flows, pressures, temperatures, densities, viscosities, vapour fraction, enthalpy flow, heads, power and duty, a control valve's design drop and a relief valve's rate and temperature. Check › Process Case chooses the active case, and everything follows it: the hydraulics and their checks, the sizing of control valves, orifices and relief valves (which now names its case), the lists, the stream table and the balances. A case used for the first time starts as a copy of the one before, so you type or import only what differs. A simulator import fills the active case: switch case and import each run. Datasheets show the other cases' values beside the active one where they differ ("Flow (Maximum)"), so one datasheet carries normal, maximum and minimum conditions. Options › Process cases names, adds and removes cases. Switching case is one entry in the history and one Undo.

heading: Changelog › 0.6.3 — 2026-11-02
text: Changelog › 0.6.3 — 2026-11-02. The PFD and the P&ID kept in step. Linked both ways. A P&ID line developed from a stream, or a stream made from a line, stays linked to it. After every change their service, phase, mass and volume flow, operating pressure and temperature and density are compared, and each remembers what they last agreed on, so the To do tab says which side changed: - The stream changed (a new simulator run imported, say): *Take the stream's value* puts it on the P&ID line. - The line changed on the P&ID: *Take the line's value to the stream* puts it on the PFD. - Both changed differently: both buttons are offered. - Equipment on one side only: a piece of equipment on the PFD but on no P&ID (or on a P&ID but on no PFD) is listed, with *Develop again* or *Make the PFD again*. Each item has *Go to*; taking a value is one edit that Undo takes back.

heading: Changelog › 0.6.2 — 2026-11-02
text: Changelog › 0.6.2 — 2026-11-02. A PFD from the P&IDs. Sheets › PFD from P&IDs. For a plant drawn as P&IDs first, one command makes its process flow diagram: - The main equipment, as the same objects (tags and data shared, never copied), laid out from the P&IDs at half scale, side by side. - One stream for each process path between two pieces of equipment or a battery limit, found by following the piping through valves, fittings, tees and off-page connectors in the drawn flow direction. Instruments, vents, drains, relief valves and bypasses are left out. - Each stream takes its line's conditions: service, flows (mass flow from volume flow and density where needed), operating pressure and temperature, density. The stream table is on the sheet and the heat and mass balance checks run on it. - Linked both ways: every line on a path knows its stream, as a developed P&ID does, so the line-versus-stream check compares them. Making it again adds only the paths not yet linked; one Undo takes it back. Developing a P&ID from a PFD and making a PFD from that P&ID gives the same streams between the same equipment.

heading: Changelog › 0.6.1 — 2026-11-02
text: Changelog › 0.6.1 — 2026-11-02. Develop a P&ID from the process flow diagram. Sheets › Develop P&ID. On a PFD sheet, one command makes a first P&ID on a new A1 sheet (PFD-300 becomes PID-300): - The same equipment: each pump, exchanger, heater and vessel is the same object on both sheets, so its tag and data are never copied and cannot drift apart. The layout follows the PFD, spread out to make room. - Streams become line numbers: each stream's number, name, phase, mass and volume flow, operating pressure and temperature and density go onto its line. A size is suggested from the flow and the project's velocity limits for the stream's phase (the smallest common size that keeps within them), with a fluid code from the phase and the project's first pipe class. - The standard arrangements are placed round the equipment: the pump's strainer, check valve, isolation valves and gauge; the exchanger's isolation valves and temperature transmitter; the vessel's relief valve, level loop, vent and drain. - Checked: the line-versus-stream check compares every line with its stream, and the To do tab lists what to look at.

heading: Changelog › 0.6.1 — 2026-11-02
text: Changelog › 0.6.1 — 2026-11-02. Developing again adds only what is new: equipment already on a P&ID and streams already made into lines are left alone. One Undo takes the whole development back. The result is a draft for the engineer to tidy and complete; check the suggested sizes as with every size. Also: arrangements fit more vessel shapes (a separator's boot and side nozzles), and a relief, vent or drain line on a free nozzle takes the fluid, pipe class and schedule of the equipment's other lines.

heading: Changelog › 0.6.0 — 2026-11-02
text: Changelog › 0.6.0 — 2026-11-02. Apply Arrangement. Select a piece of equipment (or several, or a control valve) and choose Format › Apply Arrangement. The valves, fittings and instruments your company puts round that kind of equipment are placed in one step: - Centrifugal pump: suction strainer and isolation valve, discharge check valve and isolation valve, pressure gauge, drain. - Vessel: relief valve, vent, pressure gauge, level transmitter with its controller, drain. - Shell-and-tube exchanger: isolation valves, temperature transmitter, drain. - Control valve station: block valves on both sides, a drain, and a bypass with a globe valve. - Compressor: discharge check valve, relief valve, pressure and temperature transmitters. Valves and fittings go into the line on each nozzle in order from the nozzle outward and take the line's size and pipe class; branches are tapped onto it. Instruments take the equipment's number where it is free (PI-101 on P-101), and a controller its transmitter's loop number. Applying twice adds nothing, and Undo takes the whole arrangement back. The result is a draft to tidy; the checks and To do say what still needs a value.

heading: Changelog › 0.6.0 — 2026-11-02
text: Changelog › 0.6.0 — 2026-11-02. Your own arrangements. Options › Arrangements edits them: the class each is for (its subclasses too), and each part's nozzle (alternatives separated by ; , so one arrangement fits several vessel shapes), how it goes on (in the line, tapped on, a controller beside it, a bypass round it), its symbol and its tag letters. The starter set comes with every project. Public text. Documents and help describe Datum Schema's own goals; a trademark notice is in the README and NOTICE; an automatic check keeps product names out of the window's text.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.4 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.4 — 2026-11-01. Reports you design yourself. New report. Lists › New Report, or Save as report… on any list in the bottom panel, opens the report designer: - From: any list (line list, stream list, equipment list, instrument index, valve list, take-off, I/O summary, cable schedule, I/O allocation, datasheet index…) or every object of a class with all its attributes (every pump, every control valve, every vessel, with the subclasses). - Columns: tick the ones you want and put them in order. - Filters: keep only the rows where a column is, is not, contains, does not contain, is empty, is not empty, is at least or at most a value (numbers in the column's unit; "is" takes several values separated by commas). - Group and sort: group by a column, each group opening with a heading that counts its rows and adds up its numeric columns; sort by another, smallest or largest first. - A live preview shows the rows as they will be. Saved in the project. A report is a tab of the bottom panel, always in step with the drawing: click a row to find it, edit its cells like any list's, export it to Excel (group headings in bold) or CSV, print it from File › Print. Edit report… changes it; Delete report removes it.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.3 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.3 — 2026-11-01. Equipment datasheets and stream results from a simulator. Equipment datasheets. Pumps, compressors, vessels, exchangers and every other piece of equipment now have a datasheet, opened from the Inspector, the Plant panel or the datasheet index like an instrument's. - Nozzles: each process nozzle with its line and the line's flow, pressure and temperature, from the drawing, so the datasheet and the P&ID never disagree. - Operating and design: a pump's or compressor's differential pressure and head from its suction and discharge lines, with its own flow, head, power, design and operating conditions. - New attributes in their own sections: a pump's NPSH available and required, efficiency, speed, standard, impeller, seal and driver; a compressor's stages, speed, standard and driver; a vessel's orientation, diameter, length, heads, thicknesses, corrosion allowance, design code, joint efficiency and weights; an exchanger's shell side and tube side (fluid, flow, temperatures, pressures, allowed pressure drop, fouling) and construction (TEMA type, shells, passes, tubes). Manufacturer and model for all equipment. - They are issued, revised (Δ), printed, exported to Excel and imported from Excel like instrument datasheets. A valve's Sizing data now show on its datasheet too.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.3 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.3 — 2026-11-01. Stream results from a simulator. In the Streams tab, Import results… reads a simulator's stream table saved as Excel or CSV into the PFD's streams: mass flow, actual volume flow, temperature, pressure, vapour fraction, density, enthalpy flow, phase and the mass fraction of each of the project's components. Streams are found by number or name in the header row (streams as columns) or the first column (one row per stream); units come from the label or a units column; absolute pressures are kept as gauge. A preview shows every value with what the stream has now, and what cannot be read and why (standard volume flows, mole fractions, unknown components); the import is one edit that Undo takes back. A new quantity, mass (kg or lb), for weights.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.2 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.2 — 2026-11-01. Sizing of control valves, orifice plates and relief valves. Sizing in the Inspector. Select a control valve, an orifice plate or a relief valve: the Inspector's new Sizing group sizes it from its own data and its lines, and sizes it again after every change. - A control valve's required Cv and Kv (IEC 60534-2-1, also ISA-75.01.01): liquid, with choked flow when a vapour pressure is given; gas, with the expansion factor and choked flow. The drop is the one typed (Sizing › Pressure drop at design flow) or the difference between its lines' operating pressures. With a rated Cv, it shows how much of it is used. - An orifice plate's beta ratio and bore (ISO 5167-2, Reader-Harris/Gallagher, corner taps), from its line's flow, density, viscosity and inside diameter at the differential pressure typed. - A relief valve's required area and its API 526 orifice letter (API 520 Part I): gas or vapour at critical flow, or liquid.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.2 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.2 — 2026-11-01. What it needs and what it assumed. A missing value is named (a flow on its line, a set pressure, a molar mass); a value assumed (FL 0.90, xT 0.70, k 1.3, 25 kPa across an orifice) is listed under the result. Write to the datasheet puts the result in the object's data, so it shows on its datasheet and in the lists. New Sizing data on control valves, relief devices and flow elements hold the inputs. The examples' level and relief valves size out of the box. A sizing aid, checked by the engineer.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.1 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.1 — 2026-11-01. Calculation sheets in Datum Calc. Calculations. Select a pump, compressor, exchanger, vessel, tank or line: the Inspector's new Calculations group offers the Datum Calc sheets that fit it (pump power and motor size, NPSH available, compressor power and discharge temperature, exchanger duty and area, vessel shell thickness, tank volume and filling time, line pressure drop, pipe wall thickness). Each is saved as a Datum Calc file with the object's data filled in: from the object (flow, head, power, design pressure, area), from the lines on its nozzles (density, operating pressure and temperature, mass flow), from its size and schedule (inside and outside diameter, nominal wall), from its pipe spec (corrosion allowance) and from its service limits (velocity). Each filled value says where it came from; the rest keep the sheet's typical values, listed at the top of the sheet to check. No meaningless sheets. A sheet that cannot be worked without some data (a line's flow, a pump's head, a design pressure) says what to fill in instead of mixing a sample value with yours. Every sheet the examples can make opens and computes in Datum Calc without errors.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.0 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.0 — 2026-11-01. The instrument wiring database. Junction boxes, cables and I/O cards are now objects of the project with their own data: a junction box's terminals, type and location; a cable's type, pairs, from, to, length and route; an I/O card's kind (AI, AO, DI, DO, fieldbus), channels, control system, rack and slot. Add them from Lists › Wiring (Junction boxes, Cable schedule, I/O allocation), edit them in the lists, and find them in the Plant panel. Devices name them. Each field instrument and control valve names its junction box and terminals (1, 2 or 1-4), its cable, and its I/O channel as card/channel (AI-01/3), in the Inspector's Wiring group or the loop diagram's wiring table. Cable schedule and I/O allocation. The cable schedule lists every cable with its devices and the pairs used (from and to filled in from its devices when left blank); the I/O allocation lists every channel of every card with its device, or spare, and marks channels used twice. Junction boxes list their terminals used. All print and export to Excel and CSV.

heading: Changelog › 0.5.0 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.5.0 — 2026-11-01. Check 25 finds wiring that does not add up: a junction box, cable or card that is not in the project, two devices on one channel, a channel beyond its card, a device on a card of the wrong kind (a valve on an AI card), and cables or boxes with more devices than pairs or terminals. Until a project has junction boxes, cables or cards, wiring typed as free text is left alone. Loop diagrams show the cable's type and pairs and the card's kind and control system.

heading: Changelog › 0.4.4 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.4.4 — 2026-11-01. Company rules, tag formats, and speed on large projects. Company rules. File › Options › Company rules: your own checks, on every object of a kind and its sub-kinds (a rule on Equipment covers pumps, vessels and exchangers). An attribute must be there, or its value must equal, not equal, be one of, contain, be at least or at most a value (in the project's units); choose the level and, if you like, the words. Check 24 runs them on every change. Tag formats. File › Options › Tags: the separator (P-101, P101, P_101…), a unit or area code put before the number (P-10101), numbering per sheet (101, 201…) or through the project (001, 002…), and the digits. New tags and loop numbers follow it, copies keep the width (V-007 → V-008), and Check › Renumber applies it to every tag. Speed. On a 120-sheet project (2,640 symbols, 2,760 lines) the open sheet now refreshes after an edit in about 40 ms instead of 1.9 s: objects are found by binary search, and the loop wiring check and the To do list look only at loops with wiring and datasheets that were issued. An edit takes about 25 ms, the lists under 80 ms, saving 0.1 s and opening 0.03 s.

heading: Changelog › 0.4.3 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.4.3 — 2026-11-01. Assemblies and data labels. Assemblies. Select a group on the drawing (a control valve station with its block valves and bypass, a pump set) and Format › Save as Assembly: its symbols, lines, notes and their data are kept by name. Place it again from the palette's new Assemblies tab: click it, then click the sheet (Shift keeps placing). Its symbols get the next free tags (kept where they are free, as in another project); lines to things left out become open ends. File › Options › Assemblies renames, deletes, shares them as a file and uses them for new projects. Data labels. File › Options › Data labels chooses the data shown on the drawing under every symbol of a kind and its sub-kinds: a pump's flow and head, a vessel's volume, a control valve's Cv, in the project's units.

heading: Changelog › 0.4.2 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.4.2 — 2026-11-01. Implied items: flanges, gaskets and bolts in the take-off. Implied items. Each pipe class now says what every end of a component brings with it: by default, at each flanged end, a weld-neck flange, a gasket and a bolt set, each with its description, commodity code and size range. The valve and fitting take-off adds them by size and class after the components (fourteen 3" gaskets for seven flanged 3" valves), saying which components imply them. Ends. Each component of a class has its end type (flanged, butt weld, socket weld, threaded or none); left blank, it is read from the description (“flanged RF” is flanged, “socket weld” socket weld). Edit both in File › Options › Pipe specs; a CSV table may have an Ends column.

heading: Changelog › 0.4.1 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.4.1 — 2026-11-01. Values passed along a line, and the To do list. Values passed along. A valve's or fitting's size and pipe class now follow the line it sits in: change the line and its components change with it. Control and relief valves, reducers, vents and drains are sized on their own. A value typed on the component is kept; the component follows its line again once it matches. The pipe class goes into a new field, *Pipe class (from its line)*: a valve's own *Class or rating* stays its rating (300#). The valve list shows both, as Pipe class and Rating. To do. A new tab under the drawing lists what to look at after a change: a component whose own size or pipe class differs from its line's (take the line's value with one click), a datasheet changed since it was issued (open it), a sheet changed since its last issued revision (compare it).

heading: Changelog › 0.4.0 — 2026-11-01
text: Changelog › 0.4.0 — 2026-11-01. Pipe specs: the first of the piping rules. Pipe specs. File › Options › Pipe specs holds the project's pipe classes (A1A, B2A…): each with its description, rating, material, sizes, schedule, design pressure and temperature limits and corrosion allowance, and the valves and fittings it allows, by size, each with a description and commodity code. Start from a typical carbon steel class (ASME B16.5 class 150, ½"–24", the usual valves and fittings), add an empty one, read your specs from a CSV table (Class, Component, From, To, Description, Code), or load a spec file; save a copy to use them in another project. Three new checks, only when the project has specs: 21 a line's pipe class is not one of the specs; 22 a valve or fitting its line's class does not allow at that size (vents, drains and sample points by their own size); 23 a line outside its class's sizes, design pressure or design temperature. Take-off from the spec. The valve and fitting take-off names each component from its class: its description and commodity code, ready for a requisition. Pipe class field. A line's Pipe class in the Inspector offers the project's classes. The Pump transfer example now carries its A1A spec.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.4 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.3.4 — 2026-10-31. The user guide. User guide. Help › User Guide (or File › User guide, or Tell Me) opens the guide: getting started, then every feature in chapters (drawing the plant; data and objects; checks and hydraulics with every check rule; lists and reports; instruments; process flow diagrams; symbols, standards and title blocks; revisions and review; working with other programs; examples), the keyboard shortcuts and the glossary. Search it, jump to a chapter from the contents, or Print / Save as PDF on A4. It is written from the same help as the ? buttons, so the two always agree, and any tool without a chapter of its own is still listed. Getting started now names all the lists, the I/O summary, the take-off and the stream list.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.3 — 2026-10-31
text: Changelog › 0.3.3 — 2026-10-31. Comments on the drawing. Select what a comment is about (or nothing), then Check › Comment and click the sheet where it applies. A numbered pin marks it; the Comments tab under the drawing lists them, open ones first, with replies: Reply, Resolve or Reopen, Edit, delete, or click one to go to it and select what it is about. Comments are signed with your name from File › Options and dated. The status bar counts the open ones. Several reviewers. Send each reviewer a copy of the project file. When it comes back, Check › Import Review… takes in their new comments, replies and resolutions without doubles (every comment and reply has its own id; the newest resolution wins), and Undo takes the import back. Print and export. File › Print can include the review comments as a list; the Comments list exports to Excel or CSV. Pins are never printed on the sheets, so a review does not end up on an issued drawing.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.2 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.3.2 — 2026-10-30. Your company's title block. Company title block. File › Options › Title block › *Use a company title block on every sheet* starts from a copy of the standard block; change, add or remove cells, with the block drawn as you edit. The block can be any size up to 400 × 150 mm. Each cell has a caption and shows a field (company, project, client, unit, sheet title, drawing number, revision, scale, sheet n of m, date, drawn, checked, approved), fixed text, a field of your own, or the company logo (the one chosen under Datasheets). The revision table above the block follows its width, and the drawing area keeps clear of it. Fields of your own (a contract number, a document code) are filled in for each project in the Inspector, with nothing selected, under Title block. Share it. *Save a copy* writes the block as a file; *Load a title block* reads one into another project; *Use for new projects* starts every new project with it. It prints, exports to DXF (without the logo) and is kept in the project file.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.1 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.3.1 — 2026-10-30. The valve and fitting take-off. Take-off. Lists › Take-off (and its tab under the drawing) counts every valve, control valve, fitting and in-line element on the P&IDs by type, size, pipe class and rating, with their tags and sheets: the quantities for a material requisition. The size is the item's own, else that of the lines it sits in (a component between two sizes shows both, such as 3" × 2"); the pipe class comes from its line, the rating from the item. Each object counts once, even when drawn on two sheets; process flow diagrams are left out. Print it, or export it to Excel or CSV; click a row to select its items. Tell Me now finds the take-off, the I/O summary and the stream list.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.0 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.3.0 — 2026-10-30. Stream compositions with a component balance, the I/O summary, and three instrument checks. Stream compositions. File › Options › Stream components lists the components of the project's streams, one per line. Every stream then has a mass fraction for each (Inspector › Composition; blank is none of it), the stream table on the PFD shows a row per component, and the Streams list a column. Component balance. Check 17: each component balances round every item on a PFD (within 0.5% of the mass in), and each stream's fractions add up to 1 (within 1%). Reactors are left out of the component balance, since they change their components. The Crude preheat example now carries compositions that close by hand. I/O summary. Lists › I/O Summary (and its tab under the drawing) counts the inputs and outputs each control system takes: analogue inputs (transmitters), analogue outputs (control valves), discrete inputs (switches), discrete outputs (solenoids) and fieldbus devices, with the total and the total with 20% spare per kind. An instrument's control system comes from its Wiring; its kind from its I/O channel ("AI 01-03"), else its signal, else its letters and symbol. Print it, or export it to Excel or CSV; click a row to select its instruments.

heading: Changelog › 0.3.0 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.3.0 — 2026-10-30. Instrument checks. Check 18: a transmitter's or gauge's range (typed as "0–10 bar", "-50 to 150 °C", "0-60 m3/h", or a bare range in the project's units) covers the operating pressure, temperature or flow of the line it measures. Check 19: every control valve has a fail position (FO, FC or FL). Check 20: once a loop's wiring is started, every device in it has its junction box, terminals, cable, control system and I/O channel (the control-system functions need only their system).

heading: Changelog › 0.2.0 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.2.0 — 2026-10-30. A client's own symbols, old drawings to trace over, links to Datum Pipe and Datum Sim, process flow diagrams with heat and mass balances, and revision clouds. A client's symbol library. File › Libraries › Import a legend (DXF) reads a client's legend sheet (save it as DXF from your CAD program first). Every block placed on the legend becomes a symbol, described by the text beside it. Datum Schema suggests what each one stands for (a gate valve, a centrifugal pump…) from its description and block name, and puts its connection points where lines meet the drawing. Check the suggestions in the review table, edit the connection points by clicking on the drawing, and save the library: it stays on this computer for every project, and Save a copy / Add a library file share it with colleagues. The palette's Library tab places its symbols one by one.

heading: Changelog › 0.2.0 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.2.0 — 2026-10-30. Drawing standard. File › Options › Drawing standard draws a whole project with a library's symbols. The objects do not change: the same class, tag, data, checks and lists; lines stay on their nozzles (followed by name). Switching back to Datum Schema's symbols restores the drawing exactly. A project keeps its own copies of the library symbols it uses, so it opens on any computer, and DXF export keeps the client's block names. An old drawing behind a sheet. Sheets › Old Drawing shows a DXF faintly behind the sheet, to redraw an old P&ID as a live one. A drawing larger than the sheet is scaled to fit and centred; set its size and position in the Inspector. It is never picked by mistake, and is printed and exported (on its own BACKGROUND layer in DXF) only when you ask.

heading: Changelog › 0.2.0 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.2.0 — 2026-10-30. To Datum Pipe. Select a process line, then Format › Send › To Datum Pipe: the line becomes a Datum Pipe model to start its stress analysis, with its size, schedule, design pressure and temperature, density and length, and its valves at their places along the run between two anchors. A P&ID has no routing in three dimensions, so the line goes as a straight run; add the bends and supports in Datum Pipe. What was assumed (a missing schedule, length or condition) is listed. To Datum Sim. Lists › Loop Diagrams › To Datum Sim saves a control loop as a Datum Sim model to tune: set point, PID controller, valve, process and transmitter, with a trend of SP, PV and OP. The dynamics are typical values for the measured variable (flow, level, pressure, temperature), kept as variables at the top of the model to set from the plant; level loops are integrating, with an outflow.

heading: Changelog › 0.2.0 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.2.0 — 2026-10-30. Process flow diagrams. Sheets › PFD Sheet (or tick *Process flow diagram* for a sheet in the Inspector). On a PFD, process lines are streams, numbered 1, 2, 3… in diamonds, each with mass and volume flow, temperature, pressure, vapour fraction, density and enthalpy flow. A stream table is drawn along the bottom of the sheet in the project's units, and the Streams tab lists them (edit, Excel, CSV, print). Equipment on a PFD can be the same objects as on the P&IDs. Heat and mass balances. Three new checks: 14 the mass flows into each item on a PFD equal those out (within 0.5%); 15 the enthalpy flows out less those in equal the item's duty or shaft power, or nothing (within 2%); 16 a P&ID line that names a PFD stream (Inspector › PFD stream) carries the stream's mass flow. The P&ID checks (sizes, check valves, relief, isolation) leave PFD sheets alone. The balances check the numbers typed; they are not a simulation.

heading: Changelog › 0.2.0 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.2.0 — 2026-10-30. Revisions, comparison and clouds. Inspector › Revisions › Issue… puts a row in the revision table and keeps the sheet as issued in the project file. Compare with A… lists what was added, removed or changed since (moved, rerouted, a new tag or data); click a change to go to it. Revision clouds draw a cloud round each changed area with the next revision in a triangle, printed and on the REVISION layer in DXF. Example. File › Examples › Crude preheat (PFD): feed pump, exchanger, fired heater and separator with eight streams whose heat and mass balances close by hand.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.12 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.1.12 — 2026-10-30. Tell Me shows the drawing behind it, DEXPI import, a check valve's direction, bend points kept, the logo in Excel. Tell Me (Ctrl+K). The command search now opens over the window, dimmed behind it, instead of hiding everything else. DEXPI import. File › New › From a DEXPI file opens a P&ID saved in the DEXPI exchange format (XML) as a new project: equipment, valves and instruments with their tags, positions, turns and data (converted to SI from the file's units), each line number with its pieces, valves in their lines and connections to nozzles, and the signal and impulse lines. Files from Datum Schema come back exactly as they were exported; files from other programs are read as far as their content allows, with classes Datum Schema does not know drawn with a stand-in symbol and listed, and drawings larger than the sheet scaled to fit. The DEXPI export now also keeps each symbol's turn and mirror, the exact symbol and the line types, and writes attribute values at full precision. Check valves the right way round. Check 8 now looks at which way a check valve on a pump's discharge is fitted: one that would stop the flow is reported. Right-click any in-line symbol › Turn round swaps its inlet and outlet, keeping its lines where they are.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.12 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.1.12 — 2026-10-30. Bend points kept. Dropping a valve onto a line keeps the bend points you placed: those before the valve stay on the first piece, those after it go to the second. Deleting the valve joins the pieces with all their bend points. Logo in Excel. Datasheets exported to Excel carry your company logo (PNG or JPEG) on every sheet.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.11 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.1.11 — 2026-10-30. Drawing fixes, the cause-and-effect matrix, the DEXPI exchange format, and loop diagrams in DXF. Drawing lines. The line you are drawing is now shown under the mouse all the way: press on a port and drag, or click a port and move. A click on a port starts a line that follows the mouse, snaps to the port under it (ringed), and ends at the next click: on a port, on a line (a branch) or anywhere (an open end). Escape or a right-click drops it. (Before, the line only appeared once it was finished. The box you drag to select several things is shown again too.) Adding a symbol by name. A double-click on the sheet (or Add Symbol) opens a small search box beside the point instead of a window over the drawing, so you can see where the symbol will go. Type a name or instrument letters, choose with the arrow keys, Enter places it; Escape or a click elsewhere closes it.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.11 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.1.11 — 2026-10-30. Cause and effect. Lists › Cause & Effect reads the interlocks on the P&ID into a matrix: causes down (the switches and transmitters that trip, with their trip settings), effects across (the valves and drives they act on, and what each does: a valve goes to its fail position, a drive stops), and in each cell the interlock that links them. A switch wired straight to a valve counts too. Click a tag to find it; print the matrix on A3 or export it to Excel. The Compressor package example now has a trip to show it: high-high drum level or high-high gas temperature stops the motor and opens the recycle valve. DEXPI export. Sheets › DEXPI saves the sheet in the DEXPI P&ID exchange format (Proteus XML): equipment with its nozzles, each line number with its segments, centre lines, valves and connections, the instrument functions with their letters and loop numbers, the signal and impulse lines, and the attributes (DEXPI names in SI units). It is a first mapping, checked for well-formed XML and consistent references, not yet with other programs. Loop diagrams in DXF. The loop diagram window has a DXF button: the frame, the drawing and the texts on their own layers.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.10 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.1.10 — 2026-10-30. Datasheets from Excel, your company's datasheet form, and loop diagrams. Import datasheets from Excel. Lists › Import Excel reads a workbook (.xlsx) and matches it to this project's datasheets by tag. It reads a table (a Tag column and one column per value, such as "Manufacturer" or "Set pressure (psig)") or one worksheet per datasheet, as Datum Schema exports them. Columns match by label, ignoring case and a unit in brackets; numbers are converted from the unit given (psi, °F, m³/h…) or from the project's units; choices match however their dashes were typed. A preview comes first: what will change, what is already the same, and what is not imported. Values that come from the line, the vessel or the drawing are never imported; where the file disagrees, the preview says so and where to change them. Blank cells change nothing. Untick what you do not want; the import is one step that Undo takes back. Tags with no datasheet and columns that match nothing are listed.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.10 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.1.10 — 2026-10-30. Your company's datasheet form. File › Options › Datasheets sets the form number, your logo (PNG, JPEG or SVG, up to 200 KB), a footer line, which rows the datasheet shows and the order of its sections. Hidden rows keep their data, are still imported and are still part of each issued revision. Use this layout for new projects makes it the default, for the examples too. The form number and footer go on screen, in print and in Excel; the logo on screen and in print.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.10 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.1.10 — 2026-10-30. Loop diagrams. Lists › Loop Diagrams draws every instrument loop (LT-101, LIC-101 and LV-101 make loop L-101) on an A3 sheet with the title block. Each field device is drawn with its own symbol, with its function, where it is mounted, its range or fail position, and its signal. It is wired through its junction box terminals and cable to its I/O channel in the control system, and on to the controller. Type the junction box, terminals, cable, control system and I/O channel for each device in the loop's Wiring table or in the Inspector; what is still missing is listed and noted on the drawing. Primary elements such as orifice plates are shown beside their transmitter; relief valves are not part of loops. Print one loop from its Print button, or all of them from File › Print. The Inspector has Loop diagram… for any instrument.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.9 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.1.9 — 2026-10-30. Datasheet revisions: issue, track what changed, issue again. Issue a datasheet. Issue… on a datasheet gives it a revision and a status: Preliminary, Issued for Enquiry, Issued for Purchase or As-built. Revisions run A, B, C… before purchase and 0, 1, 2… from purchase on, suggested for you; type your own if your company numbers differently. Each issue records the date, who issued it (File › Options › Your name) and a note, and it appears in the object's history. See what changed since. The issue keeps what the datasheet said. From then on every value that changes, whether typed on the datasheet or changed on its line or vessel, is marked Δ; hover it to see what it was at the last revision. The marks clear at the next issue. Revision block. Every datasheet shows, prints and exports its revisions, newest first. Printed datasheets carry the revision in the header and the title block; the Excel workbook has the revision on each sheet, a Δ column with the old values, and the revision state in its index.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.9 — 2026-10-30
text: Changelog › 0.1.9 — 2026-10-30. Datasheet index. A new list (Lists › Datasheets) shows every datasheet with its revision, status, date, who issued it and how many values changed since. Click a row to open the datasheet. Issue the … shown issues every datasheet in the filtered list at once, each with its own next revision. Like every list, it sorts, filters, groups, prints and exports to Excel and CSV. File format. Projects saved by 0.1.9 keep the issued revisions in the file, so 0.1.8 and earlier cannot open them; they ask you to update. Files from earlier versions open as before.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.8 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.1.8 — 2026-10-29. Instrument datasheets, made from the drawing. A datasheet for every instrument. Every instrument, primary element, control valve and relief device has a datasheet: General (tag, type, measured variable, loop, P&ID, area, line), Process conditions, the instrument's or valve's own data (range, signal, fail position, set pressure…), and a new Specification section (manufacturer, model, process connection, wetted and body materials, electrical connection, hazardous area, IP rating, power supply, accuracy; for control valves the required and rated Cv, characteristic, leakage class, actuator, positioner and trim; for relief devices the orifice area and relieving case). Attributes your company adds in Options › Classes get a section of their own. Process conditions from the P&ID. The datasheet takes the fluid, flow, density, viscosity, operating and design pressure and temperature, size, schedule and pipe class from the line the instrument measures or sits in, from a primary element it is tapped to, or from the vessel it is mounted on. A controller takes its transmitter's. These values show where they come from and change where they live, so the datasheet and the P&ID never disagree.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.8 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.1.8 — 2026-10-29. Open, type, print, export. Open a datasheet from the Inspector (Datasheet…) or the Plant panel. Type the instrument's own values on it; every change is in the object's history. Print one datasheet from its Print button, or all of them from File › Print on A4 pages with the title block. Excel › Datasheets exports every datasheet, one worksheet each, with an index.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.7 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.1.7 — 2026-10-29. The Plant panel: every object in its place in the plant, drawn or not. Plant panel. Beside the symbol palette, the Plant tab shows the plant hierarchy (plant › unit › area) with every object in the project: equipment, valves, instruments and line numbers. Click an object to go to its symbol. Add plants, units and areas, rename them (double-click) and remove empty ones. Drag an object onto another area to move it; the Inspector shows and changes an object's area too. Draw an object anywhere. Drag an object from the Plant panel onto a sheet to draw it there: the same object, with one tag and one set of data, can be drawn on several sheets. Delete: the object or only its drawing? Deleting the last symbol of an object asks whether to delete the object with its data or only remove it from the sheet. Objects kept this way stay in the Plant panel, marked "not drawn", ready to be drawn again. Lists. Every list has an Area column, so lists can be grouped by area.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.6 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.1.6 — 2026-10-29. Classes: every kind of object is defined by data, and you can add your own attributes. The class library. Every object belongs to a class (centrifugal pump, gate valve, control valve, instrument function, line number…), named after the open P&ID data standard (DEXPI) where a matching class is known. Classes inherit from the classes above them: a centrifugal pump has a pump's attributes (flow, head, power) and an equipment item's (service, design and operating conditions, material). The Inspector shows the class of the selected object and its attributes. Your own attributes. File › Options › Classes lists every class and its attributes. Add your company's attributes to any class (text, a choice list, or a value with units); they reach every class under it and are saved with the project. Mark one required and check 6 lists the objects where it is still empty.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.5 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.1.5 — 2026-10-29. The first step to an object-based plant engineering tool: plant objects, a database file and a history. Plant objects. Every equipment item, valve and instrument is now an object with its own tag and data; the symbol on the sheet is a view of it. A line number is an object too, owning every drawn piece of that line: a line continued through a valve, or carried to another sheet by a pair of off-page connectors, keeps its line number, and data typed on any piece belongs to the whole line. Where a line's number changes (after a reducer), New line number from here gives a piece a number of its own. Plant hierarchy. Every object sits in a plant › unit › area tree (Plant 1 › Unit 100 › Area 1 to start with), ready for the Plant panel in a coming release. The project file is a database. Projects save as one SQLite database: objects, attribute values, the hierarchy, sheets, symbols and lines, each in its own table, which any SQLite tool can read. Saving is still atomic. Projects from earlier versions open and convert.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.5 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.1.5 — 2026-10-29. History. Every change to an object is recorded with who made it, when, and the old and new value, and saved with the project. The Inspector shows the history of the selected object. Your name for the history is in Options (the computer's user name otherwise).

heading: Changelog › 0.1.4 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.1.4 — 2026-10-29. The exhibition build. Checked end to end. Before this release every example was opened, checked for errors, printed and exported to DXF in the window, and the DXF files were read back by an independent reader with no errors. README. A two-minute demo of Find the faults, the line list and its hydraulics, printing and DXF, and the screenshots.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.3 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.1.3 — 2026-10-29. Fixes from an independent review of the engine, and polish. - A valve with three or more lines on it no longer splits one line number into two (it reported a duplicate line number). - Copying and pasting a pipeline keeps one new line number across its valves. - The pump check valve and control valve isolation checks follow a line across sheets through its off-page connectors. - Deleting a valve in a small loop works again, and joining the two halves keeps data only the second half had. - A project that has used up its ids says so instead of losing what was added. - CSV quotes text with a carriage return; Excel cells no longer show a stray apostrophe. - DXF: symbol letters (M, S, RO…) stay upright like in the window; characters a DXF cannot hold are written as ?; the hydraulic badges are written OK, ! and X. Lists. Printed lists have a title block on every page. Window. An instrument's loop number shows from its tag; more checks of the window run before every release (keyboard editing, units, Tell Me).

heading: Changelog › 0.1.2 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.1.2 — 2026-10-29. Fast with big drawings; hydraulic badges in colour. Speed. Lines route much faster: a sheet with 500 symbols and 500 lines is drawn again in well under a tenth of a second after each change (it took seconds on a crowded sheet). Badges in colour. The hydraulic badge on each line is green ✓ within its limits, amber ! close to them, red ✗ well outside. Line numbers. Selecting a line highlights its line number through every drawn piece, and it stays highlighted on the other sheets. Line list. The flow and the hydraulic results come right after From and To.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.1 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.1.1 — 2026-10-29. The drawing now checks itself, lists itself and sizes its lines; the examples, printing and DXF. Examples. File › Examples: a pump transfer (tank, duty and standby pumps with strainers and check valves, a level-controlled vessel with its safety valve), a compressor package with its anti-surge loop, a steam heater with its temperature loop and condensate return, and Find the faults, the pump transfer with planted mistakes. Each example opens with no errors. Checks. Thirteen rules run on every change and fill the Checks panel: duplicate tags and line numbers, open ends, off-page connectors without a partner, size changes without a reducer, class changes without a spec break, missing tags or line data, flow arrows against each other, pumps without a check valve, vessels without relief, control valves without isolation, controllers without a measurement or a final element, instrument letters that do not fit, and lines outside their hydraulic limits. Click an issue to go to it; the status bar counts errors and warnings. Rules can be switched off in Options.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.1 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.1.1 — 2026-10-29. Line hydraulics. Every line with a flow, a density and a viscosity gets its inside diameter (from its size and schedule), velocity, Reynolds number, friction factor (Colebrook) and pressure drop per 100 m and over its length, with a ✓, ! or ✗ badge against the limits for its service (pump suction and discharge are recognised). The limits are editable in Options. Results are a sizing aid, checked by the engineer. Lists. The line list, equipment list, instrument index and valve list are always generated from the drawing. Sort, filter and group them, click a row to find it, edit a cell and the drawing follows; export to Excel or CSV. Sheets and connectors. Off-page connectors pair across sheets and show where the line continues; double-click one to jump to its partner. A legend sheet shows every symbol and line type the project uses. Notes, leader notes and Hold clouds. Print and export. Print to PDF: the sheets at their size or fitted to A3, the lists on A3 with page numbers, and the legend. Save a sheet as SVG. DXF (R12) with a layer per line type and symbol category, symbols as blocks with their tag as an attribute, the border and title block included.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.0 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.1.0 — 2026-10-29. The first release: the window, the sheet, symbols and lines, and the updater. The window. The family window in magenta: the ribbon (Home, Draw, Symbols, Lines, Instruments, Check, Lists, Sheets, View, Help and the Format tab for a selection), the File page, Options, the symbol palette on the left, the sheet in the middle, the Inspector on the right, and a panel below for the checks and the lists. Light, dark and automatic themes. Sheets. A blank A3 sheet with its border, grid zones (A–H across, 1–8 down), title block and revision table. Sheets can be A3, A1, ANSI B or ANSI D; add sheets and a legend sheet from the tabs under the drawing. With nothing selected, the Inspector edits the sheet, its revisions and the title block.

heading: Changelog › 0.1.0 — 2026-10-29
text: Changelog › 0.1.0 — 2026-10-29. Symbols and lines. About 80 symbols of our own: vessels, pumps and compressors, exchangers, manual, control and relief valves, fittings, instrument bubbles, flowmeters, line marks and off-page connectors. Drag one from the palette or double-click the sheet and type its name; it gets the next free tag. Drag from a port to another to draw a line; lines route themselves at right angles around symbols, carry a flow arrow on every segment and hop over each other. A valve dropped on a line goes into it, and both halves keep the line's data. Files. Projects save as .dschema files and open again, with recovery of unsaved work. Every save is written safely. Updates. Datum Schema checks for new versions when it starts and installs them from File › Updates, after checking the download against its checksum.

heading: Datum Schema: notes for Claude
text: Datum Schema: notes for Claude. Read docs/MEMORY.md first. It is the project's memory: architecture, decisions, roadmap, and a log of every session. The family design guide is FAMILY.md in Edgar-Mendonca/Datum (read-only from here; docs/FAMILY.md links to it). The brief this app started from is briefs/DATUM-SCHEMA.md in the same hub repo. At the end of every session that changes anything, update docs/MEMORY.md: - tick the roadmap - add a session-log entry - record any new decisions - refresh the architecture section if files moved - Rust and Tauri 2, small and efficient code, Windows first. The same look, ribbon, help, printing and updater as every Datum app (FAMILY §2–9); copy from Datum Plan (shell), Datum Sim (block canvas, wire routing), Datum Calc (units) and Datum Pipe (pipe sizes) rather than reinventing. Every copy becomes Schema's own code: never link another app. - Ship in small numbered releases (0.1.0, 0.1.1, …). Every release appears in the in-app updater. - Engine logic belongs in crates/core (pure Rust, unit-tested), not in the UI. The window never calculates: connectivity, checks, lists, hydraulics, routing, the sheet frame and DXF are the engine's. - The UI is SolidJS + Vite in ui/src/*.tsx (built to ui/dist). State lives in ui/src/store.ts.

heading: Datum Schema: notes for Claude
text: Datum Schema: notes for Claude. - The engine and the .dschema file use SI base units (m, kg, s, Pa, K). The engine sends display units (SI and US) from its unit table (crates/core/src/units.rs, copied from Datum Calc by way of Datum Pipe); ui/src/units.ts only applies them. - Symbols are our own vector drawings following the conventions of ISO 10628-2 (equipment, valves, lines) and ISA-5.1 (instruments). Never copy a symbol library from other software. - Public words (README, CHANGELOG, site.json, help, commits): never name, compare with, or say the app copies or replaces any commercial drawing, CAD or plant-design product (FAMILY §13). Standards may be named by number; file formats (DXF, CSV, Excel) may be named. - The repo is public, so CLAUDE.md, docs/MEMORY.md and docs/PLAN-*.md are public text too: describe this app's own goals; comparisons with other products stay in chat. Code comments never compare with a product ("…-style", "as … does"). File-format names only where they name a file the app reads or writes. The no_product_names tests (engine and UI) enforce it. - Hydraulic results are a sizing aid checked by the engineer; say so in the README and help. - Licences: MIT/BSD/Apache/MPL only. Record every dependency in NOTICE. Quality bar (brief §4):

heading: Datum Schema: notes for Claude
text: Datum Schema: notes for Claude. - Every check has a passing and a failing test; tags, split and merge, off-page walking, hydraulics against a hand calculation and Datum Calc's pipe pack, DXF parsed back; every example opens with 0 errors and "Find the faults" has exactly its planted faults. - Hardening (FAMILY §11): random projects never panic, damaged files open as far as possible, hostile text is shown as text. - Never cut the connectivity, the checks, the lists, the hydraulics, printing or DXF. Checks before pushing: - cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings - cargo test --workspace (includes the hardening tests) - npm run check:ui, then npm run test:ui (dumps the engine fixture, builds the window, runs the Playwright checks; set NODE_PATH=$(npm root -g) if Playwright is installed globally) - cargo deny check (licences, advisories, sources; CI runs it) Releasing: 1. Bump the version in src-tauri/Cargo.toml and crates/core/Cargo.toml. 2. Add a CHANGELOG section (## x.y.z — date). 3. Keep docs/site.json true with each release (about, steps, highlights, roadmap). 4. Run release.yml from the Actions tab (workflow_dispatch; tag pushes are blocked from Claude sessions) or push the tag vX.Y.Z. The workflow creates the tag and publishes DatumSchema-x.y.z-setup.exe and SHA256SUMS.txt.

heading: Contributing › How the code is laid out
text: Contributing › How the code is laid out. - crates/core: the engine in pure Rust: the project model and its edits, the symbol library, connectivity, tags, checks, line hydraulics, the lists, the sheet frame, routing and the DXF writer. All calculation lives here, with tests. - src-tauri: the desktop shell (commands, files, options, recovery, the updater). - ui/src: the window (SolidJS + TypeScript). It draws what the engine computes and sends edits back as operations. - docs/MEMORY.md: architecture, decisions, roadmap and a log of every session. Read it first.

heading: Contributing › Before you send a change
text: Contributing › Before you send a change. Keep code compact and in the style around it. A new check or calculation comes with a test (one passing and one failing case for a check, a hand-worked answer for a calculation); a new window feature with a UI test where it can. Symbols are our own drawings: never copy a symbol library. Never link GPL, LGPL or AGPL code into the app. By contributing you agree your work is released under the MIT licence.

Intelligent P&IDs and process flow diagrams: draw, check and list. Draw the plant with real symbols, and every symbol and line carries its data and knows what it is connected to. So Datum Schema writes the line list, equipment list, instrument index and valve list for you, always in step with the drawing; checks the drawing as you work; and sizes every line, with its velocity and pressure drop against limits. It is for process, chemical, mechanical, piping and instrument engineers, operators and students. It is free and open source (MIT), Windows first, installs in seconds and updates itself. More on the family site: edgar-mendonca.github.io/Datum/apps/schema. Hydraulic results are a sizing aid. Velocities and pressure drops help you size lines; they are checked by the engineer before they are used. The same goes for the heat and mass balance checks (they check the numbers typed, they are not a simulation) and for the models sent to Datum Pipe and Datum Sim (starting points with stated assumptions), and for the sizing of control valves, orifice plates and relief valves.

heading: What it does
text: What it does. - Real symbols: about 80 of our own drawings following ISO 10628-2 (equipment, valves, lines) and ISA-5.1 (instrument bubbles and letters), with their connection points. - Lines that know their ends: drawn port to port, routed at right angles around symbols, with flow arrows and hops; a valve dropped on a line goes into it; off-page connectors carry a line to another sheet. - Data on everything: tags, services, design and operating conditions, sizes, line numbers built from size, fluid, sequence and class, in SI or US units. - Sheets: A3, A1, ANSI B and ANSI D with border, grid zones, title block and revision table; a legend sheet; your company's own title block (cells, fields, logo), shared as a file. - Fixes for the checks: most problems come with fixes made in one click (a missing check valve put in, an open end closed, a duplicate tag renumbered, sizes and classes aligned, insulation set), and problems can be marked on the sheet.

heading: What it does
text: What it does. - Live checks: twenty-seven rules on every change (duplicate tags, open ends, size changes without a reducer, class changes without a spec break, pumps without check valves, vessels without relief, control loops, hydraulic limits, heat, mass and component balances, instrument ranges, fail positions, loop wiring, pipe specs, your company's own rules, instrument wiring and more), each a click away from the problem. - Line hydraulics: inside diameter from size and schedule, velocity, Reynolds number, Colebrook friction factor, pressure drop per 100 m and over the line, with a ✓ ! ✗ badge against the limits for its service. - Plant objects: every equipment item, valve, instrument and line number is an object in a plant › unit › area hierarchy (the Plant panel); symbols are views of it, so one object can be drawn on several sheets. Every change is recorded with who made it and when. - Classes you can extend: a class library (named after the open DEXPI data standard) defines what data each kind of object has; add your company's attributes in Options and mark them required.

heading: What it does
text: What it does. - Datasheets: one per piece of equipment (pumps, compressors, vessels, exchangers: nozzles with their lines' conditions, a pump's differential from its lines, construction, shell and tube side) and per instrument, control valve and relief device, with the process conditions taken from its line or vessel; type on it, issue it with a revision and status, see every value changed since the last issue (Δ), print it, export every datasheet to Excel; a datasheet index tracks them all; import datasheet values from Excel (matched by tag, with a preview first, never overwriting values that come from the P&ID); set your company's datasheet form (form number, logo, rows and section order). - Instrument wiring: junction boxes, cables and I/O cards as objects; a cable schedule and an I/O allocation of every channel; a check that the wiring adds up; loop diagrams with the cable and card details. - Cause and effect: the matrix of the interlocks, read from the P&ID (causes, effects with their actions, the interlock in each cell); print or Excel. - Loop diagrams: every instrument loop drawn from the P&ID on an A3 sheet, with each device wired through its junction box and cable to its I/O channel and controller; type the wiring, print one or all, or save as DXF.

heading: What it does
text: What it does. - Process flow diagrams: PFD sheets whose lines are streams (mass and volume flow, temperature, pressure, vapour fraction, density, enthalpy flow), numbered in diamonds, with their compositions, a stream table on the sheet, a stream list, and heat and mass balance checks round every item; P&ID lines can name the stream they carry and are checked against it. - A client's symbols: read a client's legend sheet (DXF) into a symbol library, with suggested meanings and connection points to review; draw a whole project to that standard and back, with the objects, data and checks unchanged; share libraries as files. - Old drawings: a DXF shown faintly behind a sheet, to redraw an old P&ID as a live one. - Review comments: pinned to the drawing, with replies and resolve or reopen; reviewers work on their own copies and their comments are taken back in without doubles. - Revisions: issue a sheet at a revision, compare it later with what changed, and cloud the changes with the revision triangle. - The Datum family: send a line to Datum Pipe as a stress model, a control loop to Datum Sim as a model to tune, and a pump, compressor, exchanger, vessel, tank or line to Datum Calc as a calculation sheet filled from its data.

heading: What it does
text: What it does. - Simulator results: import a simulator's stream table (Excel or CSV) into the PFD streams, with a preview first. - Sizing: a control valve's Cv (IEC 60534-2-1), an orifice plate's bore (ISO 5167-2) and a relief valve's area and orifice letter (API 520, API 526), from its data and its lines, written to its datasheet. - I/O summary: inputs and outputs per control system (AI, AO, DI, DO, fieldbus) with 20% spare, from the instruments' wiring and signals. - Company rules and tag formats: your own checks on any attribute of any kind of object; tags written your way (separator, unit code, numbering, digits). - Assemblies and data labels: groups saved and placed again with the next free tags; chosen data shown under each kind of symbol. - Values passed along and To do: valves and fittings take their line's size and pipe class; overrides, and datasheets and sheets changed since issue, are listed to look at. - Pipe specs: the project's pipe classes with their limits and the valves and fittings each allows by size, read from a CSV table or started from a typical class; three checks hold the drawing to them. - Valve and fitting take-off: every piping component counted by type, size, pipe class and rating, with its tags, for a material requisition.

heading: What it does
text: What it does. - Tag register: add tags before they are drawn (typed, pasted from a spreadsheet, or read from Excel or CSV) and see every tag's status, drawn or not yet. - Process cases: normal, maximum, minimum and your own; the drawing, hydraulics, sizing, lists and datasheets follow the active case, and datasheets show the others. - PFD and P&ID in step: a change to a stream or its P&ID line shows in To do, with one click to take it across; equipment on one side only is listed. - PFD from the P&IDs: make a process flow diagram from P&IDs drawn first: the main equipment and a stream for each process path, with its line's conditions. - P&ID from the PFD: develop a first P&ID from a process flow diagram in one step: the same equipment, every stream a line number with its data and a suggested size, the standard arrangements placed. - Electrical load list and data completeness: every electrical consumer with its power, voltage, operation and the total; how complete each class's data is. - Safety analysis: the protections each kind of equipment needs (pressure, level and temperature switches and alarms, flame failure, relief), what on the drawing provides each, and what is missing.

heading: What it does
text: What it does. - Insulation and heat tracing: on every line, in the line number if you like, passed to its valves, drawn and listed, with a check. - Loops in one step: a flow, pressure, temperature or level control loop placed whole on a line or vessel, with one loop number; valve positions (NC, LO, LC) drawn. - Standard arrangements: place the valves, instruments, vents and drains your company puts round a pump, vessel, exchanger, control valve or compressor in one step, in the right lines with their sizes and classes; edit them in Options. - Reports you design: start from any list or from every object of a class, choose columns, filters, sort and grouping (with counts and totals), save it in the project, export and print it. - Lists read back from Excel: edit any list or report in Excel and read it back, with a preview of every changed value first. - Lists: line list, stream list, I/O summary, take-off, equipment list, instrument index, valve list and datasheet index, always in step with the drawing; edit them, export to Excel or CSV, print them. - Print and export: PDF (sheets at their size or fitted to A3, lists, legend), SVG, DXF (R12) that opens in any CAD program, and the DEXPI P&ID exchange format (XML), which it also opens.

heading: What it does
text: What it does. - User guide: in the app (Help › User Guide), searchable and printable, with every feature step by step. - Examples: a pump transfer, a compressor package, a steam heater loop, a crude preheat process flow diagram, and "Find the faults". - Safe files: .dschema projects (a single SQLite database with the history), atomic saves, recovery of unsaved work, undo and redo for everything.

heading: What it does › The two-minute demo
text: What it does › The two-minute demo. 1. File › Examples › Find the faults: the Checks panel lists three errors and five warnings, and the status bar counts them. 2. Click "Pump P-101A has no check valve on its discharge": the pump is selected on the drawing. Drag a check valve from the palette onto its discharge line; the issue clears. 3. Click the duplicate tag issue and rename the standby pump P-101B in the Inspector; the issue clears. 4. Open the Line list: every line number with its from and to, flow, velocity and pressure drop. Click a line on the drawing to see its hydraulics and its ✓, ! or ✗ badge. 5. File › Print: the sheet with its title block, then the lists. Sheets › DXF writes the drawing for any CAD program.

heading: Datum Schema: project memory › 1. Architecture
text: Datum Schema: project memory › 1. Architecture. crates/core is the engine (pure Rust, no Tauri): the project and its edits, the symbol library, connectivity, tags, checks, hydraulics, lists, the sheet frame, line routing and the DXF writer. src-tauri is the shell: commands, files, options, recovery and the updater. ui is the window: it draws what the engine returns (view.rs: routed lines with hops, arrows and marks, placed symbols with upright texts, the frame) and sends edits as operations. Coordinates are millimetres on the sheet, y down, so a sheet prints at its true size. Engineering values are SI base units in the file (Pa, K, m³/s, kg/s, kg/m³, Pa·s, m, W); the engine's display table (units::shown) gives SI (bar, °C, m³/h, kg/h, kg/m³, cP, m, m/s, kPa, kPa/100 m, kW) and US (psi, °F, gpm, lb/h, lb/ft³, cP, ft, ft/s, psi, psi/100 ft, hp); the window only applies it.

text: Datum Schema: project memory › 1. Architecture › Release flow. release.yml (windows-latest): checks a pushed tag matches the version, takes the notes from CHANGELOG, runs the engine tests, builds the NSIS installer, writes SHA256SUMS.txt and publishes the GitHub Release. Run it from the Actions tab (tag pushes are blocked from Claude sessions).

heading: Datum Schema: project memory › 1. Architecture › How we work
text: Datum Schema: project memory › 1. Architecture › How we work. 1. The user reviews a release and sends screenshots. 2. Reproduce first. 3. Big asks get a plan file and questions; build after the answers. 4. Engine first (with a test), then the UI. 5. Check every change in the real app (the window against the real engine in Chromium; Xvfb screenshots where the shell matters). 6. Add a UI test for every bug. 7. Run all checks: clippy -D warnings, cargo test (with the hardening tests), the UI type-check and UI tests, cargo deny check. 8. Release. 9. Report in plain language: what changed, what was checked, what is not done.

heading: Datum Schema: project memory › 4. Known limits
text: Datum Schema: project memory › 4. Known limits. - DXF only (other CAD drawings must be saved as DXF first); the reader skips dimensions, images, 3D and patterned hatches (counted in the warnings). Text rotation in old drawings is not kept. - Legend suggestions are by words (description and block name); unusual legends need the review. Connection points are suggested for two-port symbols; equipment needs its points placed. - To Datum Pipe sends a straight run (a P&ID has no 3D routing) and estimated valve masses; To Datum Sim uses typical dynamics. - Compositions are mass fractions only (no molar basis); balances need every stream's mass (and enthalpy) flow; tees between streams are not balanced (draw a mixer or splitter symbol). - Revision comparison is per sheet, by object ids; a symbol deleted and placed again counts as removed and added. - DEXPI import reads one drawing per file and does not pair off-page connectors across files; line pieces are re-routed (centre lines are not kept as bend points). - Lines keep their bend points when symbols move; drag a segment again or Straighten to re-route. - Hydraulics are single-phase Darcy–Weisbach per line number (from its first piece); two-phase lines only get the two-phase velocity limits, not a two-phase pressure drop.

heading: Datum Schema: project memory › 4. Known limits
text: Datum Schema: project memory › 4. Known limits. - DXF text beyond ASCII is written as \U+XXXX escapes (CAD programs decode them; some simple viewers show them literally); the hydraulic badges are written OK, ! and X. - The examples' layouts are hand-placed; lines route themselves, so a moved symbol can make a route less tidy until a segment is dragged. - Printing uses one page size per print job (the largest page); mixed sheet sizes print best one size at a time or fitted to A3.
