heading: Background
text: Background. Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering. Bachelor's thesis: deformation behaviour and impact energy absorption of metal tubes under axial compression. Papers on strain-hardening effects during plastic buckling of axially compressed aluminium tubes, and elementary experimental studies on stress wave propagation in bars (2019, with P. B. Shahapur and T. Y. Reddy). Master's degree in Advanced Engineering Materials. Master's thesis: effect of prior deformation on slip activity in nickel alloys, measuring slip, grain orientation and microstructure with high-resolution digital image correlation (HRDIC) and EBSD maps. Tools used in research: MATLAB, Python (NumPy, SciPy, pandas, Matplotlib), Abaqus CAE, SolidWorks, Fusion 360, Arduino and embedded C, strain gauges, instrumentation amplifiers and oscilloscopes.

heading: Cairn: a browser scheduler
text: Cairn: a browser scheduler. An offline-first, single-project scheduler in React, TypeScript and Vite with a real scheduling engine, not just a Gantt picture: critical path with all four dependency types, leads and lags, task constraints, slack and critical tasks, resources and levelling, baselines, earned value, several views and report definitions. It imports and exports its own JSON, common scheduler XML and XER files, MPX and CSV, and Excel, with browser storage and autosave, and builds to a single page for static hosting. An audit listed what it still needed: dated, auditable progress updates; actual cost history; durable storage; controls-grade revisions; schedule quality checks; evidence attached to progress; round-trip validation of file exchange; collaboration; and security hardening. A count of test cases is not proof that the tests pass. The same needs shaped Datum Plan.

heading: API 617 compressor package delivery
text: API 617 compressor package delivery. Supply and engineering coordination for an electric-motor-driven centrifugal compressor package built to API 617, delivered through an EPC contractor for an oil and gas operator. The work covers technical clarifications, design review, compliance verification against the purchase specification and project standards, progress tracking, sub-vendor management, manufacturing record books and factory acceptance testing.

heading: API 617 compressor package delivery › The equipment in a package
text: API 617 compressor package delivery › The equipment in a package. A typical package breaks down into: the compressor; dry gas seals; the gearbox; bearings; couplings; the seal gas console and booster; the lube oil system and its air cooler; the anti-surge valve; the main motor; the variable frequency drive (VFD) with its transformer and chiller; gas-insulated switchgear and isolators; and the unit control panel. Each item usually comes from a different sub-vendor, so most of the work is making their interfaces meet.

heading: API 617 compressor package delivery › Interfaces between sub-vendors
text: API 617 compressor package delivery › Interfaces between sub-vendors. The driver train (motor, VFD, transformer, switchgear) has to agree with the gearbox ratio, the couplings and the compressor's speed range. Dry gas seals need a seal gas supply and booster sized for start-up, settle-out and pressurised standstill. The lube oil system serves the bearings, gearbox and couplings and needs coolers sized for the site's ambient temperature. The anti-surge valve and its controller have to match the compressor map and the recycle loop. All of it has to fit one baseframe and one control philosophy.

heading: API 617 compressor package delivery › Typical technical questions
text: API 617 compressor package delivery › Typical technical questions. - Lot sampling for valve fugitive-emission tests: how many valves of a lot, of which sizes and stem diameters, have to be tested, and whether one sample can represent a mixed lot. - Noise measured during the mechanical running test above the datasheet guarantee: the test arrangement (for example discharge to atmosphere through a long duct), measurement conditions, weighting and background correction all matter before calling it a nonconformance. - Replacement compressors on an existing baseframe: checking interface dimensions, alignment and foundation loads. - Shipping a complete heavy skid (compressor, gearbox, motor and baseframe): heavy-lift or break-bulk transport. - Control scope: whether load sharing, anti-surge control and choke protection sit in one controller or separate ones, and whether configuring choke alarms and trips falls within a given modification scope. - Material acceptance: when project standards and a manufacturer's derivative of a public material standard both apply, the deviation and the evidence of equivalence must be stated explicitly. - Weld leaks found at hydrotest (for example where a drain pipe joins a cast casing): root cause, corrective action and a qualified repair, before any retest.

heading: API 617 compressor package delivery › Quality submissions for a multi-compressor package
text: API 617 compressor package delivery › Quality submissions for a multi-compressor package. A project quality plan for the whole package; an inspection and test plan per compressor type; a procurement and manufacturing status register; a weld book with WPS, PQR, overlay and consumable procedures; one NDE procedure with an NDE map; one PMI procedure; casing hydrotest procedures; assembled-compressor leak tests after the mechanical running test; and an MRB index per package.

heading: Exhibition and visual design
text: Exhibition and visual design. Exhibition posters for equipment manufacturers at an energy trade show: centred logos, organiser logos, larger product text, a rotor image, the event's dates and stand number, and complete national flags where a flag is used. What matters most is the brand: the correct official logo, its exact typeface and colours, nothing cropped or redrawn. When a correct logo is supplied, replace only the wrong element and keep everything already approved. Partial flags, poor tables, wrong colours and awkward mobile spacing are all noticed and corrected.

heading: Material assessment for compressor service › Two tools, not one
text: Material assessment for compressor service › Two tools, not one. A materials-selection tool ranks candidate materials on property charts (now Datum Atlas). A material-assessment tool answers a different question: is the material chosen for this stage and component suitable for this gas? They share a materials database and plotting, but they are separate jobs.

heading: Material assessment for compressor service › Assessment inputs
text: Material assessment for compressor service › Assessment inputs. H₂S and CO₂ partial pressures; chloride concentration; pH; oxygen; droplet size; wet or dry service; water dew point; each stage's temperature and pressure; and the material of each component (casing, impellers, shaft, dry gas seal parts, console).

heading: Material assessment for compressor service › Outputs
text: Material assessment for compressor service › Outputs. An adjustable saturation and dew-point curve; a wet and dry phase map; sulfide stress cracking (SSC) domain overlays with the stage conditions plotted on them; and risk bars per component.

heading: Material assessment for compressor service › The database
text: Material assessment for compressor service › The database. Carbon steel for low-temperature service (standard and sour-service variants), quenched and tempered alloy steel, 316/316L stainless, precipitation-hardened 17-4PH, duplex and super duplex stainless, nickel alloys 625 and 718, and C-276. Each record holds corrosion limits (H₂S and CO₂ partial pressure, chlorides, pH, SSC domain, sour-service compliance, pitting resistance equivalent number), mechanical and physical properties, fabrication notes and a cost factor. A sour-service flag in a database is never a qualification by itself: it depends on product form, heat treatment, hardness and the actual service conditions.

heading: Material assessment for compressor service › Interfaces tried
text: Material assessment for compressor service › Interfaces tried. A desktop Tkinter version, then a browser version with inputs, graphs, a materials database and an about tab, with tooltips, PNG and SVG export, example cases, a materials editor, local saving and mobile support. The direction after that was a stronger Python version with NumPy, SciPy and Matplotlib, still reachable in a browser.

heading: Material assessment for compressor service › Selection charts
text: Material assessment for compressor service › Selection charts. Selection indices such as E/ρ, σ/ρ, stiffness-limited design and PREN, with clear controls to choose them, consistent colours, families of materials and export. These requirements carried into Datum Atlas.

heading: Manufacturing record books and document assembly › The workflow
text: Manufacturing record books and document assembly › The workflow. A manufacturing record book (MRB) combines certificates, inspection and test records, manuals and supporting documents for one piece of equipment into one coherent PDF. The steps: combine the source PDFs in the right order, keep every page readable, give each section a meaningful title, add a visible table of contents, add PDF bookmarks and clickable links from the contents to each section, keep page numbers and link targets right after inserting pages, and deliver one downloadable file. Never forget the bookmarks. Where source records are in another language, the book can be bilingual.

heading: Manufacturing record books and document assembly › Typical packages
text: Manufacturing record books and document assembly › Typical packages. Dry gas seals; lube oil systems; seal gas consoles and boosters; gearboxes; lube oil air coolers; proximity probes; junction boxes; valves; lifting beams; venturi meters; online cleaning devices; nitrogen-purged enclosures; and instruments such as pressure and temperature transmitters, pressure gauges, resistance and bimetallic thermometers, and thermowells.

heading: Manufacturing record books and document assembly › Large files
text: Manufacturing record books and document assembly › Large files. Books can run to thousands of pages and hundreds of megabytes with over a hundred bookmarks, so they are built with scripts rather than by hand: Python with PyMuPDF to merge files, export and import bookmarks as CSV, generate a contents page and create internal links. Outputs keep the table of contents and linked contents as separate versions.

heading: Manufacturing record books and document assembly › Inspection records
text: Manufacturing record books and document assembly › Inspection records. Inspection stamps and signatures can be extracted and presented from the source records for review. This is document processing only: an inspection record belongs to the item it was issued for and must never be reused or implied for anything else.

heading: Project controls for equipment packages › Weighted progress
text: Project controls for equipment packages › Weighted progress. Progress for an equipment package is the sum of each item's weight times its progress. Items carry weights by value and effort (the compressor, dry gas seals and gearbox weigh most; small electrical items least), and each item moves through phases that carry their own weights: material requisition, request for quotation, technical bid evaluation, purchase order, design, procurement, manufacturing (the largest share), factory acceptance test, packing and delivery. A procurement status register lists each tag with its vendor, equipment, weight and the planned and actual date of every phase, so planned and actual progress can be compared on the same basis. The formula has to agree with how cells store progress (fractions or 0–100) and cover every phase. Status bands such as on track, at risk and delayed are a reporting convention, not a substitute for schedule variance analysis.

heading: Project controls for equipment packages › Project framework
text: Project controls for equipment packages › Project framework. A management framework for a compressor package covers objectives, applicable standards, scope, organisation and RACI, reporting lines, planning, work breakdown structure, master schedule, milestones, progress measurement, risk, reporting and HSE. The organisation typically has a project director and project manager, project control, project engineering with planning and document control, engineering by discipline (process, mechanical, electrical, instrumentation, structural and piping), procurement with expediting and logistics, QA/QC with inspection, welding and testing, manufacturing, and commissioning.

heading: Project controls for equipment packages › Reports and dashboards
text: Project controls for equipment packages › Reports and dashboards. Weekly and monthly reports; engineering, procurement and manufacturing progress; inspection and test reports; engineering document S-curves; planned against actual progress and variance; traffic-light status; supplier scorecards; Kanban views of document status. Templates come with both the underlying registers and the management summary.

heading: Project controls for equipment packages › HSE reporting
text: Project controls for equipment packages › HSE reporting. A safety pyramid from the most serious incidents down to near misses, unsafe acts and unsafe conditions; lost-time and total recordable incident rates against targets; week-, month- and project-to-date figures with man-hours. Note that FAT means factory acceptance test elsewhere in package work, so the two contexts must not be mixed.

heading: Project controls for equipment packages › Risk and audit
text: Project controls for equipment packages › Risk and audit. Risk matrices, categories and heat maps for package components. Internal quality audits covering engineering, procurement, manufacturing, inspection, testing, sub-vendor management and quality records, kept general rather than tied to one corrective action.

heading: Project controls for equipment packages › Scheduling software references
text: Project controls for equipment packages › Scheduling software references. Detailed references to desktop scheduling tools: task information, fields and formulas, graphical indicators, bar styles, timescales, page setup, reports, network diagrams, team planner and resource views; and for enterprise schedulers, activities, layouts, activity codes, schedule options and schedule checks. An open, self-hosted project control application was also documented, with registers, approvals, baselines, multiple schedules, Gantt forecasting, document cycles, progress curves and backups, using inclusive calendar days and finish-to-start critical path, and keeping demonstration data separate from real project records.

heading: Other apps and prototypes › Résumé analysis
text: Other apps and prototypes › Résumé analysis. A Flask app comparing a résumé with a job description: keyword match with TF-IDF and cosine similarity, readability metrics and automatic summarisation. The summarisation module had been removed from the library version in use, which broke the feature: pin versions, or replace removed modules.

heading: Other apps and prototypes › Document management
text: Other apps and prototypes › Document management. A simple document management system on static hosting: upload, metadata editing, a viewer in a new tab, delete and browser storage, with a register of number, type, document number, title, revision, received, review and release dates (dd/mm/yyyy) and reviewer. A browser-only login is not real authentication.

heading: Other apps and prototypes › HR system
text: Other apps and prototypes › HR system. An open-source HR system starting from a login and a simple list, to grow into richer functions and a better interface.

heading: Other apps and prototypes › Thermowell wake frequency
text: Other apps and prototypes › Thermowell wake frequency. A calculator for thermowell wake frequency (vortex shedding against the thermowell's natural frequency), the subject of ASME PTC 19.3 TW.

heading: Other apps and prototypes › Book translation
text: Other apps and prototypes › Book translation. A local Python app to translate a technical book page by page, where waiting longer for good output was fine. It did not work in the end, and translation went back to chapter by chapter.

heading: Finite-element analysis in Python › What was tried
text: Finite-element analysis in Python › What was tried. A Python finite-element workflow: import a STEP geometry, mesh it with Gmsh, and solve a Poisson problem with an open-source solver (SfePy, then FEniCS and FEniCSx), with meshio for mesh conversion and PyVista and VTK for results.

heading: Finite-element analysis in Python › What went wrong
text: Finite-element analysis in Python › What went wrong. Example scripts written for older solver versions failed on API changes (missing integrals and problem-definition functions), editors flagged imports, an optional accelerator library raised warnings, and loading a Gmsh mesh failed with an index error in the element arrays. The move to FEniCSx went through a Conda environment with an MPI build and PyVista.

heading: Finite-element analysis in Python › What helps
text: Finite-element analysis in Python › What helps. A reproducible installation path for Windows, one small example that runs end to end, and explicit handling of geometry, mesh, boundary markers, solver and visualisation. Check the installed library's version before copying any example. The same ideas later shaped Datum Mesh, which proves its own answers against benchmarks.

heading: SHPB data processing: lessons from building the tools › Raw data
text: SHPB data processing: lessons from building the tools › Raw data. The recorded file had a time column and two gauge channels, incident and transmitted. There was no separate reflected channel: the incident gauge records both the incident and the reflected pulse, so the reflected window has to be selected from the incident channel. The processed output has time, incident, reflected and transmitted columns. Selecting a reflected window from the incident channel is not the same as inventing a reflected signal.

heading: SHPB data processing: lessons from building the tools › The workflow
text: SHPB data processing: lessons from building the tools › The workflow. Load the voltage–time data; show the raw incident and transmitted channels; select the incident and reflected windows from the incident channel and the transmitted window from the transmitted channel; crop and review each selection; reverse a pulse's polarity where needed; keep the selection and reversal controls in one figure; save the processed data; smooth with a Savitzky–Golay filter; and compute stress–strain and true stress–strain.

heading: SHPB data processing: lessons from building the tools › Errors met along the way
text: SHPB data processing: lessons from building the tools › Errors met along the way. Unsupported widget arguments in Matplotlib selectors; callback signatures that did not match; positional indexing on sliced pandas Series; a missing reflected column; undefined plot handles; and duplicate selector callbacks overwriting each other.

heading: SHPB data processing: lessons from building the tools › Later ideas
text: SHPB data processing: lessons from building the tools › Later ideas. A browser version with input, cropping, results and formula tabs, an example case, mobile support and clear theory, with Python doing the calculation for accuracy.

heading: SHPB data processing: lessons from building the tools › Ball-on-bar reference values
text: SHPB data processing: lessons from building the tools › Ball-on-bar reference values. A MATLAB tool for ball-on-bar impact used steel defaults: ball and bar radius 0.02 m, density 8000 kg/m³, Young's modulus 200 GPa, Poisson's ratio 0.3, a 145 µs window and a 1 m/s impact velocity. These are tool defaults, not experimental constants.

heading: How the software family came about › The ambition
text: How the software family came about › The ambition. One family of open-source tools for engineers, scientists, researchers and analysts, with one brand, one way of working, a separate repository per app under the MIT licence, and a launcher that installs and updates each app. Most of the apps grew out of real work: scheduling and procurement tracking, material assessment, experimental signal processing, record-book assembly, plotting and engineering calculation.

heading: How the software family came about › Names along the way
text: How the software family came about › Names along the way. The core set settled on Plan, Atlas, Plot and Calc, then grew with Sim, Mesh, Pipe, Schema and Layout. Earlier directions included separate apps for thermowell wake frequency and for SHPB pulse analysis, which were later left out of the core set.

heading: How the software family came about › Launcher and distribution
text: How the software family came about › Launcher and distribution. A desktop launcher showing every app with Install and Update buttons depending on whether it is installed and whether a newer release exists. Technologies weighed along the way: Rust, Python with JavaScript, Electron, Tauri, static web hosting and Next.js; the family settled on Rust with Tauri 2 and SolidJS, with Python bundled where an app needs science libraries.

heading: How the software family came about › Look
text: How the software family came about › Look. Swiss/International Typographic Style, technical-editorial and scientific minimalism: vector logos, one family mark, consistent colours, mobile support for anything in a browser, and a useful home page before the working screens.

heading: How the software family came about › Plot, Plan, Calc and Sim ambitions
text: How the software family came about › Plot, Plan, Calc and Sim ambitions. Plot: multi-axis graphs, linear to logistic and nonlinear fits, ANOVA and t-tests, bar, box, violin, scatter and line plots, multiple sheets, CSV and Excel import, transforms, error bars, smoothing, themes, LaTeX labels and publication exports. Plan: tasks, dependencies, Gantt, WBS, baselines, calendars and resources, dashboards, issues, cost, progress and reports, exchanging files with common schedulers, without forcing every project into one industry's structure. Calc: a library of engineering formula cards. Sim: block diagrams with later physical components, parameter sweeps, sensitivity, linearisation, frequency-response plots, PID tuning and model fitting, with examples such as compressor anti-surge, pump–pipe–tank, DC motor PID, heat exchanger, mass–spring–damper and cruise control.

heading: Technical writing, translation and office deliverables › Languages and formats
text: Technical writing, translation and office deliverables › Languages and formats. Technical documents in English and Chinese, bilingual reports, and translated source records, delivered as Word, PDF, Excel and PowerPoint.

heading: Technical writing, translation and office deliverables › Translating a technical handbook
text: Technical writing, translation and office deliverables › Translating a technical handbook. A long technical handbook translated in sequence, chapter by chapter, then the appendix and index, finishing each chapter in one part where possible and never losing track of where the work had reached.

heading: Technical writing, translation and office deliverables › Quality and correspondence
text: Technical writing, translation and office deliverables › Quality and correspondence. Rewriting quality requirements, minutes of meeting, material acceptance wording, contractual scope questions, issue trackers and pre-contract open-item letters, in professional wording that keeps the technical meaning exact.

heading: Technical writing, translation and office deliverables › Templates and presentations
text: Technical writing, translation and office deliverables › Templates and presentations. Simple Word CV templates with a photo box; progress-meeting presentations corrected for mistakes and poor tables. Deliverables have to be real files with working downloads: saying that a file exists is not enough.

heading: Websites › Personal portfolio
text: Websites › Personal portfolio. Clean and professional, without heavy 3D: the work shown plainly, an engineering project card, optional grid or list views, restrained animation (GSAP), and no flags or "independent consultant" tags.

heading: Websites › An engineering company website
text: Websites › An engineering company website. A bilingual engineering and consulting company site with a hero, about, services, industries served, projects, contact and footer; mobile layout, statistics, dark mode, the company's colours, a simple language switch and a working contact form. No country mentions, cross-border wording or flags. Eight industry cards: oil and gas, industrial manufacturing, energy and utilities, automation and electronics, R&D and start-ups, infrastructure, marine and offshore, and electrical. Trust pages: standards and capabilities, manufacturing and inspection approach, confidentiality, and a typical project workflow. Polish: animation timing, tighter mobile spacing, glass-effect buttons, a scrollbar in the palette, OpenGraph and Twitter metadata, and social icons.

heading: Websites › A community organisation website
text: Websites › A community organisation website. A Tailwind CSS site with responsive three-card grids, property cards, centred service sections, equal image and text treatment and a creator credit linking to the portfolio.

heading: Websites › Questions along the way
text: Websites › Questions along the way. How build tools, front-end frameworks and full-stack frameworks differ; how to choose front end and back end; which plugins are needed; how to optimise and secure a site; how to handle forms; how version control works; whether a free CDN can host a site; and where to get a domain. Code is usually written with AI coding agents, so the architecture has to suit that way of working.

heading: Websites › Build problems met
text: Websites › Build problems met. A missing development script and PostCSS not found on Windows; a Vite plugin import that failed and an install that was read as a Git SSH dependency and failed on authentication. The cure each time was an exact, reproducible build and publish configuration.

heading: How Edgar works › Environment
text: How Edgar works › Environment. Windows, PowerShell, Python virtual environments and pip, VS Code, GitHub repositories and GitHub Pages, and AI coding agents. Installation steps should be explicit and match that setup. Tailwind CSS is a strong preference for websites, with established libraries (DaisyUI, Bootstrap, AOS, Swiper, GSAP) over piles of custom CSS. Science work uses NumPy, SciPy, pandas, Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly and PyMuPDF; browser charts have used Chart.js and ECharts.

heading: How Edgar works › Preferences that depend on the job
text: How Edgar works › Preferences that depend on the job. Browser access and easy sharing matter, and so does real scientific capability; desktop apps, Rust, Tauri and bundled runtimes are welcome when they make an app more capable or easier to install. Separate repositories per app, open-source licences, version control, automatic updates and free hosting are recurring goals.

heading: How Edgar works › Working patterns
text: How Edgar works › Working patterns. 1. Practical outputs: an actual file, app, prompt, tracker or finished visual rather than only a discussion. 2. Iterative correction: screenshots, logos, layouts and wording refined through direct corrections. 3. Technical substance and presentation together: correct calculations and standards, readable charts and tables, consistent branding. 4. Workflow thinking: how a tool is installed, updated, hosted, exported, shared and used in real work. 5. Integration: separate ideas converge into one family or workflow. 6. Scientific strength: a simple demo is not enough where real analysis is expected. 7. Accessibility: browser access, mobile behaviour and downloadable documents. 8. Direct feedback: wrong colours, logos, missing functions and incomplete chapters are named plainly. 9. Continuity: "next", "same" and "continue" refer to the established workflow. 10. Keep what is approved: when one thing is corrected, everything else stays as it was. 11. Context-specific scope: a general reference stays general when asked. 12. Learning through use: practical work comes with the underlying concepts and mathematics.

heading: How Edgar works › How an assistant should help
text: How Edgar works › How an assistant should help. Turn requests into usable deliverables; supply the file format asked for, with a working link; give coding agents concrete prompts with scope and acceptance criteria; preserve existing work; continue long workflows without losing context; and read the actual current file before describing or editing it. In engineering: separate observations, proposed causes, calculated checks and verified results; use the actual standard edition and project documents; never treat a database flag as a sour-service qualification; never invent missing measurements; show units, assumptions and the calculation; and never claim a test passed or a design is safe without evidence. In design: clean interfaces with established libraries, the correct colours and logos, mobile layouts, a useful home page, and project-specific exclusions applied only to their own project. In explanations: the mathematics when asked, explicit setup steps, clear distinctions between build tools, front-end libraries, back-end services, hosting and storage, and no polished descriptions hiding unfinished prototypes.

heading: API 617

Related standards: API 614, API 692, API 671, ASME PTC 10.
